    28	
    29	/-- Relabel a matrix measurement along an equivalence of outcome alphabets. -/
    30	noncomputable def matrixMeasurementTransport
    31	    {alpha beta iota : Type*}
    32	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype beta] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    33	    (e : alpha ≃ beta) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota) :
    34	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement beta iota :=
    35	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
    36	    (fun b => M.effect (e.symm b))
    37	    (fun b => M.pos (e.symm b))
    38	    (by
    39	      calc
    40	        ∑ b, M.effect (e.symm b) = ∑ a, M.effect a :=
    41	          Equiv.sum_comp e.symm M.effect
    42	        _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one)
    43	
    44	@[simp] theorem matrixMeasurementTransport_effect
    45	    {alpha beta iota : Type*}
    46	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype beta] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    47	    (e : alpha ≃ beta) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    48	    (b : beta) :
    49	    (matrixMeasurementTransport e M).effect b = M.effect (e.symm b) :=
    50	  rfl
    51	
    52	/-- Relabeling a projective matrix measurement preserves projectivity. -/
    53	theorem matrixMeasurementTransport_isProjective
    54	    {alpha beta iota : Type*}
    55	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype beta] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    56	    (e : alpha ≃ beta) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    57	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) :
    58	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (matrixMeasurementTransport e M) :=
    59	  fun b => hM (e.symm b)
    60	
    61	/-- Assemble a family of matrix measurements as diagonal blocks indexed by a
    62	finite classical register. -/
    63	noncomputable def blockDiagonalMeasurement
    64	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
    65	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    66	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block]
    67	    (M : block → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota) :
    68	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha (iota × block) :=
    69	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
    70	    (fun a => Matrix.blockDiagonal fun r => (M r).effect a)
    71	    (fun a => Matrix.blockDiagonal_nonneg
    72	      (fun r => (M r).effect a) (fun r => (M r).pos a))
    73	    (by
    74	      ext ⟨i, r⟩ ⟨j, s⟩
    75	      simp only [Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply]
    76	      by_cases hrs : r = s
    77	      · subst s
    78	        simp only [if_pos]
    79	        calc
    80	          ∑ x, (M r).effect x i j = (1 : Matrix iota iota ℂ) i j :=
    81	            by
    82	              simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using
    83	                congrFun (congrFun (M r).sum_eq_one i) j
    84	          _ = (1 : Matrix (iota × block) (iota × block) ℂ)
    85	              (i, r) (j, r) := by
    86	                change (if i = j then 1 else 0) =
    87	                  (if (i, r) = (j, r) then 1 else 0)
    88	                simp
    89	      · simp [hrs])
    90	
    91	@[simp] theorem blockDiagonalMeasurement_effect
    92	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
    93	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    94	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block]
    95	    (M : block → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    96	    (a : alpha) :
    97	    (blockDiagonalMeasurement M).effect a =
    98	      Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a) :=
    99	  rfl

   101	/-- A block-diagonal family of projective measurements is projective. -/
   102	theorem blockDiagonalMeasurement_isProjective
   103	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
   104	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   105	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block]
   106	    (M : block → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
   107	    (hM : ∀ r, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (M r)) :
   108	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (blockDiagonalMeasurement M) := by
   109	  intro a
   110	  constructor
   111	  · change Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a) *
   112	        Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a) =
   113	      Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a)
   114	    rw [← Matrix.blockDiagonal_mul]
   115	    congr 1
   116	    funext r
   117	    exact (hM r a).isIdempotentElem.eq
   118	  · change (Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a))ᴴ =
   119	      Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a)
   120	    rw [Matrix.blockDiagonal_conjTranspose]
   121	    congr 1
   122	    funext r
   123	    exact (hM r a).isSelfAdjoint.star_eq

   125	/-! ## The correlated residue state -/
   126	
   127	/-- The normalized maximally correlated state on the common seed-fiber
   128	residue. -/
   129	noncomputable def seedResidueAncilla (L : LdParams) :
   130	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
   131	      (Fin (L.q / L.m) × Fin (L.q / L.m)) := by
   132	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   133	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   134	  exact eprState (Fin (L.q / L.m))
   135	
   136	/-- The seed-residue ancilla has unit norm. -/
   137	theorem seedResidueAncilla_norm (L : LdParams) :
   138	    ‖seedResidueAncilla L‖ = 1 := by
   139	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   140	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   141	  exact eprState_norm (Fin (L.q / L.m))
   142	
   143	/-- Reindexing Euclidean coordinates along an equivalence preserves norm. -/
   144	theorem reindexState_norm_eq
   145	    {iota kappa : Type*}
   146	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   147	    [Fintype kappa] [DecidableEq kappa]
   148	    (e : iota ≃ kappa) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
   149	    ‖reindexState e psi‖ = ‖psi‖ := by
   150	  rw [← sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)]
   151	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq]
   152	  change (∑ j : kappa, ‖psi (e.symm j)‖ ^ 2) = ∑ i : iota, ‖psi i‖ ^ 2
   153	  exact e.symm.sum_comp (fun i => ‖psi i‖ ^ 2)
   154	
   155	/-- The coordinate tensor of two Euclidean vectors has the product norm. -/
   156	theorem vecTensor_norm_eq
   157	    {iota kappa : Type*}
   158	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   159	    [Fintype kappa] [DecidableEq kappa]
   160	    (u : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ kappa) :
   161	    ‖vecTensor u v‖ = ‖u‖ * ‖v‖ := by
   162	  rw [← sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (mul_nonneg (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _))]
   163	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, mul_pow, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq,
   164	    EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq]
   165	  change (∑ p : iota × kappa, ‖u p.1 * v p.2‖ ^ 2) =
   166	    (∑ i : iota, ‖u i‖ ^ 2) * ∑ j : kappa, ‖v j‖ ^ 2
   167	  simp only [norm_mul, mul_pow]
   168	  rw [← Finset.univ_product_univ, Finset.sum_product, Finset.sum_mul]
   169	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   170	  intro i hi
   171	  rw [Finset.mul_sum]

   173	/-- Tensor the original strategy state with the maximally correlated residue
   174	state and shuffle the factors back into the two local carriers. -/
   175	noncomputable def seedFiberLiftedState
   176	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams) :
   177	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
   178	      ((S.ιA × Fin (L.q / L.m)) × (S.ιB × Fin (L.q / L.m))) :=
   179	  reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor S.ψ (seedResidueAncilla L))
   180	
   181	/-- The correlated seed-fiber lift preserves normalization of the strategy
   182	state. -/
   183	theorem seedFiberLiftedState_norm
   184	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams) :
   185	    ‖seedFiberLiftedState S L‖ = 1 := by
   186	  rw [seedFiberLiftedState, reindexState_norm_eq, vecTensor_norm_eq,
   187	    S.ψ_norm, seedResidueAncilla_norm, one_mul]

   189	/-! ## From the seed-indexed game to the direct game -/
   190	
   191	/-- The seed-indexed question selected in one residue block of a direct
   192	question.  Applying `ldCL` ensures that irrelevant ambient coordinates are
   193	canonicalized exactly as in the source game. -/
   194	noncomputable def seededLdQuestion (L : LdParams)
   195	    (q : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   196	    (residue : Fin (L.q / L.m)) : LdQuestion L :=
   197	  (q.1, ldCL L q.1 (ldSpaceOfDirectResidue L q.2 residue))
   198	
   199	/-- Dilate a strategy for the seed-indexed low-degree game to the directly
   200	indexed game.  The two local carriers receive correlated copies of the seed
   201	residue, and each measurement is block diagonal in that residue. -/
   202	noncomputable def ldStrategyToDirect (L : LdParams)
   203	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L)) : Strategy (directLdGame L.toDirectLdParams) where
   204	  ιA := S.ιA × Fin (L.q / L.m)
   205	  ιB := S.ιB × Fin (L.q / L.m)
   206	  ψ := seedFiberLiftedState S L
   207	  ψ_norm := seedFiberLiftedState_norm S L
   208	  A q := blockDiagonalMeasurement fun residue =>
   209	    matrixMeasurementTransport (ldDirectAnswerEquiv L)
   210	      (S.A (seededLdQuestion L q residue))
   211	  B q := blockDiagonalMeasurement fun residue =>
   212	    matrixMeasurementTransport (ldDirectAnswerEquiv L)
   213	      (S.B (seededLdQuestion L q residue))

   215	/-- Projectivity is preserved by the correlated seed-fiber dilation. -/
   216	theorem ldStrategyToDirect_isProjective (L : LdParams)
   217	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L)) (hS : S.IsProjective) :
   218	    (ldStrategyToDirect L S).IsProjective := by
   219	  constructor
   220	  · intro q
   221	    apply blockDiagonalMeasurement_isProjective
   222	    intro residue
   223	    apply matrixMeasurementTransport_isProjective
   224	    exact hS.1 (seededLdQuestion L q residue)
   225	  · intro q
   226	    apply blockDiagonalMeasurement_isProjective
   227	    intro residue
   228	    apply matrixMeasurementTransport_isProjective
   229	    exact hS.2 (seededLdQuestion L q residue)

   251	/-- A direct question reconstructed in a residue block parses back to its
   252	canonical direct form. -/
   253	theorem parse_seededLdQuestion (L : LdParams)
   254	    (q : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   255	    (residue : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   256	    parseLdQuestion L (seededLdQuestion L q residue) =

   260	/-- Coordinate formula for the correlated residue lift. -/
   261	theorem seedFiberLiftedState_apply
   262	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams)
   263	    (i : S.ιA) (j : S.ιB)
   264	    (r s : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   265	    seedFiberLiftedState S L ((i, r), (j, s)) =
   266	      if r = s then
   267	        S.ψ (i, j) * (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card (Fin (L.q / L.m)) : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹
   268	      else 0 := by
   269	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   270	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos

     4	/-!
     5	# Strategy transport for the directly indexed low-degree game
     6	
     7	This module reads one coordinate of a projective directly indexed strategy as
     8	a two-space mature low individual degree strategy.  The question and answer
     9	transport of `Transport.Questions` supplies the canonical direct question of
    10	every mature line, with the reversed coordinate order and the leading index
    11	of the decoded diagonal direction, together with answer readouts that are
    12	covariant under line rebasing; this establishes all four covariance
    13	conditions of `ProjStrat`.  The module also records exact Born-weight
    14	formulas for both directions of strategy transport.
    15	
    16	## References
    17	
    18	- `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-458`
    19	- `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:49-151`
    20	- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`
    21	-/

    34	/-- Regard a matrix-valued projective measurement as a projective measurement
    35	in the mature LDT interface. -/
    36	noncomputable def matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas
    37	    {alpha iota : Type*} [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    38	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    39	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) :
    40	    MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjMeas alpha iota where
    41	  toMeasurement := {
    42	    toSubMeas := {
    43	      outcome := M.effect
    44	      total := 1
    45	      outcome_pos := M.pos
    46	      sum_eq_total := M.sum_eq_one
    47	      total_le_one := le_rfl
    48	    }
    49	    total_eq_one := rfl
    50	  }
    51	  proj a := (hM a).isIdempotentElem.eq

   113	/-- The coordinate axis-line family is independent of the chosen affine
   114	parametrization of a mature line. -/
   115	theorem directCoordinateAxisMeasurement_reparam
   116	    (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k)
   117	    {iota : Type*} [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   118	    (M : DirectLdQuestion D →
   119	      MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectLdAnswer D) iota)
   120	    (hM : ∀ q, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (M q)) :
   121	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   122	    AxisParallelMeasurementReparamInvariant D.toLDTParameters
   123	      (directCoordinateAxisMeasurement D r M hM) := by
   124	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   125	  classical
   126	  intro line t f
   127	  simp only [directCoordinateAxisMeasurement, ProjMeas.postprocess,
   128	    SubMeas.postprocess_outcome, matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas_outcome]
   129	  rw [directAxisQuestionOf_rebase]
   130	  have hfiber :
   131	      Finset.univ.filter (fun answer =>
   132	        directAxisAnswerReadout D r (line.rebaseAt t) answer =
   133	          AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAt f t) =
   134	        Finset.univ.filter (fun answer =>
   135	          directAxisAnswerReadout D r line answer = f) := by
   136	    ext answer
   137	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
   138	    rw [directAxisAnswerReadout_rebase]
   139	    exact (AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAtEquiv t).injective.eq_iff
   140	  rw [hfiber]

   204	/-- The complex Born amplitude of a vector and two local effects. -/
   205	private noncomputable def vectorBornAmplitude
   206	    {iotaA iotaB : Type*}
   207	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   208	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   209	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB))
   210	    (A : Op iotaA) (B : Op iotaB) : ℂ :=
   211	  inner ℂ psi (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron A B) psi)

   213	/-- The real Born quadratic form of a vector and two local effects. -/
   214	private noncomputable def vectorBornWeight
   215	    {iotaA iotaB : Type*}
   216	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   217	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   218	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB))
   219	    (A : Op iotaA) (B : Op iotaB) : ℝ :=

   288	private theorem vectorBornWeight_finset_sum_left
   289	    {alpha iotaA iotaB : Type*}
   290	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   291	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   292	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB))
   293	    (s : Finset alpha) (A : alpha → Op iotaA) (B : Op iotaB) :
   294	    vectorBornWeight psi (∑ a ∈ s, A a) B =
   295	      ∑ a ∈ s, vectorBornWeight psi (A a) B := by
   296	  classical
   297	  induction s using Finset.induction_on with
   298	  | empty =>
   299	      simp [vectorBornWeight, vectorBornAmplitude_zero_left]
   300	  | @insert a s ha ih =>
   301	      rw [Finset.sum_insert ha, Finset.sum_insert ha,
   302	        vectorBornWeight_add_left, ih]

   305	    {beta iotaA iotaB : Type*}
   306	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   307	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   308	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB))
   309	    (A : Op iotaA) (s : Finset beta) (B : beta → Op iotaB) :
   310	    vectorBornWeight psi A (∑ b ∈ s, B b) =
   311	      ∑ b ∈ s, vectorBornWeight psi A (B b) := by
   312	  classical
   313	  induction s using Finset.induction_on with
   314	  | empty =>
   315	      simp [vectorBornWeight, vectorBornAmplitude_zero_right]
   316	  | @insert b s hb ih =>
   317	      rw [Finset.sum_insert hb, Finset.sum_insert hb,

   320	/-- Expectations in the density state associated with a strategy agree with
   321	the strategy's vector Born quadratic form. -/
   322	private theorem strategyQuantumState_ev_eq_vectorBornWeight
   323	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (A : Op S.ιA) (B : Op S.ιB) :
   324	    ev (strategyQuantumState S) (opTensor A B) =
   325	      vectorBornWeight S.ψ A B := by
   326	  letI : Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) := strategy_carrier_nonempty S
   327	  rw [show strategyQuantumState S =
   328	      PureState.toQuantumState (strategyPureState S) by
   329	        simp [strategyQuantumState],
   330	    PureState.ev_eq_re_inner]
   331	  unfold vectorBornWeight vectorBornAmplitude applyOperatorToState heteroKron opTensor
   332	  simp_rw [EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct]
   333	  change (star S.ψ ⬝ᵥ
   334	      (Matrix.kronecker A B *ᵥ S.ψ)).re =
   335	    ((Matrix.kronecker A B *ᵥ S.ψ) ⬝ᵥ star S.ψ).re
   336	  rw [dotProduct_comm]

   338	/-- Postprocessing both local measurements gives the exact double sum of the
   339	original Born weights over the two answer fibers. -/
   340	theorem directPostprocessBornWeight
   341	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
   342	    (hS : S.IsProjective)
   343	    {alpha beta : Type*} [Fintype alpha] [DecidableEq alpha]
   344	    [Fintype beta] [DecidableEq beta]
   345	    (x y : DirectLdQuestion D)
   346	    (readA : DirectLdAnswer D → alpha)
   347	    (readB : DirectLdAnswer D → beta)
   348	    (a : alpha) (b : beta) :
   349	    ev (strategyQuantumState S)
   350	        (opTensor
   351	          ((ProjMeas.postprocess
   352	            (matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas (S.A x) (hS.1 x)) readA).outcome a)
   353	          ((ProjMeas.postprocess
   354	            (matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas (S.B y) (hS.2 y)) readB).outcome b)) =
   355	      ∑ directA ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun answer => readA answer = a),
   356	        ∑ directB ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun answer => readB answer = b),
   357	          outcomeWeight S x y directA directB := by
   358	  rw [strategyQuantumState_ev_eq_vectorBornWeight]
   359	  simp only [ProjMeas.postprocess, SubMeas.postprocess_outcome,
   360	    matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas_outcome]
   361	  rw [vectorBornWeight_finset_sum_left]
   362	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   363	  intro directA _
   364	  rw [vectorBornWeight_finset_sum_right]
   365	  rfl

   367	/-- Correlated residue registers turn two block-diagonal effects into the
   368	uniform average of their matching source-block Born weights. -/
   369	private theorem seedFiberBlockBornAmplitude
   370	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams)
   371	    (A : Fin (L.q / L.m) → Op S.ιA)
   372	    (B : Fin (L.q / L.m) → Op S.ιB) :
   373	    vectorBornAmplitude (seedFiberLiftedState S L)
   374	        (Matrix.blockDiagonal A) (Matrix.blockDiagonal B) =
   375	      (Fintype.card (Fin (L.q / L.m)) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
   376	        ∑ residue, vectorBornAmplitude S.ψ (A residue) (B residue) := by
   377	  classical
   378	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   379	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   380	  unfold vectorBornAmplitude applyOperatorToState heteroKron Matrix.kronecker
   381	  simp_rw [EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct]
   382	  simp only [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_apply,
   383	    dotProduct, Matrix.mulVec]
   384	  simp_rw [← Finset.univ_product_univ, Finset.sum_product]
   385	  simp [seedFiberLiftedState_apply, Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply,

   396	/-- Correlated residue registers give the uniform average of the source-block
   397	Born weights. -/
   398	private theorem seedFiberBlockBornWeight
   399	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams)
   400	    (A : Fin (L.q / L.m) → Op S.ιA)
   401	    (B : Fin (L.q / L.m) → Op S.ιB) :
   402	    vectorBornWeight (seedFiberLiftedState S L)
   403	        (Matrix.blockDiagonal A) (Matrix.blockDiagonal B) =
   404	      (Fintype.card (Fin (L.q / L.m)) : ℝ)⁻¹ *
   405	        ∑ residue, vectorBornWeight S.ψ (A residue) (B residue) := by
   406	  unfold vectorBornWeight
   407	  rw [seedFiberBlockBornAmplitude]
   408	  simp [Complex.mul_re, Complex.inv_re, Complex.inv_im]

   410	/-- The Born weight of the seed-bearing direct adapter is the uniform average
   411	of the original seed-dependent Born weights over the correlated residue. -/
   412	theorem ldStrategyToDirect_bornWeight
   413	    (L : LdParams) (S : Strategy (ldGame L))
   414	    (x y : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   415	    (a b : DirectLdAnswer L.toDirectLdParams) :
   416	    outcomeWeight (ldStrategyToDirect L S) x y a b =
   417	      (Fintype.card (Fin (L.q / L.m)) : ℝ)⁻¹ *
   418	        ∑ residue,
   419	          outcomeWeight S
   420	            (seededLdQuestion L x residue)
   421	            (seededLdQuestion L y residue)
   422	            ((ldDirectAnswerEquiv L).symm a)
   423	            ((ldDirectAnswerEquiv L).symm b) := by
   424	  change vectorBornWeight (seedFiberLiftedState S L)
   425	      (Matrix.blockDiagonal fun residue =>
   426	        (S.A (seededLdQuestion L x residue)).effect
   427	          ((ldDirectAnswerEquiv L).symm a))
   428	      (Matrix.blockDiagonal fun residue =>
   429	        (S.B (seededLdQuestion L y residue)).effect
   430	          ((ldDirectAnswerEquiv L).symm b)) = _
   431	  exact seedFiberBlockBornWeight S L _ _

     4	/-!
     5	# The directly indexed low-degree game
     6	
     7	This module defines polynomial evaluation, questions, answers, and the game
     8	for the directly indexed low-degree interface.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The underlying game is `def:ld-game` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with source origin
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	open scoped BigOperators
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    23	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    24	
    25	noncomputable section
    26	
    27	/-- Coefficient lists for a univariate polynomial of degree at most `c` in the
    28	direct scalar field. -/
    29	abbrev DirectDegPoly (D : DirectLdParams) (c : ℕ) :=
    30	  Fin (c + 1) → DirectScalarQ D
    31	
    32	/-- A direct line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` lies on the line
    33	and every parameter presenting `u` gives value `a`.  The universal clause
    34	keeps the zero-direction case explicit. -/
    35	def DirectEvaluatesTo {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : DirectLineDesc D)
    36	    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    37	    (a : DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
    38	  (∃ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
    39	    ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction →
    40	      evalCoefficient f t = a
    41	
    42	/-- Option-completed evaluation of a direct line polynomial.  `none` is an
    43	explicit outcome when the point does not determine an evaluation; no field
    44	value is used as a fallback. -/
    45	noncomputable def directEvalOpt {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ}
    46	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    47	    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) : Option (DirectScalarQ D) := by
    48	  classical
    49	  exact if h : ∃ a : DirectScalarQ D, DirectEvaluatesTo line f u a then
    50	    some (Classical.choose h)
    51	  else none
    52	
    53	/-- The typed question alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
    54	abbrev DirectLdQuestion (D : DirectLdParams) := LdType × DirectLdSpace D
    55	
    56	/-- Canonicalize a common direct sample for one question type.  Irrelevant
    57	coordinates are fixed, so point questions reveal no sampled line index and
    58	axis-line questions reveal no diagonal direction. -/
    59	noncomputable def directLdMap (D : DirectLdParams) :
    60	    LdType → DirectLdSpace D → DirectLdSpace D
    61	  | .point, sample => ⟨sample.point, D.firstIndex, 0⟩
    62	  | .aline, sample =>
    63	      let direction := coordinateDirection sample.index
    64	      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, 0⟩
    65	  | .dline, sample =>
    66	      let direction := directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction
    67	      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, direction⟩
    68	
    69	/-- The directly indexed question distribution.  It has the same uniform
    70	ordered type-pair branches as `ldQuestionDistribution`, but its common sample
    71	contains an actual coordinate index rather than a field seed. -/
    72	noncomputable def directLdQuestionDistribution (D : DirectLdParams) :
    73	    Distribution (DirectLdQuestion D × DirectLdQuestion D) :=
    74	  (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>
    75	    ((sample.1.1, directLdMap D sample.1.1 sample.2),
    76	      (sample.1.2, directLdMap D sample.1.2 sample.2))
    77	
    78	/-- The directly indexed question law is probabilistic. -/
    79	theorem directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
    80	    (directLdQuestionDistribution D).IsProbability := by
    81	  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability
    82	    ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map _
    83	
    84	/-- The answer alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
    85	inductive DirectLdAnswer (D : DirectLdParams) where
    86	  | pointVals (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D)
    87	  | alinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
    88	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
    89	  deriving DecidableEq
    90	
    91	/-- A finite code for the directly indexed answer alphabet. -/
    92	abbrev DirectLdAnswerCode (D : DirectLdParams) :=
    93	  (Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
    94	    ((Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
    95	      (Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D))
    96	
    97	/-- Constructor-preserving equivalence between the inductive answer type and
    98	its finite code. -/
    99	noncomputable def directLdAnswerEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   100	    DirectLdAnswer D ≃ DirectLdAnswerCode D where
   101	  toFun
   102	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   103	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   104	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   105	  invFun
   106	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   107	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   108	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   109	  left_inv := by intro answer; cases answer <;> rfl
   110	  right_inv := by
   111	    intro answer
   112	    rcases answer with a | a
   113	    · rfl
   114	    · rcases a with a | a <;> rfl
   115	
   116	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Inhabited (DirectLdAnswer D) :=
   117	  ⟨.pointVals 0⟩
   118	
   119	noncomputable instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Fintype (DirectLdAnswer D) :=
   120	  Fintype.ofEquiv (DirectLdAnswerCode D) (directLdAnswerEquiv D).symm
   121	
   122	/-- Check that a direct-game answer has the constructor required by its
   123	question type. -/
   124	def validDirectLdAnswer {D : DirectLdParams} (t : LdType)
   125	    (answer : DirectLdAnswer D) : Bool :=
   126	  match t, answer with
   127	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   128	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   129	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   130	  | _, _ => false
   131	
   132	/-- The directly indexed axis-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
   133	def directAlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)
   134	    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)
   135	    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
   136	    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
   137	  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,
   138	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection line.index →
   139	      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   140	
   141	/-- The directly indexed diagonal-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
   142	def directDlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)
   143	    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)
   144	    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
   145	    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
   146	  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,
   147	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   148	      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   149	
   150	/-- The directly indexed low-degree win predicate.  It differs from
   151	`ldWinPredicate` only by reading the coordinate index directly from each line
   152	question. -/
   153	noncomputable def directLdWinPredicate (D : DirectLdParams) :
   154	    DirectLdQuestion D → DirectLdQuestion D →
   155	      DirectLdAnswer D → DirectLdAnswer D → Bool :=
   156	  open Classical in
   157	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   158	    if validDirectLdAnswer tA a && validDirectLdAnswer tB b then
   159	      match tA, tB, a, b with
   160	      | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   161	      | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   162	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   163	      | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   164	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   165	      | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   166	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   167	      | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   168	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   169	      | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   170	      | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   171	      | _, _, _, _ => true
   172	    else false
   173	
   174	/-- The directly indexed low-degree game at an arbitrary positive dimension.
   175	It is an internal analysis game, not the conditionally linear verifier game
   176	`ldGame`. -/
   177	noncomputable def directLdGame (D : DirectLdParams) : Game where
   178	  QuestionA := DirectLdQuestion D
   179	  QuestionB := DirectLdQuestion D
   180	  AnswerA := DirectLdAnswer D
   181	  AnswerB := DirectLdAnswer D
   182	  μ := directLdQuestionDistribution D
   183	  μ_prob := directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability D
   184	  decide := directLdWinPredicate D
   185	
   186	/-- The canonical point question associated with a geometric point. -/
   187	def directLdPointQuestionOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   188	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : DirectLdQuestion D :=
   189	  (.point, ⟨u, D.firstIndex, 0⟩)
   190	
   191	/-- Total point-answer relabeling used in the direct soundness conclusion.
   192	Wrong-form answers are folded into the zero tuple, exactly as for
   193	`ldPointValuesOrZero`. -/
   194	def directLdPointValuesOrZero (D : DirectLdParams) :
   195	    DirectLdAnswer D → Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D
   196	  | .pointVals values => values
   197	  | .alinePolys _ => 0
   198	  | .dlinePolys _ => 0
   199	
   200	/-- A simultaneous tuple of bounded polynomials for the directly indexed
   201	game. -/
   202	noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyTuple (D : DirectLdParams) :=
   203	  Fin D.k → PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d
   204	
   205	/-- A polynomial-tuple POVM for the directly indexed game. -/
   206	noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyMeasTuple (D : DirectLdParams) (ι : Type*)
   207	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   208	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectPolyTuple D) ι
   209	
   210	/-- Evaluate every component of a direct polynomial tuple at a point. -/
   211	def evalDirectPolyTupleAt {D : DirectLdParams}
   212	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (g : DirectPolyTuple D) :
   213	    Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D :=
   214	  fun j => MvPolynomial.eval u (g j).1
   215	
   216	end

    29	/-- Parameters for the directly indexed low-degree game.  Unlike `LdParams`,
    30	this directly indexed line-space construction has no divisibility field: its coordinate index is
    31	sampled from `Fin m` rather than encoded by fibers of `chiIndex`.
    32	
    33	This is the direct-index repair described in
    34	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`; it is not a second
    35	definition of the source verifier game. -/

    37	  q : ℕ
    38	  m : ℕ
    39	  d : ℕ
    40	  k : ℕ
    41	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    42	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    43	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    44	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q

    46	/-- The canonical scalar model for directly indexed parameters. -/
    47	noncomputable def DirectLdParams.model (D : DirectLdParams) : FixedFieldModel D.q :=
    48	  fixedFieldModel D.q D.hq
    49	
    50	/-- The scalar field of a directly indexed low-degree game. -/
    51	abbrev DirectScalarQ (D : DirectLdParams) := D.model.K
    52	
    53	/-- The first coordinate, available because directly indexed dimensions are
    54	positive. -/
    55	def DirectLdParams.firstIndex (D : DirectLdParams) : Fin D.m :=
    56	  ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one D.hm⟩
    57	
    58	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Nonempty (Fin D.m) := ⟨D.firstIndex⟩
    59	
    60	/-- The direct game used at the extended dimension of the combining map.  Its
    61	field, degree, and simultaneity parameters are inherited from `P`, while its
    62	dimension is `2 * P.m + 2`; no divisibility assertion is introduced.
    63	
    64	The construction has dimension `2 * P.m + 2` without requiring
    65	`2 * P.m + 2 ∣ P.q`; it supplies the directly indexed line and coordinate
    66	spaces used in the dimension-extension argument of
    67	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1257-1293`.
    68	-/
    69	def AdmissibleParams.extendedDirectLd (P : AdmissibleParams) : DirectLdParams where
    70	  q := P.q
    71	  m := 2 * P.m + 2
    72	  d := P.d

    79	/-- A common random sample for the directly indexed question distribution.
    80	The point, coordinate index, and unrestricted direction are mutually uniform. -/
    81	structure DirectLdSpace (D : DirectLdParams) where
    82	  point : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
    83	  index : Fin D.m
    84	  direction : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
    85	  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype
    86	
    87	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Nonempty (DirectLdSpace D) :=
    88	  ⟨⟨0, D.firstIndex, 0⟩⟩
    89	
    90	/-- Decompose a direct sample into its point and the remaining independent
    91	coordinates. -/
    92	private def directLdSpacePointEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
    93	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
    94	      (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ×
    95	        (Fin D.m × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) where
    96	  toFun sample := (sample.point, sample.index, sample.direction)
    97	  invFun sample := ⟨sample.1, sample.2.1, sample.2.2⟩
    98	  left_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
    99	  right_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl

   101	/-- Decompose a direct sample into its stored index and the remaining
   102	independent coordinates. -/
   103	def directLdSpaceIndexEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   104	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
   105	      Fin D.m ×
   106	        ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ×
   107	          (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) where
   108	  toFun sample := (sample.index, sample.point, sample.direction)
   109	  invFun sample := ⟨sample.2.1, sample.1, sample.2.2⟩
   110	  left_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
   111	  right_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl

   114	abbrev directLdSpaceIndexSplitEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   115	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
   116	      Fin D.m × ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) :=

   120	def directPrefixProjection {D : DirectLdParams} (i : Fin D.m)

   138	  | .axis _ _ _ => .axis

    31	/-- Numerical parameters for the low-degree game.  The ambient coefficient

    33	model supplied by each parameter record.  This is the Lean carrier for

    42	  k : ℕ

   120	chosen index and retains the suffix of the direction vector.  This is the

   602	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.

   604	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   605	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   606	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   607	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   608	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   609	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   610	
   611	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   612	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   613	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
   614	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.

   616	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   617	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   618	  open Classical in
   619	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   620	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   621	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   622	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   623	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   624	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   625	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   626	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   627	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   628	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   629	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   630	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   631	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   632	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   633	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   634	      else false

   637	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-156`, paper origin
   638	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.

   642	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   643	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   644	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P

   647	    exact Distribution.IsProbability.map
   648	      (uniformDistribution_isProbability ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P)) _
   649	  decide := ldWinPredicate P

   651	end

1	\section{The test}\label{sec:the-test}
     2	
     3	\begin{definition}[Roles]
     4	The low individual degree test will be played between two provers and a verifier.
     5	The two provers are named Player~$\mathrm{A}$ and Player~$\mathrm{B}$.
     6	A \emph{role} $r$ is an element of the set $\{\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}\}$.
     7	Given a role~$r$, we write $\overline{r}$ for the other element of the set $\{\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}\}$.
     8	\end{definition}
     9	
    10	\begin{definition}[Low individual degree test]
    11	Let~$m$ and~$d$ be nonnegative integers.
    12	Let $q$ be a prime power.
    13	Then the \emph{$(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test}
    14	is stated in \Cref{fig:test}.
    15	\end{definition}
    16	
    17	{
    18	\floatstyle{boxed} 
    19	\restylefloat{figure}
    20	\begin{figure}
    21	With probability~$\tfrac{1}{3}$ each, perform one of the following three tests.
    22	\begin{enumerate}
    23		\item \textbf{Axis-parallel lines test:}
    24			Pick a uniformly random role $\br \sim \{\mathrm{A},\mathrm{B}\}$.
    25			Let $\bu \sim \F_q^m$ be a uniformly random point.
    26			Select $\bi \sim \{1, \ldots, m\}$ uniformly at random,
    27			and let $\bell = \{\bu + t \cdot e_{\bi} \mid t \in \F_q\}$
    28			be the axis-parallel line which passes through~$\bu$ in the $\bi$-th direction.
    29			\begin{itemize}
    30			\item[$\circ$] Player~$\br$: 
    31				Give $\bell$;
    32				receive the univariate degree-$d$ polynomial $\boldf:\bell \rightarrow \F_q$.
    33			\item[$\circ$] Player~$\overline{\br}$:
    34				Give $\bu$;
    35				receive $\ba \in \F_q$.
    36			\end{itemize}
    37			Accept if $\boldf(\bu) = \ba$.
    38		\item \textbf{Self-consistency test:}
    39			Let $\bu \sim \F_q^m$ be a uniformly random point.
    40			\begin{itemize}
    41			\item[$\circ$] Player~$\mathrm{A}$: 
    42				Give $\bu$;
    43				receive $\ba \in \F_q$.
    44			\item[$\circ$] Player~$\mathrm{B}$:
    45				Give $\bu$;
    46				receive $\bb \in \F_q$.
    47			\end{itemize}
    48			Accept if $\ba = \bb$.
    49		\item \textbf{Diagonal lines test:}
    50			Pick a uniformly random role $\br \sim \{\mathrm{A},\mathrm{B}\}$.
    51			Let $\bu \sim \F_q^m$ be a uniformly random point.
    52			Select $\bi \sim \{1, \ldots, m\}$ uniformly at random,
    53			and let $\bv \in \F_q^m$ be a uniformly random point whose last $m - \bi$ coordinates are~$0$.
    54			Finally,
    55			let $\bell = \{\bu + t \cdot \bv \mid t \in \F_q\}$
    56			be the line which passes through~$\bu$ in direction~$\bv$.
    57			\begin{itemize}
    58			\item[$\circ$] Player~$\br$: 
    59				Give $\bell$;
    60				receive the univariate degree-$md$ polynomial $\boldf:\bell \rightarrow \F_q$.
    61			\item[$\circ$] Player~$\overline{\br}$:
    62				Give $\bu$;
    63				receive $\ba \in \F_q$.
    64			\end{itemize}
    65			Accept if $\boldf(\bu) = \ba$.
    66		\end{enumerate}
    67		\caption{The $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test.\label{fig:test}}
    68	\end{figure}

    71	An important class of strategies are those which are \emph{symmetric}.
    72	In this case, the bipartite state $\ket{\psi}$ Alice and Bob share is symmetric.
    73	Furthermore, for any question Alice and Bob receive, they apply the same measurement to their share of the state.
    74	This means that rather than, for example, keeping track of a separate points measurement for Alice and Bob,
    75	we can use a single measurement to refer to both of their strategies,
    76	and similarly for the axis-parallel lines and diagonal lines measurements.
    77	This is formalized in the following definition, where we also consider strategies which are projective.
    78	
    79	\begin{definition}[Symmetric, projective strategy]
    80	A \emph{symmetric, projective strategy} for the $(m,q, d)$-low individual degree test
    81	is a tuple $(\psi, A, B, L)$ defined as follows.
    82	\begin{itemize}
    83	\item[$\circ$] $\ket{\psi} \in \calH \ot \calH$ is a bipartite, permutation-invariant state.
    84	\item[$\circ$] $A = \{A^u_a\}$ contains a matrix for each $u \in \F_q^m$ and $a \in \F_q$.
    85				For each $u$, $A^u$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH$.
    86	\item[$\circ$] $B = \{B^{\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each axis-parallel line~$\ell$ in $\F_q^m$
    87				and univariate degree-$d$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \F_q$.
    88				For each $\ell$, $B^{\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH$.
    89	\item[$\circ$] $L = \{L^{\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each line~$\ell$ in $\F_q^m$
    90				and univariate degree-$md$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \F_q$.
    91				For each $\ell$, $L^{\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH$.
    92	\end{itemize}
    93	\end{definition}
    94	
    95	We can also consider more general strategies which are no longer assumed to be symmetric.
    96	In this case, Players~$\mathrm{A}$ and~$\mathrm{B}$ each have their own versions of the measurements~$A$, $B$, and~$L$.
    97	
    98	\begin{definition}[General projective strategy]
    99	A \emph{projective strategy} for the $(m,q, d)$-low individual degree test
   100	is a tuple $(\psi, A^{\mathrm{A}},B^{\mathrm{A}},L^{\mathrm{A}},A^{\mathrm{B}},B^{\mathrm{B}},L^{\mathrm{B}})$ defined as follows.
   101	\begin{itemize}
   102	\item[$\circ$] $\ket{\psi} \in \calH_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{B}}$ is a bipartite state.
   103	\end{itemize}
   104	Furthermore, for each~$w \in \{\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}\}$:
   105	\begin{itemize}
   106	\item[$\circ$] $A^{w} = \{A^{w,u}_a\}$ contains a matrix for each $u \in \F_q^m$ and $a \in \F_q$.
   107				For each $u$, $A^{w,u}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH_{w}$.
   108	\item[$\circ$] $B^{w} = \{B^{w,\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each axis-parallel line~$\ell$ in $\F_q^m$
   109				and univariate degree-$d$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \F_q$.
   110				For each $\ell$, $B^{w,\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH_{w}$.
   111	\item[$\circ$] $L^w = \{L^{w,\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each line~$\ell$ in $\F_q^m$
   112				and univariate degree-$md$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \F_q$.
   113				For each $\ell$, $L^{w,\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH_{w}$.
   114	\end{itemize}
   115	\end{definition}
   116	
   117	\begin{remark}
   118	Throughout this work, we will only consider projective strategies.
   119	So we will henceforth use the terms ``strategy" and ``symmetric strategy'' to refer exclusively to projective strategies and symmetric, projective strategies, respectively.
   120	
   121	In addition, we will spend the vast majority of this work dealing solely with symmetric strategies, as they are notationally simpler to work with.
   122	Much of this work will focus on proving~\Cref{thm:main-induction},
   123	a variant of our main theorem for symmetric strategies.
   124	Our main theorem for general strategies, \Cref{thm:main-formal} below, will be proven in \Cref{sec:induction} by a standard reduction to the symmetric case.
   125	We will only see these more cumbersome-to-write general strategies
   126	in this section, where we state \Cref{thm:main-formal},
   127	and in \Cref{sec:induction}, where we carry out the reduction.
   128	\end{remark}
   129	
   130	\begin{definition}[Good strategy]
   131	A strategy is $(\eps, \delta, \gamma)$-good if it
   132	passes the axis-parallel lines test with probability at least $1-\eps$,
   133	the self consistency test with probability at least~$1-\delta$,
   134	and the diagonal lines test with probability at least~$1-\gamma$.
   135	\end{definition}
   136	
   137	\begin{remark}\label{rem:good-strat-characterization}
   138	Using notation which will be introduced in \Cref{sec:comparing-measurements} below,
   139	a symmetric strategy is $(\eps, \delta, \gamma)$-good
   140	if and only if it satisfies the following three conditions.
   141	For $\bell$ and $\bu$ as in the axis-parallel lines test,
   142	\begin{equation*}
   143	A^u_a \ot I \simeq_{\eps} I \ot B^{\ell}_{[f(u)=a]},
   144	\quad
   145	\text{and}
   146	\quad
   147	A^u_a \ot I \simeq_{\delta} I \ot A^u_a.
   148	\end{equation*}
   149	And for $\bell$ and $\bu$ as in the diagonal lines test,
   150	\begin{equation*}
   151	A^u_a \ot I \simeq_{\gamma} I \ot L^{\ell}_{[f(u)=a]}.
   152	\end{equation*}
   153	\end{remark}
   154	
   155	\begin{notation}\label{not:conditioned-on-last-direction}
   156	Our proof will be via induction,
   157	i.e.\ proving soundness of the $(m+1,q,d)$-low individual degree test
   158	using the soundness of the $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test.
   159	To do this, we will frequently use the axis-parallel line test in the specific case of $i = m+1$.
   160	Thus, it will be convenient to introduce the following notation.
   161	Let $(\psi, A, B, L)$ be a symmetric strategy for the $(m+1, q, d)$-low individual degree test,
   162	Then for each $u \in \F_q^m$ we will write $B^u_f$ as shorthand for $B^{\ell}_f$,
   163	where $\ell = \{(u, x) \mid x \in \F_q\}$.
   164	For a function $f:\ell \rightarrow \F_q$,
   165	we will also sometimes write $f(x)$ as shorthand for $f(u,x)$.
   166	\end{notation}
   167	
   168	\begin{definition}
   169	Consider the $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test.
   170	For $j \in \{1, \ldots, m\}$,
   171	we refer to the \emph{$j$-restricted diagonal lines test}
   172	as the diagonal lines test conditioned on $\bi = j$.
   173	For example, in the $m$-restricted diagonal lines test,
   174	the line $\bell$ is simply a uniformly random line in $\F_q^m$.
   175	\end{definition}
   176	
   177	Now we state our main theorem using notation which will be introduced in \Cref{sec:prelims} below.
   178	This the formal version of \Cref{thm:main-informal}.
   179	
   180	\begin{theorem}[Main theorem; quantum soundness of the low individual degree test]\label{thm:main-formal}
   181	  Consider a projective strategy $(\psi, A^{\mathrm{A}},B^{\mathrm{A}},L^{\mathrm{A}},A^{\mathrm{B}},B^{\mathrm{B}},L^{\mathrm{B}})$ 
   182	   which passes the  $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test with probability at least $1-\eps$.
   183	  Let $k \geq md$ be an integer.
   184	  Let
   185	  \begin{equation*}
   186	  \nu = 100000 k^2m^4 \cdot \Big(\eps^{1/40000} + (d/q)^{1/40000} + e^{-k/(2560000m^2)}\Big).
   187	  \end{equation*}
   188	Then there exists projective measurements $G^{\mathrm{A}}, G^{\mathrm{B}} \in \polymeas{m}{q}{d}$ with the following properties:
   189	\begin{enumerate}
   190	  \item (Consistency with~$A$):  On average over $\bu \sim \F_q^{m}$,
   191		  \begin{align*}
   192		  A^{\mathrm{A},u}_a \otimes I
   193		  	&\simeq_{\nu} I \otimes G^{\mathrm{B}}_{[g(u)=a]},\\
   194		I \otimes A^{\mathrm{B},u}_a
   195		  	&\simeq_{\nu}  G^{\mathrm{A}}_{[g(u)=a]} \ot I.
   196		  \end{align*}
   197	\item (Self-consistency):
   198		\begin{equation*}
   199		G^{\mathrm{A}}_g \ot I \simeq_{\nu} I \ot G^{\mathrm{B}}_g.
   200		\end{equation*}
   201	\end{enumerate}
   202	\end{theorem}
   203	
   204	We note that there is a tradeoff in \Cref{thm:main-formal} specified by the parameter~$k$.
   205	As~$k$ increases, $\nu$'s prefactor $k^2$ increases.
   206	On the other hand, as $k$ increases, the term $e^{- k/(2560000m^2)}$ which also occurs in $\nu$ \emph{decreases}.
   207	Thus, when applying this theorem, one must select~$k$ to balance these competing demands.
   208	Typically, choosing $k = \poly(m)$ should be more than sufficient for applications.
   209	We believe that this parameter~$k$ is an artifact of our proof,
   210	and we hope that it will be removed in the future.

    17	\section{The assertion}
    18	
    19	We examine the statement of the commutativity theorem for the slice
    20	measurements $G^x$ in \cite[Section~\emph{Commutativity of~$G$}]{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}.%
    21	\footnote{Tracked in \ghissue{930}. The paper passage is
    22	\path{references/ldt-paper/commutativity-G.tex}, lines~228--257.}
    23	The source states that $(\psi,A,B,L)$ is an
    24	$(\eps,\delta,\gamma)$-good symmetric strategy for the $(m,q,d)$ low
    25	individual degree test. It then assumes, on average over
    26	$(\bu,\bx) \in \F_q^{m+1}$,
    27	\[
    28	  A^{u,x}_a \ot I \simeq_\zeta I \ot G^x_{[g(u)=a]},
    29	\]
    30	where $G^x$ is a projective submeasurement with outcomes in
    31	$\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$.
    32	
    33	\section{The point at issue}
    34	
    35	The displayed consistency condition is naturally a hypothesis about a
    36	strategy for the $(m+1,q,d)$ test. In that test, the point measurement
    37	$A$ is indexed by points of $\F_q^{m+1}$, which are written as
    38	$(u,x)$ with $u\in\F_q^m$ and $x\in\F_q$. A strategy for the
    39	$(m,q,d)$ test has point measurements indexed by $\F_q^m$ instead, so
    40	$A^{u,x}_a$ is not the corresponding point measurement.
    41	
    42	The surrounding argument also uses the theorem in the successor step:
    43	the slice measurements $G^x$ live in dimension $m$, and they are pasted
    44	to produce a measurement in dimension $m+1$. Thus the intended ambient
    45	strategy is the $(m+1,q,d)$ strategy, while the slice family remains a
    46	family of $m$-variable polynomial submeasurements.
    47	
    48	\section{The formal and blueprint statements}
    49	
    50	The blueprint states the corrected ambient dimension: in
    51	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch08_commutativity.tex}, the theorem
    52	\leanid{thm:com-main} assumes an $(\eps,\delta,\gamma)$-good symmetric

    54	projective submeasurements $G^x$ in $\polysub{m}{q}{d}$.

    56	The formal theorem uses the same convention.%

    62	\[
    63	  G^x_g G^y_h \ot I \approx_\nu G^y_h G^x_g \ot I,
    64	  \qquad
    65	  \nu = 30m\left(\gamma^{1/4}+\zeta^{1/4}+(d/q)^{1/4}\right),
    66	\]
    67	with the same three hypotheses of consistency with $A$, strong
    68	self-consistency, and boundedness.

    71

    18	\section{At a glance}
    19	
    20	\begin{itemize}
    21	  \item \textbf{Difficulty: medium.}  Two related matters are recorded.
    22	  First, the soundness analysis of the Pauli basis test invokes the
    23	  classical low individual degree game at dimension $2m+2$, and the game's
    24	  question distribution is undefined at that dimension for the admissible
    25	  parameters: it requires $2m+2$ to divide $q$, while admissibility supplies
    26	  only $m \mid q$; the repair is a statement-level reformulation of an
    27	  imported theorem, not a new proof.  Second, the import of the classical
    28	  game's quantum soundness from the tensor-code paper carries two open
    29	  verification obligations at every dimension: the asserted identity with
    30	  the cited tensor-code test is not an identity and must be replaced by a
    31	  reduction with a value bound, and the source's instantiation of the
    32	  theorem's auxiliary parameter violates its lower bound at small
    33	  dimensions (Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}).
    34	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight:} for the recommended direction, about
    35	  \textbf{3--5 new definitions or interfaces} (a line-point distribution with

    39	  and the $\chi$-based game (parsing pullback, seed-fiber averaging with
    40	  its open synchronicity-branch control, and a dilation--compression round

    42	  Discharging the import obligations of
    43	  Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations} adds the pair-measurement

    59	\section{Key theorem forms}
    60	
    61	Throughout, $q = 2^k$ with $k$ odd is an admissible field size, the tuple
    62	$(q,m,d)$ is admissible when moreover $d \ge 1$ and $m \mid q$, and
    63	$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ denotes the $m$-variate polynomial representatives
    64	over $\F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$.  The comparison involves four
    65	theorem forms.
    66	\begin{enumerate}
    67	  \item \textbf{Source theorem form} (the polynomial-pair measurement).  There
    68	  is a function $\delta_S(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$,
    69	  for universal constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$, such that for every
    70	  admissible $(q,m,d)$ and every projective strategy for the Pauli basis test
    71	  succeeding with probability at least $1-\eps$, there is a projective
    72	  measurement $\{\hat S_{g_X,g_Z}\}$ with outcomes pairs of polynomials in
    73	  $\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ whose evaluations are $\delta_S$-consistent, on
    74	  average over a uniform point $u \in \F_q^m$ and in both bases
    75	  $W \in \{X,Z\}$, with the corresponding points measurements
    76	  $\{\hat M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\}$ of the strategy, together with the
    77	  symmetric counterpart of this relation.
    78	  \item \textbf{Missing instantiation obligation.}  The classical low
    79	  individual degree game with parameter tuple $(q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)$ is well
    80	  defined, and the combined point and line measurements assembled in the
    81	  analysis constitute a strategy for it of value at least
    82	  $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$.  The game's question distribution draws
    83	  its axis and diagonal indices through an index function
    84	  $\chi_{2m+2}\colon \F_q \to \{1,\ldots,2m+2\}$ with classes of equal size
    85	  $q/(2m+2)$, so the game exists only when $2m+2$ divides $q$.
    86	  \item \textbf{Restricted form supported by the present route.}  The source
    87	  theorem form under the additional hypothesis $2m+2 \mid q$.  Among
    88	  admissible tuples this hypothesis holds exactly when $m = 1$ and
    89	  $q \ge 8$; it fails for every admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$ and for
    90	  $(q,m) = (2,1)$.
    91	  \item \textbf{Repaired import form} (recommended target).  Quantum
    92	  soundness of the directly indexed variant of the classical low individual
    93	  degree game over $\F_q^{m'}$, for every dimension $m' \ge 1$ and
    94	  admissible $q$, with no divisibility hypothesis: the question
    95	  distribution samples the axis index, and the diagonal prefix index,
    96	  uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,m'\}$ directly rather than through an index
    97	  function on $\F_q$, and line questions carry the sampled index itself in
    98	  place of the seed $s \in \F_q$; the error is
    99	  $\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}(\eps,q,m',d,k) = a(dm'k)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} +
   100	  2^{-bm'd})$.  This is a candidate target form, not an established one:
   101	  proving it carries the same two import obligations as the $\chi$-based
   102	  import (Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}), and deriving the present
   103	  form from it when $m' \mid q$ requires the strategy transport described
   104	  under the candidate repairs below, whose synchronicity step is an open
   105	  obligation.
   106	\end{enumerate}

   108	\section{The source assertion and the obstruction}
   109	
   110	We examine the final step of the subsection ``Applying the classical
   111	low-degree test'' in the analysis of the Pauli basis test in the compression
   112	paper of Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright, and Yuen (MIP$^{*}$=RE,
   113	arXiv:2001.04383), whose quantum soundness component builds on the low
   114	individual degree test of \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}.%
   115	\footnote{Tracked in \localissue{0002}.  In the mirror of the source
   116	consulted here, the polynomial-pair lemma and its proof are at
   117	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
   118	lines~1267--1288; the sub-line lemma is at lines~1063--1116 and the combined
   119	line lemma at lines~1020--1034 of the same file.  The game parametrization
   120	with its divisibility, the index function, the soundness statement with its
   121	proof, and admissibility are at

   123	lines~33--35, 214--219, 413--458, and 958--961.}

   126	$\{\hat Q^{\ell}_f\}$, indexed by points of $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and lines in

   130	  \mathsf{ldparams} = (q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)

   138	The game, however, is parametrized by tuples $(q,m',d,k)$ with $q$ an
   139	admissible field size \emph{and $m'$ dividing $q$}.  The divisibility is not
   140	incidental: the question distribution is a conditionally linear distribution
   141	in which a uniform seed coordinate $s \in \F_q$, read as an integer in
   142	$\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$, determines the axis or diagonal index through the unique
   143	$\chi(s)$ with
   144	\[
   145	  s = (\chi(s)-1)\,\frac{q}{m'} + r, \qquad 0 \le r < \frac{q}{m'},
   146	  \tag{\path{eq:chi-func}}

   152	Admissibility of $(q,m,d)$ supplies only $m \mid q$.  Since an admissible $q$
   153	is a power of two, $m \mid q$ forces $m = 2^j$.  For $j \ge 1$ the integer
   154	$m+1 \ge 3$ is odd, so $2m+2 = 2(m+1)$ has an odd factor exceeding $1$ and
   155	divides no power of two; for $m = 1$ the condition $4 \mid q$ holds for every
   156	admissible $q$ except $q = 2$.  Thus the instantiation at dimension $2m+2$ is

   158	$(q,m,d) = (8,2,1)$ is admissible, while $6 \nmid 8$.  The source performs

   161	the Pauli basis test that rests on it, only for $m = 1$ and $q \ge 8$.

   163	\section{What the cited soundness theorem requires: the import obligations}
   164	\label{sec:import-obligations}
   165	
   166	The quantum soundness theorem for the classical game inherits the constraint
   167	$m' \mid q$ solely because it is stated for the game just described; its
   168	proof fixes an admissible $q$ with $m' \mid q$, asserts that the game with
   169	simultaneity parameter $1$ is \emph{identical} to the two-prover tensor-code
   170	test for the Reed--Solomon tensor code $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$ of the same
   171	authors' \emph{Quantum soundness of testing tensor codes} (arXiv:2111.08131)
   172	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}, and concludes by Theorem~4.7 there, instantiated with
   173	that theorem's auxiliary integer parameter --- denoted $k$ in that source,
   174	and written $K$ here to avoid clashing with the field exponent and the
   175	simultaneity parameter --- chosen as $(m')^3 d$.  Neither
   176	the asserted identity nor the instantiation is complete as stated, so the
   177	import carries two verification obligations, which this section details and
   178	which the blueprint's proof node for the soundness statement records as
   179	open.  Both obligations are independent of the divisibility question: they
   180	arise at every dimension, for the $\chi$-based game where it is defined and
   181	equally for the directly indexed variant proposed under the candidate
   182	repairs.
   183	
   184	\paragraph{The cited test.}
   185	In the two-prover tensor-code test (Figures~1 and~2 of
   186	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}; the two-prover strategy format and the goodness
   187	measure are Definitions~4.5 and~4.6 there), the referee performs one of
   188	three subtests with probability $1/3$ each, assigning the two roles of each
   189	subtest to the two provers uniformly at random.  \emph{Axis-parallel lines
   190	test}: sample a uniform point $u \in [n]^{m'}$ and a uniform axis
   191	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$; send the axis-parallel line $\ell$ through $u$ in
   192	direction $j$ to one prover, who answers a codeword $g \in \mathcal C$;
   193	send $u$ to the other, who answers a field value $a$; accept iff
   194	$g(u_j) = a$.  \emph{Subcube commutation test}: sample
   195	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$ and a subcube $H \subseteq [n]^{m'}$ by fixing the
   196	last $j-1$ coordinates uniformly; sample $u, v$ independently and uniformly
   197	in $H$ and a uniform order bit; send the ordered pair $(u,v)$ or $(v,u)$ to
   198	one prover, who answers a pair $(b_u, b_v)$ of field values; send $u$ to
   199	the other, who answers $a$; accept iff $b_u = a$.  \emph{Synchronicity
   200	test}: send one identical question --- a line, a point, or an ordered
   201	pair, with probability $1/3$ each --- to both provers and accept iff their
   202	answers agree.  Theorem~4.7 supposes a two-prover strategy passing this
   203	test with probability $1-\eps$ together with an integer parameter
   204	$K \ge 12 m' t$, where $t$ is the interpolation parameter of the base code
   205	--- for the degree-$d$ Reed--Solomon code, of blocklength $n = q$ and
   206	distance $q-d$, one has $t = d+1$ --- and produces projective measurements
   207	$\{G_c\}$ and $\{\tilde G_c\}$ with outcomes in $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$,
   208	consistent with one prover's points measurements, with the other prover's
   209	lines measurements, and with each other, up to
   210	$\eta'(m',t,K,\eps,n^{-1}) = \mathrm{poly}(m',t,K) \cdot
   211	\mathrm{poly}(\eps, n^{-1}, e^{-K/(m')^2})$.
   212	
   213	\paragraph{Obligation 1: the game correspondence.}
   214	The source asserts that the $\chi$-based game at parameters $(q,m',d,1)$
   215	is this test.  It is not, in four respects.
   216	(i)~The game has no pair questions.  A pair question of the test reveals
   217	two points of a \emph{hidden} subcube --- the subcube itself is not sent
   218	--- and is answered by two field values, while the game's diagonal-line
   219	question reveals a full line description and is answered by a degree-$m'd$
   220	polynomial.  A reduction must construct the pair measurements from the
   221	diagonal-line measurements by post-processing (measure a line through $u$
   222	and $v$ and evaluate the answered polynomial at the two parameters), and
   223	both directions of the information mismatch matter: the game's line
   224	description carries an index and a seed, neither of which is a function of
   225	the pair $(u,v)$, so the constructed measurement must average over the
   226	compatible indices and seeds; and the game's diagonal lines fix the
   227	\emph{first} $i-1$ coordinates where the test's subcubes fix the
   228	\emph{last} $j-1$, so the coordinate conventions must be aligned.  The
   229	construction must preserve projectivity and must match the law of the
   230	hidden-subcube pair with the law induced by the game's diagonal sampling.
   231	(ii)~The game's line questions carry the seed $s \in \F_q$; the test's
   232	carry only the line.  A strategy may depend on the seed beyond its class
   233	$\chi^{-1}(i)$, and removing this dependence runs into the fiber-averaging
   234	difficulty made explicit under the candidate repairs: averaging preserves
   235	the line-versus-point branches exactly but not the synchronicity branches.
   236	(iii)~The branch weights differ: each nontrivial cross-test has mass $1/3$
   237	in the test against $2/9$ in the game.  Once the per-branch predicates are
   238	matched, the intended bookkeeping bound is that the constructed strategy's
   239	rejection probability in the test is at most $\tfrac32$ times the game's
   240	rejection probability, up to the $O(1/(m'q))$ of item~(iv); this bound is
   241	the target of the obligation, not an established fact.
   242	(iv)~The game's predicate fixes an acceptance convention on diagonal
   243	questions with zero direction --- an event of probability at most
   244	$2/(m'q)$, recorded in the blueprint's remark on zero directions --- for
   245	which the test has no counterpart branch.
   246	Finally, the displayed conclusions of Theorem~4.7 pair one prover's points
   247	measurements with the other prover's tensor-codeword measurement, and the
   248	first prover's tensor-codeword measurement with the second prover's lines
   249	measurements, while the game-level statement asserts the point consistency
   250	in both directions; deriving the stated form uses the role symmetrization
   251	of the test and belongs to the correspondence.  None of these steps is
   252	difficult to state, but none is carried out in the source, and together
   253	they replace the asserted one-line identity by a reduction carrying its
   254	own value bound.
   255	
   256	\paragraph{Obligation 2: the parameter bound.}
   257	Theorem~4.7 requires $K \ge 12 m' t = 12 m' (d+1)$.  The source
   258	instantiates $K = (m')^3 d$, which meets the bound iff
   259	$(m')^2 d \ge 12(d+1)$: this holds for all $d \ge 1$ when $m' \ge 5$,
   260	holds at $m' = 4$ exactly when $d \ge 3$, and fails for every $d$ when
   261	$m' \le 3$.  In the game's parameter domain the dimension divides the
   262	admissible field size and is therefore a power of two, so the source's
   263	instantiation violates the hypothesis exactly at $m' \in \{1,2\}$ for
   264	every $d$ and at $m' = 4$ for $d \in \{1,2\}$ --- in particular, in the
   265	multilinear regime $d = 1$, at every dimension $m' \le 4$.  A candidate
   266	repair is to instantiate $K = \max((m')^3 d,\, 12 m'(d+1))$; the open
   267	obligation is then to re-absorb the error, that is, to check that
   268	$\mathrm{poly}(m',t,K)$ and $e^{-K/(m')^2}$ still collapse to the form
   269	$a(dm')^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bm'd})$ in the small-$m'$ cases where the
   270	maximum is $12m'(d+1)$ --- plausible, since there
   271	$e^{-K/(m')^2} = e^{-12(d+1)/m'}$ decays in $d$ at a rate comparable to
   272	$2^{-m'd}$ for $m' \le 4$, but not checked here.
   273	
   274	In the correspondence of Obligation~1, the only role of the divisibility
   275	$m' \mid q$ is to make the $\chi$-sampled index uniform.  The underlying
   276	mathematics does not need the divisibility.  The low
   277	individual degree test of \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree} samples its axis
   278	index $i$ uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,m'\}$ directly, with no index function
   279	on $\F_q$ and no divisibility hypothesis,%
   280	\footnote{See the test figure in \path{references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex}.}
   281	and the tensor-code test is likewise a test about the code
   282	$\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$, not about an encoding of indices into $\F_q$.  The
   283	$\chi$-based packaging exists so that the question distribution is
   284	conditionally linear, which the introspection machinery requires for the
   285	game the players actually play --- the Pauli basis test at dimension $m$,
   286	where admissibility does supply the divisibility.  The game at dimension
   287	$2m+2$ never appears in a verifier; it is an internal analysis device in the
   288	proof of the polynomial-pair lemma, so nothing there requires its question
   289	distribution to be conditionally linear.
