    17	\section{Purpose}
    18	
    19	When a formalization relies on a cited mathematical source, the cited source
    20	should remain intact.  It is a source, not an errata file.  If a possible gap,
    21	missing hypothesis, incorrect numerical constant, or other mathematical
    22	discrepancy is found, the matter should be recorded in a separate LaTeX note.
    23	In this repository such notes live under \path{docs/paper-gaps/}.  The same
    24	principle applies when the formal development has already diverged from the
    25	cited source, for instance by changing a statement so that it compiles, or by
    26	using a different mathematical route because an available formal-library theorem
    27	has a slightly different form.  Such a note is a mathematical note first, and a
    28	record of the formalization second: it should be readable by a mathematician or
    29	mathematical physicist who has not followed the issue discussion.
    30	
    31	The note should isolate the mathematical mechanism.  It should say what the
    32	cited source asserts, what the cited results actually imply, where a term or
    33	hypothesis is lost, and what statement the formal development proves instead.
    34	If the formal proof takes a different route, the note should explain the
    35	replacement argument and the hypotheses on which it rests.  This is especially
    36	important when the proof uses a theorem, construction, or convention from
    37	Mathlib which is not part of the cited argument.  In that case the note should
    38	state the Mathlib result in ordinary mathematical language, explain how it is
    39	specialized to the notation of the paper, and compare its hypotheses and
    40	conclusion with the step it replaces.  It should not merely say that \Lean{} did
    41	not accept a proof, that the modified proof compiles, or that a named library
    42	lemma was applied.
    43	
    44	The documents in this directory should themselves follow this standard.  A
    45	policy or template which reads like a checklist will tend to produce checklist
    46	notes; the examples and templates should therefore be written as mathematical
    47	prose.
    48	
    49	\section{Concision and Readability}
    50	
    51	A paper-gap note should be short enough that a reader can understand the issue
    52	in one sitting.  The first page should answer four questions: what the source
    53	uses, how hard the remaining formal work is, what the formalization or audit
    54	checked, and what the current verdict is.  Begin with a short
    55	\emph{At a glance} section when the note concerns an open or recently resolved
    56	formalization task.  That section should estimate the difficulty, the rough
    57	implementation weight, the split between Mathlib reuse and project-local work,
    58	and the key Mathlib APIs or modules.  Use honest ranges, not false precision.
    59	
    60	The \emph{Key theorem forms} section should be Section~2, immediately after
    61	\emph{At a glance}.  Put the theorem forms before the source details so the
    62	reader knows what the formalization is aiming to prove.  After that, keep the
    63	source assertion, the mechanism being checked, the blueprint/formal comparison,
    64	and the conclusion.  Use more sections only when a counterexample or long
    65	derivation genuinely needs room.
    66	
    67	Keep background to the minimum needed for the local point.  Prefer one clear
    68	special case over a general restatement of the surrounding theorem.  Use displayed
    69	equations for the source assertion, the key calculation, and the theorem forms;
    70	avoid displays for traceability data, declaration names, or long lists.  The
    71	blueprint/formal comparison should be compact and should not repeat the theorem
    72	forms.  The section ``Form of the Note'' below specifies where traceability data
    73	belongs; the body should read as mathematical prose, not as a log.
    74	
    75	If the verdict is that there is no mathematical discrepancy, say so plainly and
    76	stop.  Keep the conclusion highly compact, normally under twenty source lines.
    77	If the only remaining work is an implementation task, name it briefly and link
    78	the issue or pull request in a footnote.
    79	
    80	\section{When the Investigation Starts}
    81	
    82	The investigation starts when the obstruction appears to be mathematical rather
    83	than merely formal.  No final judgement is needed at this stage.  It is enough
    84	that, after reading the relevant source and attempting the corresponding formal
    85	statement, the proof seems to require a different scalar, an additional
    86	hypothesis, a different tensor placement, a distinction between two objects which
    87	the prose identifies, or an auxiliary assertion not supplied by the cited
    88	argument.
    89	
    90	The same investigation should also start when such a deviation is discovered
    91	after the fact.  If the existing formal development or informal blueprint has
    92	already changed the statement, strengthened a hypothesis, weakened a conclusion,
    93	inserted an unadvertised lemma, or replaced the cited proof by a different
    94	formal-library argument, the mathematical change should be documented even if all
    95	relevant files already compile.
    96	
    97	At this early stage the purpose is to preserve the question while it is still
    98	local.  The note may later conclude that the matter is only notational, that an
    99	intermediate estimate in the cited source needs a harmless correction, that a
   100	missing hypothesis is genuinely needed, or that no discrepancy remains.  Thus
   101	the trigger is not the severity of the eventual verdict, but the appearance of a
   102	real mismatch between the cited reasoning and the statement that can be
   103	formalized.
   104	
   105	A failed tactic search, a missing formal lemma, or an inconvenient coercion is
   106	not enough.  The obstruction must survive translation back into ordinary
   107	mathematics.
   108	
   109	Sometimes an investigation uncovers an improvement that is not a discrepancy:
   110	the formalization works correctly, but it could be simplified by using an
   111	existing library, replacing a custom type, or adopting a cleaner proof route.
   112	These are not, by themselves, paper-gap notes.  They are action items.  When
   113	such an improvement is identified, open a GitHub issue or pull request that
   114	describes the proposed change.  If the investigation also produces a paper-gap
   115	note, link the issue or pull request from that note: the note records the
   116	mathematical justification, and the issue or pull request drives the
   117	implementation.
   118	
   119	\section{When to Write a Note}
   120	
   121	A note should be written once the source argument and the formal proof no longer
   122	match as mathematical arguments.  This includes, for instance, a numerical
   123	estimate whose constant does not follow from the cited lemma, a displayed
   124	conclusion which uses an unstated hypothesis, or a step in which two objects are
   125	identified although they must remain distinct.  In analytic, algebraic,
   126	probabilistic, or quantum arguments, such distinctions may concern the domain of
   127	a map, the placement of a tensor factor, the type of an outcome, the distinction
   128	between a structure and a substructure, or the scalar carried by an approximation
   129	relation.
   130	
   131	A note is required when an audit finds that a Lean declaration associated with a
   132	source-labelled statement has acquired an extra non-source hypothesis, such as
   133	bridge, residual, repair, producer, or obligation-structure data.  Such a
   134	declaration is temporary proof debt, not a replacement for the source theorem,
   135	and should not be introduced merely to avoid a \verb|sorry|.  The note must say
   136	plainly that the Lean result is conditional, identify the source-faithful theorem
   137	form that remains to be proved, and give the intended obligation discharger or
   138	removal plan.  The blueprint should not mark the source-labelled statement with
   139	\verb|\leanok| by pointing to this conditional helper.
   140	
   141	Changing a Lean theorem away from the statement in
   142	\path{references/ldt-paper/} is strongly discouraged.  A paper-gap note should
   143	not make such a change look routine: it should explain the mathematical
   144	necessity, or else classify the change as proof debt to be removed.
   145	
   146	When an existing conditional helper is audited, the first task is to extract any
   147	argument it already contains into source-faithful lemmas.  If the remaining
   148	bridge hypothesis cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the formal
   149	development should restore the source theorem statement and record the missing
   150	proof obligation explicitly, rather than retaining the strengthened statement as
   151	though it were the paper theorem.
   152	
   153	This requirement is not meant to classify every explicit Lean side condition as
   154	a discrepancy.  Positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances,
   155	and denominator nonvanishing hypotheses may be faithful encodings of the domain
   156	in which the paper's theorem is stated.  The note should distinguish such
   157	boundary hypotheses from hypotheses that supply an unproved step of the paper
   158	argument.
   159	
   160	A note is also appropriate when the proof becomes formal only after changing an
   161	intermediate scalar, weakening a conclusion, strengthening a hypothesis, or
   162	inserting an additional lemma which is not simply an expansion of the cited
   163	argument.  These are mathematical changes, even when they are harmless for the
   164	final theorem.  It is likewise appropriate when an available formal-library
   165	theorem proves the needed result under a somewhat different formulation from the
   166	cited source.  In that case the note should be deliberately pedagogical.  It
   167	should explain, in ordinary mathematical language, what the replacement result
   168	says, how it is specialized, which hypotheses are new or differently packaged,
   169	and why the resulting statement is a legitimate substitute for the step in the
   170	cited argument.  If the issue remains open after reasonable attempts, the note
   171	should say what has been checked and what remains unknown.
   172	
   173	\section{Counterexamples}
   174	
   175	If the cited assertion appears to be false, the note should not stop at saying
   176	that the proof cannot be formalized.  It should give the counterexample, or the
   177	smallest relevant part of it, in ordinary mathematical notation.  The example
   178	should be accompanied by enough verification that the reader can see both sides:
   179	the hypotheses of the cited assertion hold, and its conclusion fails.
   180	
   181	When feasible, the counterexample should also be formalized in \Lean{}.  This is
   182	especially valuable when the example is finite, algebraic, computational, or
   183	otherwise small enough that the failure can be checked without reproducing the
   184	whole surrounding theory.  The note should then state the mathematical content
   185	of the checked counterexample and identify the corresponding Lean declaration in
   186	a footnote.  The Lean file is not a substitute for the prose: the prose should
   187	still explain why the example refutes the cited assertion.
   188	
   189	\section{Revision of a Note}
   190	
   191	A paper-gap note may be provisional.  It may begin as soon as the mathematical
   192	obstruction has been isolated well enough to state the question, and it may be
   193	revised as the calculation, the blueprint, or the corresponding \Lean{}
   194	declarations become clearer.  The first version need not know the final
   195	classification, but it should say plainly which mathematical point is known and
   196	which point remains unsettled.
   197	
   198	Later revisions should not make the note into a chronological log.  They should
   199	rewrite the document so that it remains a coherent account of the present
   200	mathematical understanding.  If the verdict changes, the conclusion should state
   201	the current verdict; the linked issue or pull request can preserve the earlier
   202	discussion.
   203

   211	serve the exposition rather than govern it: the main text should be organized

   218	be done briefly.  Only after the notation is in place should the note state the
   219	assertion in the cited source, using a bibliographic citation such as
   220	\verb|\cite[Section~...]{...}| when the section or chapter is known.

  1929	\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for the consistency conclusions in directly indexed coordinates]
  1930		\label{lem:direct-ld-consistency-coordinates}

  1937		three consistency implications obtained from the projective polynomial
  1938		measurements of Theorem~\ref{thm:main-formal} after changing to the
  1939		directly indexed coordinates. In that presentation the sampled coordinate

  1947			      directly indexed game, fix

  1951			      polynomials of individual degree at most $d$, consistency with
  1952			      error $\delta$ between the coordinate-$r$ LDT point family of
  1953			      Alice and the evaluation family of $G^{\mathrm B}$ implies

  1955			      off-diagonal defect, evaluated on $\psi$ and averaged uniformly

  1957			\item let $S=(\psi,A,B)$ be a projective strategy for the
  1958			      directly indexed game, fix
  1959			      $r\in\operatorname{Fin}(k)=\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$, and let
  1960			      $G^{\mathrm A}$ be a projective measurement on
  1961			      $\hilb_{\mathrm A}$ indexed by the same single polynomials,

  1990		\label{lem:direct-ld-residue-compression}

  1992		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldStrategyToDirect_polynomialPoint_compression}
  1993		\leanok

  1996		compression identities between the classical low individual degree game
  1997		and its directly indexed presentation.
  1998	
  1999		Let $(\psi, A, B)$ be a strategy for the classical game with parameters
  2000		$(q,m,d,k)$, and extend it to the directly indexed game by adjoining to
  2001		each player a register of dimension $q/m$, the common size of the
  2002		classes of the index function $\chi$ of
  2003		Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution}; the two copies of that
  2004		register are perfectly correlated in the extended state. For a

  2006		$\hilb_{\mathrm B}\ot\C^{q/m}$, let $\bar G^{\mathrm B}$ be the

     3	/-!
     4	# Matrix-valued measurements for the MIP*=RE project
     5	
     6	This file provides the matrix-valued measurement layer used by the LDT formalization.
     7	
     8	## Main definitions
     9	
    10	* `Submeasurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to at most the identity.
    11	* `Measurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to exactly the identity.
    12	* `Submeasurement.postprocess` — data-processed submeasurements via answer relabeling.
    13	* `Measurement.postprocess` — the paper's postprocessing proposition for complete POVMs.
    14	* `inconsistency` — the off-diagonal mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`.
    15	* `diagOverlap` — the diagonal mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`.
    16	
    17	## References
    18	
    19	This file builds the project's finite-dimensional measurement layer on top of
    20	the normalized-trace and positive-operator facts in `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix`
    21	for the quantum formalization in `references/ldt-paper/`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder

    26	namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	/-! ## Submeasurements and measurements -/
    29	
    30	/--
    31	A submeasurement on a finite answer type `α` is a family of PSD matrices
    32	`M : α → Op d` with `∑ a, M a ≤ 1`.
    33	-/
    34	structure Submeasurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
    35	  /-- The effect operators. -/
    36	  effect : α → Op d
    37	  /-- Each effect is positive semidefinite. -/
    38	  pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a
    39	  /-- The effects sum to at most the identity. -/
    40	  sum_le_one : ∑ a, effect a ≤ 1
    41	
    42	/--
    43	A measurement is a submeasurement whose effects sum exactly to the identity.
    44	-/
    45	structure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    46	    extends Submeasurement α d where
    47	  /-- The effects sum to the identity. -/
    48	  sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1
    49	
    50	/-! ## Totals and postprocessing -/
    51	
    52	namespace Submeasurement
    53	
    54	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    55	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    56	
    57	/-! ### Totals and postprocessing -/
    58	
    59	/-- The total operator `∑ a, M_a`. -/
    60	noncomputable def total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d :=
    61	  ∑ a, M.effect a
    62	
    63	/--
    64	Data processing: relabel the answer set by `f : α → β`, summing the effects over
    65	fibers.
    66	-/
    67	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    68	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d where
    69	  effect b := ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    70	  pos b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
    71	  sum_le_one := by
    72	    calc
    73	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    74	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
    75	      _ ≤ 1 := M.sum_le_one
    76	
    77	/-- Restatement of `sum_le_one` in terms of the named total operator. -/
    78	theorem total_le_one (M : Submeasurement α d) :
    79	    M.total ≤ 1 := by
    80	  simpa [total] using M.sum_le_one
    81	
    82	/-- Postprocessing preserves the sum of all effects. -/
    83	theorem postprocess_sum_eq [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    84	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    85	    ∑ a, M.effect a = ∑ b, (M.postprocess f).effect b :=
    86	  (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect).symm
    87	
    88	/-- Postprocessing preserves the named total operator. -/
    89	theorem postprocess_total [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    90	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    91	    (M.postprocess f).total = M.total := by
    92	  simpa [total] using (M.postprocess_sum_eq f).symm
    93	
    94	end Submeasurement

   105	the inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper
   106	sites that are explicitly POVMs rather than relaxed sub-POVMs.
   107	-/
   108	def ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)
   109	    (sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1) : Measurement α d where
   110	  effect := effect
   111	  pos := pos
   112	  sum_le_one := le_of_eq sum_eq_one
   113	  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one
   114	
   115	/-- The named total of a complete measurement is the identity. -/
   116	theorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :
   117	    M.total = 1 :=
   118	  M.sum_eq_one
   119	
   120	/--
   121	Postprocess a complete measurement by relabeling outcomes.
   122	
   123	This formalizes `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex:169--180`: regrouping
   124	the effects along the fibers of `f` preserves the total operator, so a POVM
   125	remains a POVM after postprocessing.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   128	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) : Measurement β d where
   129	  toSubmeasurement := M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f
   130	  sum_eq_one := by
   131	    calc
   132	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
   133	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
   134	      _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one
   135	
   136	@[simp] theorem postprocess_effect [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   137	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
   138	    (M.postprocess f).effect b =
   139	      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a :=
   140	  rfl
   141	
   142	@[simp] theorem postprocess_to_submeasurement [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   143	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) :
   144	    (M.postprocess f).toSubmeasurement = M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f :=
   145	  rfl
   146	
   147	/-- A complete measurement is determined by its effects. -/
   148	theorem ext {M N : Measurement α d} (h : ∀ a, M.effect a = N.effect a) :
   149	    M = N := by
   150	  cases M with
   151	  | mk M hM =>
   152	      cases N with
   153	      | mk N hN =>
   154	          cases M with
   155	          | mk effectM posM leM =>
   156	              cases N with
   157	              | mk effectN posN leN =>
   158	                  simp only at h
   159	                  have heffect : effectM = effectN := funext h
   160	                  subst effectN
   161	                  rfl
   162	
   163	/-- Relabeling along `f` and then along `g` is relabeling along `g ∘ f`: the
   164	fiber of `g ∘ f` over `c` is the disjoint union of the fibers of `f` over the
   165	fiber of `g` over `c`, and regrouping a finite sum of effects along it does not
   166	change the sum. -/
   167	theorem postprocess_comp {γ : Type*} [Fintype γ]
   168	    [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
   169	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (g : β → γ) :
   170	    (M.postprocess f).postprocess g = M.postprocess (fun a => g (f a)) := by
   171	  classical
   172	  apply ext
   173	  intro c
   174	  calc
   175	    ((M.postprocess f).postprocess g).effect c =
   176	        ∑ b : β, if g b = c then
   177	          ∑ a : α, if f a = b then M.effect a else 0
   178	        else 0 := by
   179	          change (∑ b ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun b : β => g b = c),
   180	            ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a : α => f a = b), M.effect a) = _
   181	          rw [Finset.sum_filter]
   182	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   183	          intro b _
   184	          by_cases hgb : g b = c
   185	          · simp only [hgb, if_true]
   186	            rw [Finset.sum_filter]
   187	          · simp [hgb]
   188	    _ = ∑ b : β, ∑ a : α,
   189	        if g b = c ∧ f a = b then M.effect a else 0 := by
   190	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   191	          intro b _
   192	          by_cases hgc : g b = c <;> simp [hgc]
   193	    _ = ∑ a : α, ∑ b : β,
   194	        if g b = c ∧ f a = b then M.effect a else 0 := by
   195	          rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   196	    _ = ∑ a : α,
   197	        if g (f a) = c then M.effect a else 0 := by
   198	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   199	          intro a _
   200	          by_cases hgc : g (f a) = c
   201	          · rw [Finset.sum_eq_single (f a)]
   202	            · simp [hgc]
   203	            · intro b _ hba
   204	              by_cases hfa : f a = b
   205	              · exact (hba hfa.symm).elim
   206	              · simp [hfa]
   207	            · simp
   208	          · have hzero :
   209	                (∑ b : β,
   210	                  if g b = c ∧ f a = b then M.effect a else 0) = 0 := by
   211	              apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
   212	              intro b _
   213	              by_cases hfa : f a = b
   214	              · subst b
   215	                simp [hgc]
   216	              · simp [hfa]
   217	            simp [hgc, hzero]
   218	    _ = (M.postprocess (fun a => g (f a))).effect c := by
   219	          change _ = ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter
   220	            (fun a : α => g (f a) = c), M.effect a
   221	          rw [Finset.sum_filter]
   222	
   223	end Measurement
   224	
   225	/-! ## Overlap definitions -/
   226	
   227	section Overlap
   228	
   229	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   230	variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   231	
   232	/-- The off-diagonal overlap mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`. -/
   233	noncomputable def inconsistency (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   234	  ∑ a, ∑ b ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun b => b ≠ a), normalizedTrace (M a * N b)
   235	
   236	/-- The diagonal overlap mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`. -/
   237	noncomputable def diagOverlap (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   238	  ∑ a, normalizedTrace (M a * N a)
   239	
   240	end Overlap
   241	
   242	end MIPStarRE.Quantum

     7

    18	/-- Evaluate a polynomial-valued submeasurement at a point. -/
    19	noncomputable def evaluateAt {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    20	    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q] (u : Point params)
    21	    (G : SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι) : SubMeas (Fq params) ι :=
    22	  postprocess G (fun g => g u)
    23	
    24	/-- Evaluation after adjoining an unused coordinate agrees with evaluation before
    25	adjoining that coordinate. -/
    26	@[simp] theorem evaluateAt_postprocess_appendAtHeight_appendPoint
    27	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    28	    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    29	    (G : SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι)
    30	    (x : Fq params) (u : Point params) (y : Fq params) :
    31	    evaluateAt params.next (appendPoint params u y)
    32	        (postprocess G (fun g => Polynomial.appendAtHeight params g x)) =
    33	      evaluateAt params u G := by
    34	  unfold evaluateAt
    35	  rw [SubMeas.postprocess_comp]
    36	  congr
    37	  funext g
    38	  exact Polynomial.appendAtHeight_apply_appendPoint params g x u y
    39	
    40	/-- View a global polynomial submeasurement as a point-indexed answer family. -/
    41	noncomputable def polynomialEvaluationFamily {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    42	    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    43	    (G : SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι) :
    44	    IdxSubMeas (Point params) (Fq params) ι :=
    45	  fun u => evaluateAt params u G
    46	
    47	/-- View a global polynomial measurement as a point-indexed answer measurement family.
    48	
    49	The submeasurement-valued `polynomialEvaluationFamily` is the form used by most
    50	consistency statements.  The heterogeneous triangle step in the final theorem
    51	uses complete measurements, so this version keeps the same postprocessing while
    52	retaining the total-mass proof. -/
    53	noncomputable def polynomialEvaluationMeasurementFamily
    54	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    55	    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    56	    (G : Measurement (Polynomial params) ι) :
    57	    IdxMeas (Point params) (Fq params) ι :=
    58	  fun u =>
    59	    { toSubMeas := evaluateAt params u G.toSubMeas
    60	      total_eq_one := G.total_eq_one }
    61	
    62	namespace Test
    63	
    64	/-- Namespace-compatible form of `polynomialEvaluationMeasurementFamily`.
    65	
    66	This name is used by the two-space final-theorem route, where the surrounding
    67	theorems live in the `Test` namespace. -/

    73	  MIPStarRE.LDT.polynomialEvaluationMeasurementFamily params G

    77	/-- Evaluate an indexed slice family at a point `(u, x)` in `F_q^{m+1}`. -/
    78	noncomputable def evaluateFiberFamilyAtNextPoint {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    79	    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    80	    (G : IdxSubMeas (Fq params) (Polynomial params) ι) :
    81	    IdxSubMeas (Point params.next) (Fq params) ι :=

    83	
    84	/-- Questionwise matching mass `∑_a ⟨ψ, A_a B_a ψ⟩`, summed over outcomes. -/
    85	noncomputable def qMatchMass {Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    86	    [Fintype Outcome]
    87	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (A B : SubMeas Outcome ι) : Error :=
    88	  ∑ a, ev ψ (A.outcome a * B.outcome a)
    89	
    90	/-- Questionwise off-diagonal mass surrogate for consistency. -/
    91	noncomputable def qConsDefect {Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    92	    [Fintype Outcome]
    93	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (A B : SubMeas Outcome ι) : Error :=
    94	  let totalOverlap := ev ψ (A.total * B.total)
    95	  max 0 (totalOverlap - qMatchMass ψ A B)
    96	
    97	/-- Questionwise squared-distance defect. -/
    98	noncomputable def qSDDCore {Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    99	    [Fintype Outcome]
   100	    (ψ : QuantumState ι)
   101	    (A B : Outcome → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) : Error :=
   102	  ∑ a, ev ψ ((A a - B a)ᴴ * (A a - B a))
   103	
   104	/-- Questionwise squared-distance defect. -/
   105	noncomputable def qSDD {Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   106	    [Fintype Outcome]
   107	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (A B : SubMeas Outcome ι) : Error :=
   108	  qSDDCore ψ A.outcome B.outcome
   109	
   110	/-- State-dependent distance for raw operator families.
   111	Matches the paper's `≈_δ` for arbitrary matrix families.
   112	This keeps the raw-family API separate while sharing the same core formula as
   113	`qSDD`. -/
   114	noncomputable def qSDDOp {Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   115	    [Fintype Outcome]
   116	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (A B : OpFamily Outcome ι) : Error :=
   117	  qSDDCore ψ A.outcome B.outcome
   118	
   119	/-- Questionwise strong self-consistency defect. -/
   120	noncomputable def qSSCDefect {Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   121	    [Fintype Outcome]
   122	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (A : SubMeas Outcome ι) : Error :=
   123	  let totalMass := ev ψ A.total
   124	  let diagonalMass := ∑ a, ev ψ (A.outcome a * A.outcome a)
   125	  max 0 (totalMass - diagonalMass)
   126	
   127	/-- Averaged off-diagonal mass for consistency statements. -/
   128	noncomputable def consError {Question Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   129	    [Fintype Outcome]
   130	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (𝒟 : Distribution Question)
   131	    (A B : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ι) : Error :=
   132	  avgOver 𝒟 (fun q => qConsDefect ψ (A q) (B q))
   133	
   134	/-- Averaged squared distance for `≈_δ`. -/
   135	noncomputable def sddError {Question Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   136	    [Fintype Outcome]
   137	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (𝒟 : Distribution Question)
   138	    (A B : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ι) : Error :=
   139	  avgOver 𝒟 (fun q => qSDD ψ (A q) (B q))
   140	
   141	/-- Averaged squared distance for raw operator families. -/
   142	noncomputable def sddErrorOp {Question Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   143	    [Fintype Outcome]
   144	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (𝒟 : Distribution Question)
   145	    (A B : IdxOpFamily Question Outcome ι) : Error :=
   146	  avgOver 𝒟 (fun q => qSDDOp ψ (A q) (B q))
   147	
   148	/-- Averaged defect in strong self-consistency. -/
   149	noncomputable def sscError {Question Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   150	    [Fintype Outcome]
   151	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (𝒟 : Distribution Question)
   152	    (A : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ι) : Error :=
   153	  avgOver 𝒟 (fun q => qSSCDefect ψ (A q))
   154	
   155	/-- Total mass of a submeasurement on state `ψ`, computed from the concrete total operator. -/
   156	noncomputable def subMeasMass {Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   157	    [Fintype Outcome] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   158	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (A : SubMeas Outcome ι) : Error :=
   159	  ev ψ A.total
   160	
   161	/-- Averaged total mass of an indexed submeasurement. -/
   162	noncomputable def idxSubMeasMass {Question Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   163	    [Fintype Outcome] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   164	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (𝒟 : Distribution Question)
   165	    (A : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ι) : Error :=
   166	  avgOver 𝒟 (fun q => subMeasMass ψ (A q))
   167	
   168	/-- Defect in domination by an operator witness, measured at the expectation-value level. -/
   169	noncomputable def bndError {Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   170	    [Fintype Outcome] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   171	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (A : SubMeas Outcome ι)
   172	    (Z : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) : Error :=
   173	  max 0 (subMeasMass ψ A - ev ψ Z)
   174	
   175	/-- Bipartite matching mass `∑_a ⟨ψ, (A_a ⊗ B_a) ψ⟩`, with `A` on the left
   176	register and `B` on the right register of a tensor-product state. -/
   177	noncomputable def qBipartiteMatchMass {Outcome : Type*}
   178	    {ιA ιB : Type*} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   179	    [Fintype Outcome]
   180	    (ψ : QuantumState (ιA × ιB))
   181	    (A : SubMeas Outcome ιA) (B : SubMeas Outcome ιB) : Error :=
   182	  ∑ a, ev ψ (opTensor (A.outcome a) (B.outcome a))
   183	
   184	/-- Bipartite questionwise consistency defect.
   185	
   186	In the paper (Definition 4.8), the consistency of `A` on `H_A` and `B` on
   187	`H_B` for a shared state `|ψ⟩ ∈ H_A ⊗ H_B` is:
   188	  `E_x ∑_{a≠b} ⟨ψ| A^x_a ⊗ B^x_b |ψ⟩ ≤ δ`
   189	which equals
   190	  `max 0 (⟨ψ| A_total ⊗ B_total |ψ⟩ − ∑_a ⟨ψ| A_a ⊗ B_a |ψ⟩)`. -/
   191	noncomputable def qBipartiteConsDefect {Outcome : Type*}
   192	    {ιA ιB : Type*} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   193	    [Fintype Outcome]
   194	    (ψ : QuantumState (ιA × ιB))
   195	    (A : SubMeas Outcome ιA) (B : SubMeas Outcome ιB) : Error :=
   196	  let totalOverlap := ev ψ (opTensor A.total B.total)
   197	  max 0 (totalOverlap - qBipartiteMatchMass ψ A B)
   198	
   199	/-- Averaged bipartite off-diagonal mass for consistency statements. -/
   200	noncomputable def bipartiteConsError {Question Outcome : Type*}
   201	    {ιA ιB : Type*} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   202	    [Fintype Outcome]
   203	    (ψ : QuantumState (ιA × ιB)) (𝒟 : Distribution Question)
   204	    (A : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ιA)
   205	    (B : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ιB) : Error :=
   206	  avgOver 𝒟 (fun q => qBipartiteConsDefect ψ (A q) (B q))
   207	
   208	/-- **Bridge lemma**: the bipartite consistency defect equals the same-space
   209	`qConsDefect` applied to the left/right-placed submeasurements. -/
   210	theorem qBipartiteConsDefect_eq_qConsDefect_placed {Outcome : Type*}
   211	    {ιA ιB : Type*} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   212	    [Fintype Outcome]
   213	    (ψ : QuantumState (ιA × ιB))
   214	    (A : SubMeas Outcome ιA) (B : SubMeas Outcome ιB) :
   215	    qBipartiteConsDefect ψ A B =
   216	      qConsDefect ψ (leftPlacedSubMeas A) (rightPlacedSubMeas B) := by
   217	  simp only [qBipartiteConsDefect, qConsDefect, qBipartiteMatchMass, qMatchMass,
   218	    leftPlacedSubMeas_total, rightPlacedSubMeas_total,
   219	    leftPlacedSubMeas_outcome, rightPlacedSubMeas_outcome,
   220	    leftTensor_mul_rightTensor_eq_opTensor]
   221	
   222	/-- **Bridge lemma**: averaged bipartite consistency equals the same-space
   223	`consError` applied to the left/right-placed families. -/
   224	theorem bipartiteConsError_eq_consError_placed {Question Outcome : Type*}
   225	    {ιA ιB : Type*} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   226	    [Fintype Outcome]
   227	    (ψ : QuantumState (ιA × ιB)) (𝒟 : Distribution Question)
   228	    (A : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ιA)
   229	    (B : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ιB) :
   230	    bipartiteConsError ψ 𝒟 A B =
   231	      consError ψ 𝒟
   232	        (fun q => leftPlacedSubMeas (A q))
   233	        (fun q => rightPlacedSubMeas (B q)) := by
   234	  unfold bipartiteConsError consError
   235	  congr 1; funext q
   236	  exact qBipartiteConsDefect_eq_qConsDefect_placed ψ (A q) (B q)
   237	
   238	/-- Consistency relation (bipartite, paper Definition 4.8).
   239	
   240	The state `ψ` lives on `H_A ⊗ H_B`, Alice's submeasurement `A` acts on
   241	`H_A`, and Bob's submeasurement `B` acts on `H_B`. The relation encodes
   242	  `E_{x ∼ D} ∑_{a≠b} ⟨ψ| A^x_a ⊗ B^x_b |ψ⟩ ≤ δ`. -/
   243	structure ConsRel {Question Outcome : Type*}
   244	    {ιA ιB : Type*} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   245	    [Fintype Outcome]
   246	    (ψ : QuantumState (ιA × ιB)) (𝒟 : Distribution Question)
   247	    (A : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ιA)
   248	    (B : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ιB)
   249	    (δ : Error) : Prop where
   250	  offDiagonalBound : bipartiteConsError ψ 𝒟 A B ≤ δ
   251	
   252	/-- State-dependent distance relation. -/
   253	structure SDDRel {Question Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   254	    [Fintype Outcome]
   255	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (𝒟 : Distribution Question)
   256	    (A B : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ι) (δ : Error) : Prop where
   257	  squaredDistanceBound : sddError ψ 𝒟 A B ≤ δ
   258	
   259	/-- State-dependent distance relation for raw operator families. -/
   260	structure SDDOpRel {Question Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   261	    [Fintype Outcome]
   262	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (𝒟 : Distribution Question)
   263	    (A B : IdxOpFamily Question Outcome ι) (δ : Error) : Prop where
   264	  squaredDistanceBound : sddErrorOp ψ 𝒟 A B ≤ δ
   265	
   266	/-- Strong self-consistency relation. -/
   267	structure SSCRel {Question Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   268	    [Fintype Outcome]
   269	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (𝒟 : Distribution Question)
   270	    (A : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ι) (δ : Error) : Prop where
   271	  diagonalOverlapBound : sscError ψ 𝒟 A ≤ δ
   272	
   273	/-- Bipartite questionwise strong self-consistency defect.
   274	This is the paper's SSC condition (Definition 4.3/4.4):
   275	  `max 0 (∑ₐ ev ψ (Aₐ ⊗ I) − ∑ₐ ev ψ (Aₐ ⊗ Aₐ))`.
   276	It measures the gap between the total mass on one register and the
   277	diagonal cross-register overlap. -/
   278	noncomputable def qBipartiteSSCDefect
   279	    {Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   280	    [Fintype Outcome]

    13	/-- A paper-local submeasurement with outcomes in `α` and Hilbert space index `ι`.
    14	
    15	There is intentionally no global `Inhabited` instance: the zero family satisfies
    16	these raw axioms, but using it as an ambient default would silently turn later
    17	arguments into vacuous submeasurement statements. -/
    18	structure SubMeas (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] where
    19	  outcome : α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι := fun _ => 0
    20	  total : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι := 0
    21	  outcome_pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ outcome a
    22	  sum_eq_total : ∑ a, outcome a = total
    23	  total_le_one : total ≤ 1

    25	/-- A paper-local measurement: a POVM whose PSD effects sum to the identity. -/
    26	structure Measurement (α : Type*) (ι : Type*) [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    27	    extends SubMeas α ι where
    28	  total_eq_one : total = 1

    30	set_option linter.unusedFintypeInType false in

    32	/-- For a trivial distinguished-outcome measurement, every outcome operator is
    33	positive semidefinite: `0 ≤ if a = a₀ then 1 else 0`. -/
    34	private theorem Measurement.trivialDistinguishedOutcome_outcome_pos
    35	    {α : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (a₀ a : α) :
    36	    (0 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) ≤ if a = a₀ then 1 else 0 := by
    37	  by_cases h : a = a₀ <;> simp [h]
    38	
    39	open scoped Classical in
    40	/-- ⚠️ DEGENERATE — Construct a trivial measurement where only the distinguished
    41	outcome `a₀` is the identity and all other outcomes are zero.
    42	
    43	This is a valid POVM but highly degenerate: it is only used in vacuous
    44	fallback branches of the proof where the error bound is ≥ 1 (see
    45	`Test/MainTheorem.lean:mainFormal_trivial_witness`).
    46	
    47	Call this function explicitly with a chosen outcome.  There is intentionally no
    48	ambient `Inhabited (Measurement α ι)` instance: choosing a hidden
    49	`default : α` would make degenerate witnesses available to paper-facing
    50	existential statements without displaying the selected outcome. -/
    51	noncomputable def Measurement.trivialDistinguishedOutcome
    52	    {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
    53	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    54	    (a₀ : α) : Measurement α ι where
    55	  toSubMeas := {
    56	    outcome := fun a => if a = a₀ then 1 else 0
    57	    total := 1
    58	    outcome_pos := fun a => Measurement.trivialDistinguishedOutcome_outcome_pos a₀ a
    59	    sum_eq_total :=
    60	      (Finset.sum_ite_eq' Finset.univ a₀ fun _ => 1).trans (if_pos (Finset.mem_univ a₀))

    62	  }

   105	/-- Two submeasurements are equal when they have the same outcome operators and

   107	@[ext] theorem SubMeas.ext {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   108	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   109	    {A B : SubMeas α ι}
   110	    (houtcome : ∀ a : α, A.outcome a = B.outcome a)
   111	    (htotal : A.total = B.total) :
   112	    A = B := by
   113	  cases A with
   114	  | mk outcomeA totalA posA sumA leA =>
   115	      cases B with
   116	      | mk outcomeB totalB posB sumB leB =>
   117	          have houtcome' : outcomeA = outcomeB := by
   118	            funext a
   119	            exact houtcome a
   120	          cases houtcome'
   121	          cases htotal
   122	          cases Subsingleton.elim posB posA
   123	          cases Subsingleton.elim sumB sumA
   124	          cases Subsingleton.elim leB leA
   125	          rfl

   127	/-- Two measurements are equal when they have the same outcome operators. -/
   128	@[ext] theorem Measurement.ext {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}

   130	    {A B : Measurement α ι}

   132	    A = B := by
   133	  cases A with
   134	  | mk AtoSubMeas AtotalEqOne =>
   135	      cases B with
   136	      | mk BtoSubMeas BtotalEqOne =>
   137	          have hsub : AtoSubMeas = BtoSubMeas := by
   138	            apply SubMeas.ext

   140	              simpa using houtcome a
   141	            · calc
   142	                AtoSubMeas.total = 1 := AtotalEqOne

   145	          cases Subsingleton.elim BtotalEqOne AtotalEqOne
   146	          rfl

   150	@[ext] theorem ProjMeas.ext {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   151	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   152	    {A B : ProjMeas α ι}
   153	    (houtcome : ∀ a : α, A.outcome a = B.outcome a) :
   154	    A = B := by

   173	  total := A
   174	  outcome_pos := fun _ => hA_pos

   205	theorem Measurement.outcome_le_one {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}

   211	/-- Postprocessing is functorial: postprocessing by `f` and then by `g`
   212	agrees with a single postprocessing by the composite `g ∘ f`. -/
   213	@[simp] theorem postprocess_comp {α β γ : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   214	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype γ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   215	    (A : SubMeas α ι) (f : α → β) (g : β → γ) :
   216	    postprocess (postprocess A f) g = postprocess A (fun a => g (f a)) := by

   218	  refine SubMeas.ext ?_ rfl
   219	  intro c
   220	  calc
   221	    (postprocess (postprocess A f) g).outcome c
   222	        = ∑ b : β,
   223	            if g b = c then

   225	            else 0 := by
   226	              simp [postprocess, Finset.sum_filter]
   227	    _ = ∑ b : β, ∑ a : α,
   228	          if g b = c ∧ f a = b then

    19	/-- The off-diagonal defect in `def:consistency`, blueprint
    20	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    21	noncomputable def consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
    22	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    23	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    24	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    25	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    26	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    27	    ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
    28	      if a = b then 0 else
    29	        (inner ℂ ψ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm
    30	          ((A x a * B x b).mulVec ψ))).re)

    32	/-- A uniform consistency defect is invariant under a bijective relabeling of
    33	its question type. -/
    34	theorem consistencyDefect_uniform_question_equiv
    35	    {X Y Outcome iota : Type*}
    36	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Nonempty X]
    37	    [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y] [Nonempty Y]
    38	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
    39	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    40	    (e : X ≃ Y) (A B : Y → Outcome → Op iota)
    41	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
    42	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
    43	        (fun x a => A (e x) a) (fun x a => B (e x) a) psi =
    44	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Y) A B psi := by
    45	  unfold consistencyDefect
    46	  simpa using avgOver_uniform_equiv e (fun x =>
    47	    ∑ a : Outcome, ∑ b : Outcome,
    48	      if a = b then 0 else
    49	        (inner ℂ psi ((EuclideanSpace.equiv iota ℂ).symm
    50	          (((A (e x) a) * (B (e x) b)).mulVec psi))).re)
    51	
    52	/-- A consistency defect is invariant under a bijective relabeling of both
    53	outcome families. -/
    54	theorem consistencyDefect_outcome_equiv
    55	    {X Alpha Beta iota : Type*}
    56	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X]
    57	    [Fintype Alpha] [DecidableEq Alpha]
    58	    [Fintype Beta] [DecidableEq Beta]
    59	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    60	    (mu : Distribution X) (e : Beta ≃ Alpha)
    61	    (A B : X → Alpha → Op iota) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
    62	    consistencyDefect mu
    63	        (fun x b => A x (e b)) (fun x b => B x (e b)) psi =
    64	      consistencyDefect mu A B psi := by
    65	  unfold consistencyDefect
    66	  apply avgOver_congr
    67	  intro x
    68	  let term : Alpha → Alpha → ℝ := fun a b =>

   759	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for Proposition 4.29: on a unit state and
   760	probability distribution, defect is one minus diagonal overlap. -/
   761	theorem consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_overlap {X α ι : Type*}

   763	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

   769	        stateQForm ψ ((A x).effect a * (B x).effect a)) := by

   217	/-- The positive cardinality of every seed-fiber residue type. -/
   218	theorem LdParams.seedFiberCard_pos (L : LdParams) : 0 < L.q / L.m := by
   219	  exact Nat.div_pos (Nat.le_of_dvd (by
   220	    obtain ⟨n, hn, hq⟩ := L.hq
   221	    rw [hq]
   222	    exact Nat.pow_pos (by decide)) L.hdvd) L.hm

   224	/-- Divisibility identifies the field cardinality with the product of the
   225	index cardinality and the common fiber cardinality. -/
   226	theorem LdParams.seedFiberProduct_eq (L : LdParams) :
   227	    L.q = L.m * (L.q / L.m) :=
   228	  (Nat.mul_div_cancel' L.hdvd).symm

   230	/-- Casting between equal finite cardinalities preserves the underlying
   231	natural-number representative. -/
   232	@[simp] private theorem equivCastFin_val {m n : ℕ} (h : m = n) (i : Fin m) :
   233	    (Equiv.cast (congrArg Fin h) i).val = i.val := by
   234	  subst n
   235	  rfl

   237	/-- A field seed is uniquely a coordinate index and a residue in its equal
   238	`chiIndex` fiber. -/
   239	noncomputable def seedFiberEquiv (L : LdParams) :
   240	    ScalarQ L ≃ Fin L.m × Fin (L.q / L.m) :=
   241	  (binaryRepresentation L.model).trans <|
   242	    (Equiv.cast <| congrArg Fin L.seedFiberProduct_eq).trans
   243	      finProdFinEquiv.symm
   244	
   245	@[simp] theorem seedFiberEquiv_fst (L : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ L) :
   246	    (seedFiberEquiv L s).1 = chiIndex L s := by
   247	  letI : NeZero L.m := ⟨Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one L.hm)⟩
   248	  have hquot : (binaryRepresentation L.model s).val / (L.q / L.m) < L.m := by
   249	    apply (Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul L.seedFiberCard_pos).mpr
   250	    rw [Nat.mul_div_cancel' L.hdvd]
   251	    exact (binaryRepresentation L.model s).isLt
   252	  simp only [seedFiberEquiv, Equiv.trans_apply]
   253	  apply Fin.ext
   254	  change
   255	    (Equiv.cast (congrArg Fin L.seedFiberProduct_eq)
   256	      (binaryRepresentation L.model s)).val / (L.q / L.m) =
   257	      (Fin.ofNat L.m ((binaryRepresentation L.model s).val / (L.q / L.m))).val

   259	  · exact (Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hquot).symm
   260	  · exact L.seedFiberProduct_eq

   263	noncomputable def seedOfIndexResidue (L : LdParams)

   273	    (i : Fin L.m) (r : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   274	    chiIndex L (seedOfIndexResidue L i r) = i := by

     4	/-!
     5	# Average lemmas for finite-support distributions
     6	
     7	This module contains the finite-sum and uniform-average lemmas for the project
     8	`Distribution` type.  The primitive distribution definitions, uniform
     9	distributions, and total variation distance live in
    10	`MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.Distribution`.
    11	
    12	## Main declarations
    13	
    14	The main results are the algebraic rules for `avgOver`, scalar and
    15	operator-valued forms of the module-valued finite-sum rules for uniform
    16	distributions, and the comparison between finite uniform averages and Mathlib
    17	uniform probability mass functions.
    18	
    19	## References
    20	
    21	These are formalization-internal finite probability lemmas for the low
    22	individual degree test development.

    29	/-! ### Averaging infrastructure
    30	
    31	Linearity proofs use `Distribution.weightedSumLinearMap`; order and support
    32	estimates use Mathlib's `Finset.sum` API. -/
    33	
    34	/-- Averaging the zero function gives zero. -/
    35	theorem avgOver_zero {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) :
    36	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun _ => 0) = 0 := by
    37	  simp [Distribution.avgOver_eq_weightedSumLinearMap]
    38	
    39	/-- Averaging preserves order when weights are nonneg. -/
    40	theorem avgOver_mono {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f g : α → Error)
    41	    (hfg : ∀ a, f a ≤ g a) :
    42	    avgOver 𝒟 f ≤ avgOver 𝒟 g := by
    43	  simp only [avgOver]
    44	  exact Finset.sum_le_sum fun a _ => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hfg a) (𝒟.nonnegative a)
    45	
    46	/-- Averaging a nonneg function with nonneg weights gives a nonneg result. -/
    47	theorem avgOver_nonneg {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f : α → Error)
    48	    (hf : ∀ a, 0 ≤ f a) :
    49	    0 ≤ avgOver 𝒟 f := by
    50	  simpa [avgOver_zero] using avgOver_mono 𝒟 (fun _ => 0) f hf
    51	
    52	/-- Averaging distributes over addition. -/
    53	theorem avgOver_add {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f g : α → Error) :
    54	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => f a + g a) =
    55	      avgOver 𝒟 f + avgOver 𝒟 g := by
    56	  change avgOver 𝒟 (f + g) = avgOver 𝒟 f + avgOver 𝒟 g
    57	  simpa [Distribution.avgOver_eq_weightedSumLinearMap] using
    58	    map_add (𝒟.weightedSumLinearMap Error) f g
    59	
    60	/-- Averaging distributes over subtraction. -/
    61	theorem avgOver_sub {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f g : α → Error) :
    62	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => f a - g a) =
    63	      avgOver 𝒟 f - avgOver 𝒟 g := by
    64	  change avgOver 𝒟 (f - g) = avgOver 𝒟 f - avgOver 𝒟 g
    65	  simpa [Distribution.avgOver_eq_weightedSumLinearMap] using
    66	    map_sub (𝒟.weightedSumLinearMap Error) f g
    67	
    68	/-- Averaging commutes with scalar multiplication. -/
    69	theorem avgOver_const_mul {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
    70	    (c : Error) (f : α → Error) :
    71	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => c * f a) =
    72	      c * avgOver 𝒟 f := by
    73	  change avgOver 𝒟 (c • f) = c • avgOver 𝒟 f
    74	  simp [Distribution.avgOver_eq_weightedSumLinearMap, smul_eq_mul]
    75	
    76	/-- Averaging commutes with scalar multiplication on the right. -/
    77	theorem avgOver_mul_const {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
    78	    (f : α → Error) (c : Error) :
    79	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => f a * c) = avgOver 𝒟 f * c := by
    80	  unfold avgOver
    81	  calc
    82	    ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a * (f a * c)
    83	      = ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, (𝒟.weight a * f a) * c := by
    84	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    85	          intro a _
    86	          ring
    87	    _ = (∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a * f a) * c := by
    88	          rw [Finset.sum_mul]

   111	theorem avgOver_comm {α β : Type*} (𝒟α : Distribution α) (𝒟β : Distribution β)

   113	    avgOver 𝒟α (fun a => avgOver 𝒟β (f a)) =

   116	  simp_rw [Finset.mul_sum]

   127	    avgOver 𝒟 f = avgOver 𝒟 g := by

    64	    [Fintype Outcome] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    65	    (MA MB : Measurement Outcome ι) : Measurement Outcome (Role × ι) where

    67	    { outcome := fun a => roleCond Role.A (MA.outcome a) + roleCond Role.B (MB.outcome a)

    69	      outcome_pos := fun a => add_nonneg

    71	        (roleCond_nonneg Role.B (MB.outcome_pos a))

    76	        (congrArg₂ (fun X Y => roleCond Role.A X + roleCond Role.B Y)
    77	          MA.sum_eq MB.sum_eq).trans roleCond_one_sum

    94	/-- For complete measurements, the bipartite consistency defect is the total
    95	expectation minus the matching mass. -/
    96	theorem qBipartiteConsDefect_of_measurements {Outcome : Type*} {ιA ιB : Type*}
    97	    [Fintype Outcome]
    98	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    99	    (ψ : QuantumState (ιA × ιB))
   100	    (A : Measurement Outcome ιA) (B : Measurement Outcome ιB) :
   101	    qBipartiteConsDefect ψ A.toSubMeas B.toSubMeas =
   102	      ev ψ (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)) -
   103	        qBipartiteMatchMass ψ A.toSubMeas B.toSubMeas := by
   104	  have hmatch_le :
   105	      qBipartiteMatchMass ψ A.toSubMeas B.toSubMeas ≤
   106	        ev ψ (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)) := by
   107	    calc
   108	      qBipartiteMatchMass ψ A.toSubMeas B.toSubMeas
   109	        = ∑ a : Outcome, ev ψ (opTensor (A.outcome a) (B.outcome a)) := by
   110	            rfl
   111	      _ ≤ ∑ a : Outcome, ev ψ (leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB) (A.outcome a)) := by
   112	            refine Finset.sum_le_sum ?_
   113	            intro a _
   114	            exact ev_mono ψ _ _ <|
   115	              opTensor_le_leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB)
   116	                (A.outcome_pos a) (Measurement.outcome_le_one B a)
   117	      _ = ev ψ (leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB) A.total) := by
   118	            rw [← ev_sum ψ (fun a : Outcome => leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB) (A.outcome a))]
   119	            rw [leftTensor_finset_sum (ι₂ := ιB) Finset.univ A.outcome, A.sum_eq_total]
   120	      _ = ev ψ (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)) := by
   121	            simp [A.total_eq_one, leftTensor]
   122	  unfold qBipartiteConsDefect
   123	  rw [show ev ψ (opTensor A.toSubMeas.total B.toSubMeas.total) =
   124	      ev ψ (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)) by
   125	    simp [A.total_eq_one, B.total_eq_one, opTensor]]
   126	  rw [max_eq_right (sub_nonneg.mpr hmatch_le)]

  1929	\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for the consistency conclusions in directly indexed coordinates]
  1930		\label{lem:direct-ld-consistency-coordinates}
  1931		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.directPointPolynomial_consistencyDefect_le}
  1932		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.directPolynomialPoint_consistencyDefect_le}

  1935		\uses{def:consistency, def:ld-game, thm:main-formal}
  1936		This is not a named statement of \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. It records the
  1937		three consistency implications obtained from the projective polynomial
  1938		measurements of Theorem~\ref{thm:main-formal} after changing to the
  1939		directly indexed coordinates. In that presentation the sampled coordinate
  1940		is carried by the question itself rather than by a residue class of
  1941		$\F_q$; see Remark~\ref{rem:qld-4-7-divisibility}.
  1942	
  1943		Fix directly indexed parameters $D=(q,m,d,k)$ and let $\delta\in\R$.
  1944		The following three implications hold:
  1945		\begin{enumerate}
  1946			\item let $S=(\psi,A,B)$ be a projective strategy for the
  1947			      directly indexed game, fix
  1948			      $r\in\operatorname{Fin}(k)=\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$, and let
  1949			      $G^{\mathrm B}$ be a projective measurement on
  1950			      $\hilb_{\mathrm B}$ indexed by single $m$-variate
  1951			      polynomials of individual degree at most $d$, consistency with
  1952			      error $\delta$ between the coordinate-$r$ LDT point family of
  1953			      Alice and the evaluation family of $G^{\mathrm B}$ implies
  1954			      that the corresponding directly indexed point/polynomial
  1955			      off-diagonal defect, evaluated on $\psi$ and averaged uniformly
  1956			      over $u\in\F_q^m$, is at most $\delta$;
  1957			\item let $S=(\psi,A,B)$ be a projective strategy for the
  1958			      directly indexed game, fix
  1959			      $r\in\operatorname{Fin}(k)=\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$, and let
  1960			      $G^{\mathrm A}$ be a projective measurement on
  1961			      $\hilb_{\mathrm A}$ indexed by the same single polynomials,
  1962			      consistency with error $\delta$ between its evaluation family
  1963			      and the coordinate-$r$ LDT point family of Bob implies the
  1964			      corresponding directly indexed polynomial/point defect bound
  1965			      $\delta$, again averaged uniformly over $u\in\F_q^m$;
  1966			\item let $S=(\psi,A,B)$ be an arbitrary strategy for the
  1967			      directly indexed game, with no projectivity assumption on $S$,
  1968			      and let $G^{\mathrm A}$ and $G^{\mathrm B}$ be projective
  1969			      measurements on the two players' spaces indexed by single
  1970			      polynomials. Consistency with error $\delta$ between these two

  1973			      polynomial/polynomial defect is at most $\delta$.
  1974		\end{enumerate}

  1976		third concerns no coordinate. All three use single-polynomial projective
  1977		measurements; they do not construct a joint measurement of a
  1978		$k$-tuple of polynomials.

  1989	\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for the compression of a correlated residue register]
  1990		\label{lem:direct-ld-residue-compression}
  1991		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldStrategyToDirect_pointPolynomial_compression}
  1992		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldStrategyToDirect_polynomialPoint_compression}
  1993		\leanok
  1994		\uses{def:consistency, def:ld-game, def:ld-question-distribution}
  1995		This is not a named statement of \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. It records two
  1996		compression identities between the classical low individual degree game
  1997		and its directly indexed presentation.
  1998	
  1999		Let $(\psi, A, B)$ be a strategy for the classical game with parameters
  2000		$(q,m,d,k)$, and extend it to the directly indexed game by adjoining to
  2001		each player a register of dimension $q/m$, the common size of the
  2002		classes of the index function $\chi$ of
  2003		Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution}; the two copies of that
  2004		register are perfectly correlated in the extended state. For a
  2005		polynomial-tuple POVM $G^{\mathrm B}$ on
  2006		$\hilb_{\mathrm B}\ot\C^{q/m}$, let $\bar G^{\mathrm B}$ be the
  2007		normalized average of its diagonal blocks over the residue register.
  2008		Then, over a uniformly random point $u\in\F_q^m$, the off-diagonal
  2009		defect between Alice's point measurement and the evaluation of
  2010		$G^{\mathrm B}$ on the extended strategy equals the defect between
  2011		Alice's original point measurement and the evaluation of
  2012		$\bar G^{\mathrm B}$ on $(\psi,A,B)$.
  2013	
  2014		Similarly, for every polynomial-tuple POVM $G^{\mathrm A}$ on
  2015		$\hilb_{\mathrm A}\ot\C^{q/m}$, compression gives equality between
  2016		the extended polynomial/point defect and the defect between the
  2017		evaluation of $\bar G^{\mathrm A}$ and Bob's original point
  2018		measurement. No projectivity hypothesis is imposed on the strategy or
  2019		on either polynomial-tuple POVM.
  2020	\end{lemma}
  2021	\begin{proof}
  2022		\leanok
  2023		The point measurement of the extended strategy is the block-diagonal
  2024		amplification of the original point measurement, while polynomial
  2025		evaluation commutes with averaging the diagonal blocks. The quadratic
  2026		form of the correlated state against each mixed pair of operators is
  2027		therefore the quadratic form of the original state against the
  2028		compressed pair, and summing the off-diagonal terms gives both identities.
  2029	\end{proof}

  2032		The preceding lemma does not compare defects in which both families are
  2033		polynomial measurements on the extended carriers. The extended state
  2034		pairs equal residues, whereas separate compression averages independently

diff --git a/MIPStarRE/Quantum/Measurement.lean b/MIPStarRE/Quantum/Measurement.lean

--- a/MIPStarRE/Quantum/Measurement.lean
+++ b/MIPStarRE/Quantum/Measurement.lean
@@ -146,2 +146,78 @@ noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
 
+/-- A complete measurement is determined by its effects. -/
+theorem ext {M N : Measurement α d} (h : ∀ a, M.effect a = N.effect a) :
+    M = N := by
+  cases M with
+  | mk M hM =>
+      cases N with
+      | mk N hN =>
+          cases M with
+          | mk effectM posM leM =>
+              cases N with
+              | mk effectN posN leN =>
+                  simp only at h
+                  have heffect : effectM = effectN := funext h
+                  subst effectN
+                  rfl
+
+/-- Relabeling along `f` and then along `g` is relabeling along `g ∘ f`: the
+fiber of `g ∘ f` over `c` is the disjoint union of the fibers of `f` over the
+fiber of `g` over `c`, and regrouping a finite sum of effects along it does not
+change the sum. -/
+theorem postprocess_comp {γ : Type*} [Fintype γ]
+    [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
+    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (g : β → γ) :
+    (M.postprocess f).postprocess g = M.postprocess (fun a => g (f a)) := by
+  classical
+  apply ext
+  intro c
+  calc
+    ((M.postprocess f).postprocess g).effect c =
+        ∑ b : β, if g b = c then
+          ∑ a : α, if f a = b then M.effect a else 0
+        else 0 := by
+          change (∑ b ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun b : β => g b = c),
+            ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a : α => f a = b), M.effect a) = _
+          rw [Finset.sum_filter]
+          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+          intro b _
+          by_cases hgb : g b = c
+          · simp only [hgb, if_true]
+            rw [Finset.sum_filter]
+          · simp [hgb]
+    _ = ∑ b : β, ∑ a : α,
+        if g b = c ∧ f a = b then M.effect a else 0 := by
+          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+          intro b _
+          by_cases hgc : g b = c <;> simp [hgc]
+    _ = ∑ a : α, ∑ b : β,
+        if g b = c ∧ f a = b then M.effect a else 0 := by
+          rw [Finset.sum_comm]
+    _ = ∑ a : α,
+        if g (f a) = c then M.effect a else 0 := by
+          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+          intro a _
+          by_cases hgc : g (f a) = c
+          · rw [Finset.sum_eq_single (f a)]
+            · simp [hgc]
+            · intro b _ hba
+              by_cases hfa : f a = b
+              · exact (hba hfa.symm).elim
+              · simp [hfa]
+            · simp
+          · have hzero :
+                (∑ b : β,
+                  if g b = c ∧ f a = b then M.effect a else 0) = 0 := by
+              apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
+              intro b _
+              by_cases hfa : f a = b
+              · subst b
+                simp [hgc]
+              · simp [hfa]
+            simp [hgc, hzero]
+    _ = (M.postprocess (fun a => g (f a))).effect c := by
+          change _ = ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter
+            (fun a : α => g (f a) = c), M.effect a
+          rw [Finset.sum_filter]
+

     6	The classical and Pauli question distributions use affine lines in a finite

    14	the formalization support nodes `lem:line-rep-kernel` and

    16	The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:102-174`.

    25	/--

    30	-/

    32	    (u v : Fin m → K) : Set (Fin m → K) :=
    33	  {x | ∃ t : K, x = u + t • v}
    34

    38	-/
    39	def coordinateDirection {m : ℕ}
    40	    (i : Fin m) : Fin m → K :=
    41	  Pi.single i 1
    42	
    43	/--

     3	/-!
     4	# Matrix-valued measurements for the MIP*=RE project
     5	
     6	This file provides the matrix-valued measurement layer used by the LDT formalization.
     7	
     8	## Main definitions
     9	
    10	* `Submeasurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to at most the identity.
    11	* `Measurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to exactly the identity.
    12	* `Submeasurement.postprocess` — data-processed submeasurements via answer relabeling.
    13	* `Measurement.postprocess` — the paper's postprocessing proposition for complete POVMs.
    14	* `inconsistency` — the off-diagonal mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`.
    15	* `diagOverlap` — the diagonal mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`.
    16	
    17	## References
    18	
    19	This file builds the project's finite-dimensional measurement layer on top of
    20	the normalized-trace and positive-operator facts in `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix`
    21	for the quantum formalization in `references/ldt-paper/`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    25	
    26	namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	/-! ## Submeasurements and measurements -/
    29	
    30	/--
    31	A submeasurement on a finite answer type `α` is a family of PSD matrices
    32	`M : α → Op d` with `∑ a, M a ≤ 1`.
    33	-/
    34	structure Submeasurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
    35	  /-- The effect operators. -/
    36	  effect : α → Op d
    37	  /-- Each effect is positive semidefinite. -/
    38	  pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a
    39	  /-- The effects sum to at most the identity. -/
    40	  sum_le_one : ∑ a, effect a ≤ 1
    41	
    42	/--
    43	A measurement is a submeasurement whose effects sum exactly to the identity.
    44	-/
    45	structure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    46	    extends Submeasurement α d where
    47	  /-- The effects sum to the identity. -/
    48	  sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1
    49	
    50	/-! ## Totals and postprocessing -/
    51	
    52	namespace Submeasurement
    53	
    54	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    55	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    56	
    57	/-! ### Totals and postprocessing -/
    58	
    59	/-- The total operator `∑ a, M_a`. -/
    60	noncomputable def total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d :=
    61	  ∑ a, M.effect a
    62	
    63	/--
    64	Data processing: relabel the answer set by `f : α → β`, summing the effects over
    65	fibers.
    66	-/
    67	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    68	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d where
    69	  effect b := ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    70	  pos b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
    71	  sum_le_one := by
    72	    calc
    73	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    74	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
    75	      _ ≤ 1 := M.sum_le_one
    76	
    77	/-- Restatement of `sum_le_one` in terms of the named total operator. -/
    78	theorem total_le_one (M : Submeasurement α d) :
    79	    M.total ≤ 1 := by
    80	  simpa [total] using M.sum_le_one
    81	
    82	/-- Postprocessing preserves the sum of all effects. -/
    83	theorem postprocess_sum_eq [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    84	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    85	    ∑ a, M.effect a = ∑ b, (M.postprocess f).effect b :=
    86	  (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect).symm
    87	
    88	/-- Postprocessing preserves the named total operator. -/
    89	theorem postprocess_total [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    90	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    91	    (M.postprocess f).total = M.total := by
    92	  simpa [total] using (M.postprocess_sum_eq f).symm
    93	
    94	end Submeasurement

    96	namespace Measurement
    97	
    98	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]

   101	/--
   102	Build a complete measurement from effects whose sum is exactly the identity.
   103	
   104	This constructor keeps the equality proof as the primary hypothesis and derives
   105	the inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper
   106	sites that are explicitly POVMs rather than relaxed sub-POVMs.
   107	-/
   108	def ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)
   109	    (sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1) : Measurement α d where
   110	  effect := effect
   111	  pos := pos
   112	  sum_le_one := le_of_eq sum_eq_one
   113	  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one
   114	
   115	/-- The named total of a complete measurement is the identity. -/
   116	theorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :
   117	    M.total = 1 :=
   118	  M.sum_eq_one
   119	
   120	/--
   121	Postprocess a complete measurement by relabeling outcomes.
   122	
   123	This formalizes `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex:169--180`: regrouping
   124	the effects along the fibers of `f` preserves the total operator, so a POVM
   125	remains a POVM after postprocessing.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   128	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) : Measurement β d where
   129	  toSubmeasurement := M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f
   130	  sum_eq_one := by
   131	    calc
   132	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
   133	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
   134	      _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one

   136	@[simp] theorem postprocess_effect [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   137	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
   138	    (M.postprocess f).effect b =

   140	  rfl
   141	
   142	@[simp] theorem postprocess_to_submeasurement [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   143	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) :
   144	    (M.postprocess f).toSubmeasurement = M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f :=
   145	  rfl
   146	
   147	/-- A complete measurement is determined by its effects. -/
   148	theorem ext {M N : Measurement α d} (h : ∀ a, M.effect a = N.effect a) :
   149	    M = N := by
   150	  cases M with
   151	  | mk M hM =>
   152	      cases N with
   153	      | mk N hN =>
   154	          cases M with
   155	          | mk effectM posM leM =>
   156	              cases N with
   157	              | mk effectN posN leN =>
   158	                  simp only at h
   159	                  have heffect : effectM = effectN := funext h
   160	                  subst effectN
   161	                  rfl
   162	
   163	/-- Relabeling along `f` and then along `g` is relabeling along `g ∘ f`: the

   165	fiber of `g` over `c`, and regrouping a finite sum of effects along it does not
   166	change the sum. -/
   167	theorem postprocess_comp {γ : Type*} [Fintype γ]
   168	    [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
   169	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (g : β → γ) :
   170	    (M.postprocess f).postprocess g = M.postprocess (fun a => g (f a)) := by
   171	  classical
   172	  apply ext

   174	  calc
   175	    ((M.postprocess f).postprocess g).effect c =

   182	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   183	          intro b _
   184	          by_cases hgb : g b = c
   185	          · simp only [hgb, if_true]
   186	            rw [Finset.sum_filter]
   187	          · simp [hgb]
   188	    _ = ∑ b : β, ∑ a : α,
   189	        if g b = c ∧ f a = b then M.effect a else 0 := by
   190	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   191	          intro b _
   192	          by_cases hgc : g b = c <;> simp [hgc]
   193	    _ = ∑ a : α, ∑ b : β,
   194	        if g b = c ∧ f a = b then M.effect a else 0 := by
   195	          rw [Finset.sum_comm]

   200	          by_cases hgc : g (f a) = c

   205	              · exact (hba hfa.symm).elim
   206	              · simp [hfa]
   207	            · simp
   208	          · have hzero :

   210	                  if g b = c ∧ f a = b then M.effect a else 0) = 0 := by
   211	              apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
   212	              intro b _
   213	              by_cases hfa : f a = b
   214	              · subst b
   215	                simp [hgc]
   216	              · simp [hfa]
   217	            simp [hgc, hzero]

   219	          change _ = ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter

   221	          rw [Finset.sum_filter]
   222

   232	/-- The off-diagonal overlap mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`. -/

    28	/-! ## Equality of the two consistency formulations -/
    29	
    30	-- The following identities identify pure-state expectation with the
    31	-- Euclidean quadratic form used in the consistency calculations below.  They
    32	-- send a pure state to its Euclidean coordinate vector and identify the
    33	-- quadratic form of that vector with evaluation in the associated density
    34	-- state; they are stated for an arbitrary finite index type in
    35	-- `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/DistanceTheorems/Support.lean`.
    36	export MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus (pureStateEuclideanVector
    37	  pureStateEuclideanVector_apply pureStateEuclideanVector_norm
    38	  pureState_stateQForm_eq_ev)

    40	/-- For complete projective families and a pure bipartite state, the LDT
    41	consistency relation is exactly the QPBT off-diagonal defect.  In
    42	particular, changing between the density and vector formulations incurs no
    43	loss in the error parameter. -/
    44	theorem consRel_iff_consistencyDefect
    45	    {Question Outcome iotaA iotaB : Type*}
    46	    [Fintype Question] [DecidableEq Question]
    47	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
    48	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
    49	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
    50	    [Nonempty (iotaA × iotaB)]
    51	    (psi : PureState (iotaA × iotaB))
    52	    (mu : Distribution Question) (hmu : mu.IsProbability)
    53	    (A : Question → ProjMeas Outcome iotaA)
    54	    (B : Question → ProjMeas Outcome iotaB) (delta : ℝ) :
    55	    ConsRel (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB)) mu
    56	        (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) delta ↔
    57	      consistencyDefect mu
    58	        (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
    59	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a))
    60	        (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) ≤ delta := by
    61	  let AM : Question → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement Outcome (iotaA × iotaB) :=
    62	    fun x => DistanceCalculus.leftPlacedMeasurement
    63	      (ldtMeasurementToMatrixMeasurement (A x).toMeasurement)
    64	  let BM : Question → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement Outcome (iotaA × iotaB) :=
    65	    fun x => DistanceCalculus.rightPlacedMeasurement
    66	      (ldtMeasurementToMatrixMeasurement (B x).toMeasurement)
    67	  have hAM (x : Question) (a : Outcome) :
    68	      (AM x).effect a = heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1 := rfl
    69	  have hBM (x : Question) (a : Outcome) :
    70	      (BM x).effect a = heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a) := rfl
    71	  have hdefect :
    72	      consistencyDefect mu
    73	          (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
    74	          (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a))
    75	          (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) =
    76	        bipartiteConsError (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB)) mu
    77	          (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) := by
    78	    calc
    79	      consistencyDefect mu
    80	          (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
    81	          (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a))
    82	          (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) =
    83	          1 - avgOver mu (fun x => ∑ a,
    84	            DistanceCalculus.stateQForm (pureStateEuclideanVector psi)
    85	              ((AM x).effect a * (BM x).effect a)) := by
    86	            simpa only [hAM, hBM] using
    87	              DistanceCalculus.consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_overlap
    88	                mu AM BM (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) hmu
    89	                  (pureStateEuclideanVector_norm psi)
    90	      _ = avgOver mu (fun x => 1 - ∑ a,
    91	            DistanceCalculus.stateQForm (pureStateEuclideanVector psi)
    92	              ((AM x).effect a * (BM x).effect a)) := by
    93	            rw [avgOver_sub, avgOver_const_of_isProbability mu hmu]
    94	      _ = bipartiteConsError (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB)) mu
    95	          (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) := by
    96	            unfold bipartiteConsError
    97	            apply avgOver_congr
    98	            intro x
    99	            rw [qBipartiteConsDefect_of_measurements
   100	              (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB))
   101	              (A x).toMeasurement (B x).toMeasurement]
   102	            rw [ev_one_of_isNormalized (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB))
   103	              psi.toQuantumState_isNormalized]
   104	            congr 1
   105	            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   106	            intro a _
   107	            rw [hAM, hBM]
   108	            rw [DistanceCalculus.placed_product_stateQForm_eq]
   109	            exact pureState_stateQForm_eq_ev psi
   110	              (opTensor ((A x).outcome a) ((B x).outcome a))
   111	  constructor
   112	  · intro h
   113	    rw [hdefect]
   114	    exact h.offDiagonalBound
   115	  · intro h
   116	    refine ⟨?_⟩
   117	    rw [← hdefect]
   118	    exact h

    26	  | .A => .B
