+/-! ## The three LDT conclusions in direct coordinates -/
+
+/-- The direct single-coordinate point/global defect is exactly the LDT
+defect after the polynomial, point, and scalar equivalences. -/
+theorem directPointPolynomial_consistencyDefect_eq
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
+    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    ∀ (G : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιB),
+      consistencyDefect
+          (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
+          (fun u a => heteroKron
+            ((directPointCoordinateMeasurementA D S r u).effect a) 1)
+          (fun u a => heteroKron 1
+            ((directPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G u).effect a)) S.ψ =
+        consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
+          (ldtPointAPlaced D S hS r)
+          (ldtPolynomialEvaluationRight D G) S.ψ := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  intro G
+  calc
+    consistencyDefect
+        (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
+        (fun u a => heteroKron
+          ((directPointCoordinateMeasurementA D S r u).effect a) 1)
+        (fun u a => heteroKron 1
+          ((directPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G u).effect a)) S.ψ =
+      consistencyDefect
+        (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
+        (fun u a => ldtPointAPlaced D S hS r
+          (directPointEquiv D u) (directScalarEquiv D a))
+        (fun u a => ldtPolynomialEvaluationRight D G
+          (directPointEquiv D u) (directScalarEquiv D a)) S.ψ := by
+          apply consistencyDefect_congr
+          · intro u a
+            unfold ldtPointAPlaced
+            congr 1
+            exact (directCoordinatePointMeasurement_effect_transport
+              D S hS r u a).symm
+          · intro u a
+            unfold ldtPolynomialEvaluationRight
+            congr 1
+            exact directPolynomialMeasurement_evaluation_effect D G u a
+    _ = consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
+        (ldtPointAPlaced D S hS r)
+        (ldtPolynomialEvaluationRight D G) S.ψ :=
+      consistencyDefect_uniform_question_outcome_equiv
+        (directPointEquiv D) (directScalarEquiv D)
+        (ldtPointAPlaced D S hS r)
+        (ldtPolynomialEvaluationRight D G) S.ψ
+
+/-- Convert the point-on-Alice/global-on-Bob conclusion of `LDT.Test.mainFormal`
+for one simultaneous coordinate to the direct QPBT defect, with the identical
+numerical bound. -/
+theorem directPointPolynomial_consistencyDefect_le
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
+    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    ∀ (G : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιB)
+      (delta : ℝ),
+      ConsRel (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).state
+          (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
+          (IdxProjMeas.toIdxSubMeas
+            (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementA)
+          (polynomialEvaluationFamily D.toLDTParameters G.toSubMeas) delta →
+        consistencyDefect
+          (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
+          (fun u a => heteroKron
+            ((directPointCoordinateMeasurementA D S r u).effect a) 1)
+          (fun u a => heteroKron 1
+            ((directPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G u).effect a))
+          S.ψ ≤ delta := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  intro G delta h
+  rw [directPointPolynomial_consistencyDefect_eq D S hS r G]
+  apply strategyConsRel_consistencyDefect_le S
+    (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
+    (uniformDistribution_isProbability (Point D.toLDTParameters))
+    (ldtCoordinatePointMeasurementA D S hS r)
+    (ldtPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G) delta
+  change ConsRel (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).state
+    (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
+    (IdxProjMeas.toIdxSubMeas
+      (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementA)
+    (polynomialEvaluationFamily D.toLDTParameters G.toSubMeas) delta
+  exact h
+
+/-- The direct single-coordinate global/point defect is exactly the LDT
+defect after the polynomial, point, and scalar equivalences. -/
+theorem directPolynomialPoint_consistencyDefect_eq
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
+    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    ∀ (G : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιA),
+      consistencyDefect
+          (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
+          (fun u a => heteroKron
+            ((directPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G u).effect a) 1)
+          (fun u a => heteroKron 1
+            ((directPointCoordinateMeasurementB D S r u).effect a)) S.ψ =
+        consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
+          (ldtPolynomialEvaluationLeft D G)
+          (ldtPointBPlaced D S hS r) S.ψ := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  intro G
+  calc
+    consistencyDefect
+        (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
+        (fun u a => heteroKron
+          ((directPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G u).effect a) 1)
+        (fun u a => heteroKron 1
+          ((directPointCoordinateMeasurementB D S r u).effect a)) S.ψ =
+      consistencyDefect
+        (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
+        (fun u a => ldtPolynomialEvaluationLeft D G
+          (directPointEquiv D u) (directScalarEquiv D a))
+        (fun u a => ldtPointBPlaced D S hS r
+          (directPointEquiv D u) (directScalarEquiv D a)) S.ψ := by
+          apply consistencyDefect_congr
+          · intro u a
+            unfold ldtPolynomialEvaluationLeft
+            congr 1
+            exact directPolynomialMeasurement_evaluation_effect D G u a
+          · intro u a
+            unfold ldtPointBPlaced
+            congr 1
+            exact (directCoordinatePointMeasurementB_effect_transport
+              D S hS r u a).symm
+    _ = consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
+        (ldtPolynomialEvaluationLeft D G)
+        (ldtPointBPlaced D S hS r) S.ψ :=
+      consistencyDefect_uniform_question_outcome_equiv
+        (directPointEquiv D) (directScalarEquiv D)
+        (ldtPolynomialEvaluationLeft D G)
+        (ldtPointBPlaced D S hS r) S.ψ
+
+/-- Convert the global-on-Alice/point-on-Bob conclusion of
+`LDT.Test.mainFormal` for one simultaneous coordinate to the direct QPBT
+defect, with the identical numerical bound. -/
+theorem directPolynomialPoint_consistencyDefect_le
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
+    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    ∀ (G : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιA)
+      (delta : ℝ),
+      ConsRel (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).state
+          (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
+          (polynomialEvaluationFamily D.toLDTParameters G.toSubMeas)
+          (IdxProjMeas.toIdxSubMeas
+            (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementB) delta →
+        consistencyDefect
+          (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
+          (fun u a => heteroKron
+            ((directPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G u).effect a) 1)
+          (fun u a => heteroKron 1
+            ((directPointCoordinateMeasurementB D S r u).effect a))
+          S.ψ ≤ delta := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  intro G delta h
+  have hbase :
+      ConsRel (strategyQuantumState S)
+        (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
+        (fun u => (ldtPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G u).toSubMeas)
+        (fun u => (ldtCoordinatePointMeasurementB D S hS r u).toSubMeas)
+        delta := by
+    change ConsRel (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).state
+      (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
+      (polynomialEvaluationFamily D.toLDTParameters G.toSubMeas)
+      (IdxProjMeas.toIdxSubMeas
+        (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementB) delta
+    exact h
+  have hldt := strategyConsRel_consistencyDefect_le S
+    (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
+    (uniformDistribution_isProbability (Point D.toLDTParameters))
+    (ldtPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G)
+    (ldtCoordinatePointMeasurementB D S hS r) delta hbase
+  have heq := consistencyDefect_congr
+    (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
+    (ldtPolynomialEvaluationLeft D G)
+    (fun u a => heteroKron
+      ((ldtPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G u).outcome a) 1)
+    (ldtPointBPlaced D S hS r)
+    (fun u a => heteroKron 1
+      ((ldtCoordinatePointMeasurementB D S hS r u).outcome a)) S.ψ
+    (by intro u a; rfl) (by intro u a; rfl)
+  rw [directPolynomialPoint_consistencyDefect_eq D S hS r G, heq]
+  exact hldt
+
+/-- Relabeling both global polynomial measurements identifies their direct
+QPBT defect with the LDT global/global defect. -/
+theorem directPolynomialPolynomial_consistencyDefect_eq
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    ∀ (GA : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιA)
+      (GB : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιB),
+      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
+          (fun _ g => heteroKron ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GA).effect g) 1)
+          (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GB).effect g))
+          S.ψ =
+        consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
+          (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialLeftPlaced D GA g)
+          (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialRightPlaced D GB g) S.ψ := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  intro GA GB
+  calc
+    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
+        (fun _ g => heteroKron ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GA).effect g) 1)
+        (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GB).effect g))
+        S.ψ =
+      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
+        (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialLeftPlaced D GA (directPolyEquivPolynomial D g))
+        (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialRightPlaced D GB (directPolyEquivPolynomial D g))
+        S.ψ := by
+          apply consistencyDefect_congr
+          · intro _ g
+            unfold ldtPolynomialLeftPlaced
+            rw [directPolynomialMeasurement_effect]
+          · intro _ g
+            unfold ldtPolynomialRightPlaced
+            rw [directPolynomialMeasurement_effect]
+    _ = consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
+        (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialLeftPlaced D GA g)
+        (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialRightPlaced D GB g) S.ψ :=
+      consistencyDefect_outcome_equiv (uniformDistribution Unit)
+        (directPolyEquivPolynomial D)
+        (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialLeftPlaced D GA g)
+        (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialRightPlaced D GB g) S.ψ
+
+/-- Convert the global/global conclusion of `LDT.Test.mainFormal` to the direct
+QPBT defect, with the identical numerical bound. -/
+theorem directPolynomialPolynomial_consistencyDefect_le
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    ∀ (GA : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιA)
+      (GB : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιB)
+      (delta : ℝ),
+      ConsRel (strategyQuantumState S) (uniformDistribution Unit)
+          (constSubMeasFamily GA.toSubMeas)
+          (constSubMeasFamily GB.toSubMeas) delta →
+        consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
+          (fun _ g => heteroKron ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GA).effect g) 1)
+          (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GB).effect g))
+          S.ψ ≤ delta := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  intro GA GB delta h
+  have hldt := strategyConsRel_consistencyDefect_le S
+    (uniformDistribution Unit) (uniformDistribution_isProbability Unit)
+    (fun _ => GA) (fun _ => GB) delta h
+  have heq := consistencyDefect_congr (uniformDistribution Unit)
+    (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialLeftPlaced D GA g)
+    (fun _ g => heteroKron (GA.outcome g) 1)
+    (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialRightPlaced D GB g)
+    (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 (GB.outcome g)) S.ψ
+    (by intro _ g; rfl) (by intro _ g; rfl)
+  rw [directPolynomialPolynomial_consistencyDefect_eq D S GA GB, heq]
+  exact hldt
+

+    ∀ (G : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιB)

+    (uniformDistribution_isProbability (Point D.toLDTParameters))
+    (ldtCoordinatePointMeasurementA D S hS r)
+    (ldtPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G) delta h
+

+import MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.StrategyRole.Algebra

+/-!
+# State conversion and direct point readout
+
+This module contains the pure-state conversion and direct point-readout
+portion of the low-degree consistency transport.
+
+## References
+
+- `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:393-458`
+- `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:180-202`
+- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder

+/-! ## Equality of the two consistency formulations -/
+
+-- The following identities identify pure-state expectation with the
+-- Euclidean quadratic form used in the consistency calculations below.  They
+-- send a pure state to its Euclidean coordinate vector and identify the
+-- quadratic form of that vector with evaluation in the associated density
+-- state; they are stated for an arbitrary finite index type in
+-- `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/DistanceTheorems/Support.lean`.
+export MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus (pureStateEuclideanVector
+  pureStateEuclideanVector_apply pureStateEuclideanVector_norm
+  pureState_stateQForm_eq_ev)
+
+/-- For complete projective families and a pure bipartite state, the LDT
+consistency relation is exactly the QPBT off-diagonal defect.  In
+particular, changing between the density and vector formulations incurs no
+loss in the error parameter. -/
+theorem consRel_iff_consistencyDefect
+    {Question Outcome iotaA iotaB : Type*}
+    [Fintype Question] [DecidableEq Question]
+    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
+    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
+    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
+    [Nonempty (iotaA × iotaB)]
+    (psi : PureState (iotaA × iotaB))
+    (mu : Distribution Question) (hmu : mu.IsProbability)
+    (A : Question → ProjMeas Outcome iotaA)
+    (B : Question → ProjMeas Outcome iotaB) (delta : ℝ) :
+    ConsRel (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB)) mu
+        (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) delta ↔
+      consistencyDefect mu
+        (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
+        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a))
+        (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) ≤ delta := by
+  let AM : Question → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement Outcome (iotaA × iotaB) :=
+    fun x => DistanceCalculus.leftPlacedMeasurement
+      (ldtMeasurementToMatrixMeasurement (A x).toMeasurement)
+  let BM : Question → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement Outcome (iotaA × iotaB) :=
+    fun x => DistanceCalculus.rightPlacedMeasurement
+      (ldtMeasurementToMatrixMeasurement (B x).toMeasurement)
+  have hAM (x : Question) (a : Outcome) :
+      (AM x).effect a = heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1 := rfl
+  have hBM (x : Question) (a : Outcome) :
+      (BM x).effect a = heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a) := rfl
+  have hdefect :
+      consistencyDefect mu
+          (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
+          (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a))
+          (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) =
+        bipartiteConsError (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB)) mu
+          (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) := by
+    calc
+      consistencyDefect mu
+          (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
+          (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a))
+          (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) =
+          1 - avgOver mu (fun x => ∑ a,
+            DistanceCalculus.stateQForm (pureStateEuclideanVector psi)
+              ((AM x).effect a * (BM x).effect a)) := by
+            simpa only [hAM, hBM] using
+              DistanceCalculus.consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_overlap
+                mu AM BM (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) hmu
+                  (pureStateEuclideanVector_norm psi)
+      _ = avgOver mu (fun x => 1 - ∑ a,
+            DistanceCalculus.stateQForm (pureStateEuclideanVector psi)
+              ((AM x).effect a * (BM x).effect a)) := by
+            rw [avgOver_sub, avgOver_const_of_isProbability mu hmu]
+      _ = bipartiteConsError (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB)) mu
+          (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) := by
+            unfold bipartiteConsError
+            apply avgOver_congr
+            intro x
+            rw [qBipartiteConsDefect_of_measurements
+              (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB))
+              (A x).toMeasurement (B x).toMeasurement]
+            rw [ev_one_of_isNormalized (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB))
+              psi.toQuantumState_isNormalized]
+            congr 1
+            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+            intro a _
+            rw [hAM, hBM]
+            rw [DistanceCalculus.placed_product_stateQForm_eq]
+            exact pureState_stateQForm_eq_ev psi
+              (opTensor ((A x).outcome a) ((B x).outcome a))
+  constructor
+  · intro h
+    rw [hdefect]
+    exact h.offDiagonalBound
+  · intro h
+    refine ⟨?_⟩
+    rw [← hdefect]
+    exact h

+/-! ## Direct-strategy state and point readout -/
+
+private theorem quantumState_ext
+    {iota : Type*} [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
+    {rho sigma : QuantumState iota} (h : rho.density = sigma.density) : rho = sigma := by
+  cases rho with
+  | mk rho hrho =>
+      cases sigma with
+      | mk sigma hsigma =>
+          simp only at h
+          subst sigma
+          rfl
+
+/-- The pure state carried by a game strategy, regarded as an LDT pure state. -/
+noncomputable def gameStrategyPureState {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) :
+    letI : Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
+      (strategyQuantumState_isNormalized S).nonempty
+    PureState (S.ιA × S.ιB) := by
+  letI : Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
+    (strategyQuantumState_isNormalized S).nonempty
+  exact strategyPureState S
+
+@[simp] theorem gameStrategyPureState_vector {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) :
+    letI : Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
+      (strategyQuantumState_isNormalized S).nonempty
+    (gameStrategyPureState S).vector = S.ψ := by
+  letI : Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
+    (strategyQuantumState_isNormalized S).nonempty
+  rfl
+
+/-- The density state used by `directCoordinateProjStrat` is the density of
+the strategy's displayed pure state. -/
+theorem strategyQuantumState_eq_gameStrategyPureState
+    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) :
+    letI : Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
+      (strategyQuantumState_isNormalized S).nonempty
+    strategyQuantumState S =
+      (gameStrategyPureState S : QuantumState (S.ιA × S.ιB)) := by
+  letI : Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
+    (strategyQuantumState_isNormalized S).nonempty
+  apply quantumState_ext
+  rfl
+
+/-- The Euclidean vector of the strategy's pure-state presentation is the
+original game vector. -/
+@[simp] theorem gameStrategyPureState_euclideanVector
+    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) :
+    letI : Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
+      (strategyQuantumState_isNormalized S).nonempty
+    pureStateEuclideanVector (gameStrategyPureState S) = S.ψ := by
+  letI : Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
+    (strategyQuantumState_isNormalized S).nonempty
+  apply (EuclideanSpace.equiv (S.ιA × S.ιB) ℂ).injective
+  rfl
+
+/-- An LDT consistency relation on the density state associated with a game
+strategy gives the identical QPBT defect bound on the strategy vector. -/
+theorem strategyConsRel_consistencyDefect_le
+    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
+    {Question Outcome : Type*}
+    [Fintype Question] [DecidableEq Question]
+    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
+    (mu : Distribution Question) (hmu : mu.IsProbability)
+    (A : Question → ProjMeas Outcome S.ιA)
+    (B : Question → ProjMeas Outcome S.ιB) (delta : ℝ)
+    (h : ConsRel (strategyQuantumState S) mu
+      (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) delta) :
+    consistencyDefect mu
+      (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
+      (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a)) S.ψ ≤ delta := by
+  letI : Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
+    (strategyQuantumState_isNormalized S).nonempty
+  let pure : PureState (S.ιA × S.ιB) := strategyPureState S
+  have hpure :
+      ConsRel (pure : QuantumState (S.ιA × S.ιB)) mu
+        (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) delta := by
+    simpa [pure, strategyQuantumState] using h
+  have hconverted := (consRel_iff_consistencyDefect pure mu hmu A B delta).mp hpure
+  have hv : pureStateEuclideanVector pure = S.ψ := by
+    exact gameStrategyPureState_euclideanVector S
+  rw [hv] at hconverted
+  exact hconverted
+
+@[simp] theorem directPointQuestionOf_directPointEquiv
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
+    directPointQuestionOf D (directPointEquiv D u) =
+      directLdPointQuestionOf D u := by
+  unfold directPointQuestionOf ldtPointToDirect
+  rw [(directPointEquiv D).symm_apply_apply]
+
+/-- LDT points associated with direct parameters have a canonical zero
+witness. -/
+instance directLdtPointNonempty (D : DirectLdParams) :
+    Nonempty (Point D.toLDTParameters) :=
+  ⟨fun _ => ⟨0, D.toLDTParameters.hq⟩⟩
+
+/-- The LDT scalar readout is the direct coordinate readout followed by
+the scalar coding equivalence. -/
+@[simp] theorem directPointAnswerReadout_eq
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k) (answer : DirectLdAnswer D) :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    directPointAnswerReadout D r answer =
+      directScalarEquiv D (directLdPointValuesOrZero D answer r) := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  cases answer <;> rfl
+
+/-- At corresponding points and scalar outcomes, the LDT point effect is
+the effect of the direct point measurement followed by coordinate projection. -/
+theorem directCoordinatePointMeasurement_effect_transport
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
+    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k)
+    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (a : DirectScalarQ D) :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    (((directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementA
+      (directPointEquiv D u)).outcome (directScalarEquiv D a)) =
+      ((S.A (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
+        (fun answer => directLdPointValuesOrZero D answer r)).effect a := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  classical
+  simp only [directCoordinateProjStrat, directCoordinatePointMeasurement,
+    directLdGame,
+    ProjMeas.postprocess, SubMeas.postprocess_outcome,
+    matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas_outcome,
+    directPointQuestionOf_directPointEquiv,
+    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
+  congr 1
+  ext answer
+  rw [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_filter]
+  simp only [Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
+  simpa only [directPointAnswerReadout_eq] using
+    (directScalarEquiv D).injective.eq_iff
+
+/-- Bob's point effects satisfy the same direct-to-LDT readout identity. -/
+theorem directCoordinatePointMeasurementB_effect_transport
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
+    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k)
+    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (a : DirectScalarQ D) :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    (((directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementB
+      (directPointEquiv D u)).outcome (directScalarEquiv D a)) =
+      ((S.B (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
+        (fun answer => directLdPointValuesOrZero D answer r)).effect a := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  classical
+  simp only [directCoordinateProjStrat, directCoordinatePointMeasurement,
+    directLdGame,
+    ProjMeas.postprocess, SubMeas.postprocess_outcome,
+    matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas_outcome,
+    directPointQuestionOf_directPointEquiv,
+    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
+  congr 1
+  ext answer
+  rw [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_filter]
+  simp only [Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
+  simpa only [directPointAnswerReadout_eq] using
+    (directScalarEquiv D).injective.eq_iff
+
+/-- Alice's direct point measurement followed by projection to coordinate
+`r`. -/
+noncomputable def directPointCoordinateMeasurementA
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
+    (r : Fin D.k) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
+    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectScalarQ D) S.ιA :=
+  (S.A (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
+    (fun answer => directLdPointValuesOrZero D answer r)
+
+/-- Bob's direct point measurement followed by projection to coordinate
+`r`. -/
+noncomputable def directPointCoordinateMeasurementB
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
+    (r : Fin D.k) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
+    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectScalarQ D) S.ιB :=
+  (S.B (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
+    (fun answer => directLdPointValuesOrZero D answer r)
+
+/-- Evaluate a transported LDT polynomial measurement at a direct point. -/
+noncomputable def directPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement
+    (D : DirectLdParams) :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    {iota : Type*} → [Fintype iota] → [DecidableEq iota] →
+      ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) iota →
+        (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) →
+          MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectScalarQ D) iota := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  intro iota _ _ G u
+  exact (directPolynomialMeasurement D G).postprocess
+    (fun g => MvPolynomial.eval u g.1)
+
+/-- Alice's LDT point family obtained from direct coordinate `r`. -/
+noncomputable def ldtCoordinatePointMeasurementA
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
+    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    IdxProjMeas (Point D.toLDTParameters) (Fq D.toLDTParameters) S.ιA := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  exact (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementA
+
+/-- Bob's LDT point family obtained from direct coordinate `r`. -/
+noncomputable def ldtCoordinatePointMeasurementB
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
+    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    IdxProjMeas (Point D.toLDTParameters) (Fq D.toLDTParameters) S.ιB := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  exact (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementB
+
+/-- The LDT projective evaluation family associated with a global
+polynomial projective measurement. -/
+noncomputable def ldtPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement
+    (D : DirectLdParams) :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    {iota : Type*} → [Fintype iota] → [DecidableEq iota] →
+      ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) iota →
+        IdxProjMeas (Point D.toLDTParameters) (Fq D.toLDTParameters) iota := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  intro iota _ _ G u
+  exact ProjMeas.postprocess G (fun g => g u)
+
+/-- Left placement of Alice's LDT point family. -/
+noncomputable def ldtPointAPlaced
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
+    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    Point D.toLDTParameters → Fq D.toLDTParameters → Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  intro u a
+  exact heteroKron ((ldtCoordinatePointMeasurementA D S hS r u).outcome a) 1
+
+/-- Right placement of Bob's LDT point family. -/
+noncomputable def ldtPointBPlaced
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
+    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    Point D.toLDTParameters → Fq D.toLDTParameters → Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  intro u a
+  exact heteroKron 1 ((ldtCoordinatePointMeasurementB D S hS r u).outcome a)
+
+/-- Left placement of an LDT polynomial evaluation family. -/
+noncomputable def ldtPolynomialEvaluationLeft
+    (D : DirectLdParams) {iotaA iotaB : Type*}
+    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
+    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB] :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) iotaA →
+      Point D.toLDTParameters → Fq D.toLDTParameters → Op (iotaA × iotaB) := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  intro G u a
+  exact heteroKron ((ldtPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G u).outcome a) 1
+
+/-- Right placement of an LDT polynomial evaluation family. -/
+noncomputable def ldtPolynomialEvaluationRight
+    (D : DirectLdParams) {iotaA iotaB : Type*}
+    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
+    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB] :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) iotaB →
+      Point D.toLDTParameters → Fq D.toLDTParameters → Op (iotaA × iotaB) := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  intro G u a
+  exact heteroKron 1 ((ldtPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G u).outcome a)
+
+/-- Left placement of an LDT global polynomial measurement. -/
+noncomputable def ldtPolynomialLeftPlaced
+    (D : DirectLdParams) {iotaA iotaB : Type*}
+    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
+    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB] :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) iotaA →
+      MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters → Op (iotaA × iotaB) := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  intro G g
+  exact heteroKron (G.outcome g) 1
+
+/-- Right placement of an LDT global polynomial measurement. -/
+noncomputable def ldtPolynomialRightPlaced
+    (D : DirectLdParams) {iotaA iotaB : Type*}
+    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
+    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB] :

+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  intro G g
+  exact heteroKron 1 (G.outcome g)

   140	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   141	  exact eprState_norm (Fin (L.q / L.m))
   142	
   143	/-- Reindexing Euclidean coordinates along an equivalence preserves norm. -/
   144	theorem reindexState_norm_eq
   145	    {iota kappa : Type*}
   146	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   147	    [Fintype kappa] [DecidableEq kappa]
   148	    (e : iota ≃ kappa) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
   149	    ‖reindexState e psi‖ = ‖psi‖ := by
   150	  rw [← sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)]
   151	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq]
   152	  change (∑ j : kappa, ‖psi (e.symm j)‖ ^ 2) = ∑ i : iota, ‖psi i‖ ^ 2
   153	  exact e.symm.sum_comp (fun i => ‖psi i‖ ^ 2)
   154	
   155	/-- The coordinate tensor of two Euclidean vectors has the product norm. -/
   156	theorem vecTensor_norm_eq
   157	    {iota kappa : Type*}
   158	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   159	    [Fintype kappa] [DecidableEq kappa]
   160	    (u : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ kappa) :
   161	    ‖vecTensor u v‖ = ‖u‖ * ‖v‖ := by
   162	  rw [← sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (mul_nonneg (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _))]
   163	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, mul_pow, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq,
   164	    EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq]
   165	  change (∑ p : iota × kappa, ‖u p.1 * v p.2‖ ^ 2) =
   166	    (∑ i : iota, ‖u i‖ ^ 2) * ∑ j : kappa, ‖v j‖ ^ 2
   167	  simp only [norm_mul, mul_pow]
   168	  rw [← Finset.univ_product_univ, Finset.sum_product, Finset.sum_mul]
   169	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   170	  intro i hi
   171	  rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   172	
   173	/-- Tensor the original strategy state with the maximally correlated residue
   174	state and shuffle the factors back into the two local carriers. -/
   175	noncomputable def seedFiberLiftedState
   176	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams) :
   177	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
   178	      ((S.ιA × Fin (L.q / L.m)) × (S.ιB × Fin (L.q / L.m))) :=
   179	  reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor S.ψ (seedResidueAncilla L))
   180	
   181	/-- The correlated seed-fiber lift preserves normalization of the strategy
   182	state. -/
   183	theorem seedFiberLiftedState_norm
   184	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams) :
   185	    ‖seedFiberLiftedState S L‖ = 1 := by
   186	  rw [seedFiberLiftedState, reindexState_norm_eq, vecTensor_norm_eq,
   187	    S.ψ_norm, seedResidueAncilla_norm, one_mul]
   188	
   189	/-! ## From the seed-indexed game to the direct game -/
   190	
   191	/-- The seed-indexed question selected in one residue block of a direct
   192	question.  Applying `ldCL` ensures that irrelevant ambient coordinates are
   193	canonicalized exactly as in the source game. -/
   194	noncomputable def seededLdQuestion (L : LdParams)
   195	    (q : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   196	    (residue : Fin (L.q / L.m)) : LdQuestion L :=
   197	  (q.1, ldCL L q.1 (ldSpaceOfDirectResidue L q.2 residue))
   198	
   199	/-- Dilate a strategy for the seed-indexed low-degree game to the directly
   200	indexed game.  The two local carriers receive correlated copies of the seed
   201	residue, and each measurement is block diagonal in that residue. -/
   202	noncomputable def ldStrategyToDirect (L : LdParams)
   203	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L)) : Strategy (directLdGame L.toDirectLdParams) where
   204	  ιA := S.ιA × Fin (L.q / L.m)
   205	  ιB := S.ιB × Fin (L.q / L.m)
   206	  ψ := seedFiberLiftedState S L
   207	  ψ_norm := seedFiberLiftedState_norm S L
   208	  A q := blockDiagonalMeasurement fun residue =>
   209	    matrixMeasurementTransport (ldDirectAnswerEquiv L)
   210	      (S.A (seededLdQuestion L q residue))
   211	  B q := blockDiagonalMeasurement fun residue =>
   212	    matrixMeasurementTransport (ldDirectAnswerEquiv L)
   213	      (S.B (seededLdQuestion L q residue))
   214	
   215	/-- Projectivity is preserved by the correlated seed-fiber dilation. -/
   216	theorem ldStrategyToDirect_isProjective (L : LdParams)
   217	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L)) (hS : S.IsProjective) :
   218	    (ldStrategyToDirect L S).IsProjective := by
   219	  constructor
   220	  · intro q
   221	    apply blockDiagonalMeasurement_isProjective
   222	    intro residue
   223	    apply matrixMeasurementTransport_isProjective
   224	    exact hS.1 (seededLdQuestion L q residue)
   225	  · intro q
   226	    apply blockDiagonalMeasurement_isProjective
   227	    intro residue
   228	    apply matrixMeasurementTransport_isProjective
   229	    exact hS.2 (seededLdQuestion L q residue)
   230	
   231	@[simp] theorem ldStrategyToDirect_A_effect (L : LdParams)
   232	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L))
   233	    (q : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   234	    (answer : DirectLdAnswer L.toDirectLdParams) :
   235	    ((ldStrategyToDirect L S).A q).effect answer =
   236	      Matrix.blockDiagonal fun residue =>
   237	        (S.A (seededLdQuestion L q residue)).effect
   238	          ((ldDirectAnswerEquiv L).symm answer) :=
   239	  rfl
   240	
   241	@[simp] theorem ldStrategyToDirect_B_effect (L : LdParams)
   242	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L))
   243	    (q : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   244	    (answer : DirectLdAnswer L.toDirectLdParams) :
   245	    ((ldStrategyToDirect L S).B q).effect answer =
   246	      Matrix.blockDiagonal fun residue =>
   247	        (S.B (seededLdQuestion L q residue)).effect
   248	          ((ldDirectAnswerEquiv L).symm answer) :=
   249	  rfl
   250	
   251	/-- A direct question reconstructed in a residue block parses back to its
   252	canonical direct form. -/
   253	theorem parse_seededLdQuestion (L : LdParams)
   254	    (q : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   255	    (residue : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   256	    parseLdQuestion L (seededLdQuestion L q residue) =
   257	      (q.1, directLdMap L.toDirectLdParams q.1 q.2) := by
   258	  exact parseLdQuestion_ldCL_ofDirectResidue L q.1 q.2 residue
   259	
   260	/-- Coordinate formula for the correlated residue lift. -/
   261	theorem seedFiberLiftedState_apply
   262	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams)
   263	    (i : S.ιA) (j : S.ιB)
   264	    (r s : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   265	    seedFiberLiftedState S L ((i, r), (j, s)) =
   266	      if r = s then
   267	        S.ψ (i, j) * (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card (Fin (L.q / L.m)) : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹
   268	      else 0 := by
   269	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   270	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   271	  simp [seedFiberLiftedState, reindexState, vecTensor, seedResidueAncilla,
   272	    eprState, prodShuffle]
   273	
   274	end
   275	
   276	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Observables.LineDefs
     2	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.DistributionMarginals
     3	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.PauliBasisTest
     4	
     5	/-!
     6	# Geometry for the directly indexed low-degree game
     7	
     8	This module defines the parameters, line carrier, and line-point distributions
     9	for the directly indexed low-degree game.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The line-point distributions originate in
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-272`.
    15	The directly indexed repair is documented in
    16	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    24	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    25	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    26	
    27	noncomputable section
    28	
    29	/-- Parameters for the directly indexed low-degree game.  Unlike `LdParams`,
    30	this directly indexed line-space construction has no divisibility field: its coordinate index is
    31	sampled from `Fin m` rather than encoded by fibers of `chiIndex`.
    32	
    33	This is the direct-index repair described in
    34	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`; it is not a second
    35	definition of the source verifier game. -/
    36	structure DirectLdParams where
    37	  q : ℕ
    38	  m : ℕ
    39	  d : ℕ
    40	  k : ℕ
    41	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    42	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    43	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    44	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    45	
    46	/-- The canonical scalar model for directly indexed parameters. -/
    47	noncomputable def DirectLdParams.model (D : DirectLdParams) : FixedFieldModel D.q :=
    48	  fixedFieldModel D.q D.hq
    49	
    50	/-- The scalar field of a directly indexed low-degree game. -/
    51	abbrev DirectScalarQ (D : DirectLdParams) := D.model.K
    52	
    53	/-- The first coordinate, available because directly indexed dimensions are
    54	positive. -/
    55	def DirectLdParams.firstIndex (D : DirectLdParams) : Fin D.m :=
    56	  ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one D.hm⟩
    57	
    58	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Nonempty (Fin D.m) := ⟨D.firstIndex⟩
    59	
    60	/-- The direct game used at the extended dimension of the combining map.  Its
    61	field, degree, and simultaneity parameters are inherited from `P`, while its
    62	dimension is `2 * P.m + 2`; no divisibility assertion is introduced.
    63	
    64	The construction has dimension `2 * P.m + 2` without requiring
    65	`2 * P.m + 2 ∣ P.q`; it supplies the directly indexed line and coordinate
    66	spaces used in the dimension-extension argument of
    67	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1257-1293`.
    68	-/
    69	def AdmissibleParams.extendedDirectLd (P : AdmissibleParams) : DirectLdParams where
    70	  q := P.q
    71	  m := 2 * P.m + 2
    72	  d := P.d
    73	  k := 1
    74	  hm := by omega
    75	  hd := P.hd
    76	  hk := by decide
    77	  hq := P.hq
    78	
    79	/-- A common random sample for the directly indexed question distribution.
    80	The point, coordinate index, and unrestricted direction are mutually uniform. -/
    81	structure DirectLdSpace (D : DirectLdParams) where
    82	  point : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
    83	  index : Fin D.m
    84	  direction : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
    85	  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype
    86	
    87	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Nonempty (DirectLdSpace D) :=
    88	  ⟨⟨0, D.firstIndex, 0⟩⟩
    89	
    90	/-- Decompose a direct sample into its point and the remaining independent
    91	coordinates. -/
    92	private def directLdSpacePointEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
    93	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
    94	      (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ×
    95	        (Fin D.m × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) where
    96	  toFun sample := (sample.point, sample.index, sample.direction)
    97	  invFun sample := ⟨sample.1, sample.2.1, sample.2.2⟩
    98	  left_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
    99	  right_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
   100	
   101	/-- Decompose a direct sample into its stored index and the remaining
   102	independent coordinates. -/
   103	def directLdSpaceIndexEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   104	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
   105	      Fin D.m ×
   106	        ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ×
   107	          (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) where
   108	  toFun sample := (sample.index, sample.point, sample.direction)
   109	  invFun sample := ⟨sample.2.1, sample.1, sample.2.2⟩
   110	  left_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
   111	  right_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
   112	
   113	/-- Compatibility name for the index-first direct-sample decomposition. -/
   114	abbrev directLdSpaceIndexSplitEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   115	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
   116	      Fin D.m × ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) :=
   117	  directLdSpaceIndexEquiv D
   118	
   119	/-- Zero the coordinates preceding the directly sampled prefix index. -/
   120	def directPrefixProjection {D : DirectLdParams} (i : Fin D.m)
   121	    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D :=
   122	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   123	
   124	/-- Canonical line descriptions whose coordinate index is stored directly.
   125	Coordinates are numbered from zero, so `index = i` represents coordinate
   126	`i + 1` in the paper. -/
   127	inductive DirectLineDesc (D : DirectLdParams) where
   128	  | axis (base : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (index : Fin D.m)
   129	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap (coordinateDirection index) base = base)
   130	  | diagonal (base : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (index : Fin D.m)
   131	      (direction : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
   132	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap direction base = base)
   133	      (prefixZero : ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < index.val → direction j = 0)
   134	  deriving DecidableEq
   135	
   136	/-- The kind of a directly indexed line. -/
   137	def DirectLineDesc.kind {D : DirectLdParams} : DirectLineDesc D → LineKind
   138	  | .axis _ _ _ => .axis
   139	  | .diagonal _ _ _ _ _ => .diagonal
   140	
   141	/-- The coordinate index stored in a directly indexed line. -/
   142	def DirectLineDesc.index {D : DirectLdParams} : DirectLineDesc D → Fin D.m
   143	  | .axis _ index _ => index
   144	  | .diagonal _ index _ _ _ => index
   145	
   146	/-- The canonical base point of a directly indexed line. -/
   147	def DirectLineDesc.base {D : DirectLdParams} :
   148	    DirectLineDesc D → Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
   149	  | .axis base _ _ => base
   150	  | .diagonal base _ _ _ _ => base
   151	
   152	/-- The geometric direction of a directly indexed line. -/
   153	def DirectLineDesc.direction {D : DirectLdParams} (line : DirectLineDesc D) :
   154	    Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D :=
   155	  match line with
   156	  | .axis _ index _ => coordinateDirection index
   157	  | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction
   158	
   159	/-- The base of a directly indexed description is fixed by its geometric
   160	direction. -/
   161	theorem DirectLineDesc.base_fixed {D : DirectLdParams} (line : DirectLineDesc D) :
   162	    lineRepMap line.direction line.base = line.base := by
   163	  cases line with
   164	  | axis base index baseFixed => exact baseFixed
   165	  | diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact baseFixed
   166	
   167	/-- Every directly indexed diagonal description retains its prefix-zero
   168	invariant. -/
   169	theorem DirectLineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero {D : DirectLdParams}
   170	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) (hline : line.kind = .diagonal) :
   171	    ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < line.index.val → line.direction j = 0 := by
   172	  cases line with
   173	  | axis base index baseFixed => simp [DirectLineDesc.kind] at hline
   174	  | diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact prefixZero
   175	
   176	/-- The point set represented by a directly indexed line. -/
   177	noncomputable def DirectLineDesc.pointSet {D : DirectLdParams}
   178	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) : Set (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :=
   179	  linePoints line.base line.direction
   180	
   140	
   141	/-- The directly indexed diagonal-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
   142	def directDlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)
   143	    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)
   144	    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
   145	    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
   146	  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,
   147	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   148	      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   149	
   150	/-- The directly indexed low-degree win predicate.  It differs from
   151	`ldWinPredicate` only by reading the coordinate index directly from each line
   152	question. -/
   153	noncomputable def directLdWinPredicate (D : DirectLdParams) :
   154	    DirectLdQuestion D → DirectLdQuestion D →
   155	      DirectLdAnswer D → DirectLdAnswer D → Bool :=
   156	  open Classical in
   157	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   158	    if validDirectLdAnswer tA a && validDirectLdAnswer tB b then
   159	      match tA, tB, a, b with
   160	      | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   161	      | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   162	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   163	      | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   164	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   165	      | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   166	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   167	      | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   168	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   169	      | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   170	      | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   171	      | _, _, _, _ => true
   172	    else false
   173	
   174	/-- The directly indexed low-degree game at an arbitrary positive dimension.
   175	It is an internal analysis game, not the conditionally linear verifier game
   176	`ldGame`. -/
   177	noncomputable def directLdGame (D : DirectLdParams) : Game where
   178	  QuestionA := DirectLdQuestion D
   179	  QuestionB := DirectLdQuestion D
   180	  AnswerA := DirectLdAnswer D
   181	  AnswerB := DirectLdAnswer D
   182	  μ := directLdQuestionDistribution D
   183	  μ_prob := directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability D
   184	  decide := directLdWinPredicate D
   185	
   186	/-- The canonical point question associated with a geometric point. -/
   187	def directLdPointQuestionOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   188	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : DirectLdQuestion D :=
   189	  (.point, ⟨u, D.firstIndex, 0⟩)
   190	
   191	/-- Total point-answer relabeling used in the direct soundness conclusion.
   192	Wrong-form answers are folded into the zero tuple, exactly as for
   193	`ldPointValuesOrZero`. -/
   194	def directLdPointValuesOrZero (D : DirectLdParams) :
   195	    DirectLdAnswer D → Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D
   196	  | .pointVals values => values
   197	  | .alinePolys _ => 0
   198	  | .dlinePolys _ => 0
   199	
   200	/-- A simultaneous tuple of bounded polynomials for the directly indexed
   201	game. -/
   202	noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyTuple (D : DirectLdParams) :=
   203	  Fin D.k → PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d
   204	
   205	/-- A polynomial-tuple POVM for the directly indexed game. -/
   206	noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyMeasTuple (D : DirectLdParams) (ι : Type*)
   207	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   208	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectPolyTuple D) ι
   209	
   210	/-- Evaluate every component of a direct polynomial tuple at a point. -/
   211	def evalDirectPolyTupleAt {D : DirectLdParams}
   212	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (g : DirectPolyTuple D) :
   213	    Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D :=
   214	  fun j => MvPolynomial.eval u (g j).1
   215	
   216	end
   217	
   218	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.DistributionAvg
     2	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.Distance
     3	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.DistributionAux
     4	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.State
     5	
     6	/-! # State-dependent consistency and strategy closeness
     7	
     8	The definitions are the finite-dimensional forms of `def:consistency` and
     9	`def:strategy-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-237`,
    10	from `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-288`.
    11	-/
    12	
    13	open scoped BigOperators
    14	
    15	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    16	
    17	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    18	
    19	/-- The off-diagonal defect in `def:consistency`, blueprint
    20	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    21	noncomputable def consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
    22	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    23	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    24	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    25	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    26	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    27	    ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
    28	      if a = b then 0 else
    29	        (inner ℂ ψ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm
    30	          ((A x a * B x b).mulVec ψ))).re)
    31	
    32	/-- A uniform consistency defect is invariant under a bijective relabeling of
    33	its question type. -/
    34	theorem consistencyDefect_uniform_question_equiv
    35	    {X Y Outcome iota : Type*}
    36	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Nonempty X]
    37	    [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y] [Nonempty Y]
    38	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
    39	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    40	    (e : X ≃ Y) (A B : Y → Outcome → Op iota)
    41	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
    42	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
    43	        (fun x a => A (e x) a) (fun x a => B (e x) a) psi =
    44	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Y) A B psi := by
    45	  unfold consistencyDefect
    46	  simpa using avgOver_uniform_equiv e (fun x =>
    47	    ∑ a : Outcome, ∑ b : Outcome,
    48	      if a = b then 0 else
    49	        (inner ℂ psi ((EuclideanSpace.equiv iota ℂ).symm
    50	          (((A (e x) a) * (B (e x) b)).mulVec psi))).re)
    51	
    52	/-- A consistency defect is invariant under a bijective relabeling of both
    53	outcome families. -/
    54	theorem consistencyDefect_outcome_equiv
    55	    {X Alpha Beta iota : Type*}
    56	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X]
    57	    [Fintype Alpha] [DecidableEq Alpha]
    58	    [Fintype Beta] [DecidableEq Beta]
    59	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    60	    (mu : Distribution X) (e : Beta ≃ Alpha)
    61	    (A B : X → Alpha → Op iota) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
    62	    consistencyDefect mu
    63	        (fun x b => A x (e b)) (fun x b => B x (e b)) psi =
    64	      consistencyDefect mu A B psi := by
    65	  unfold consistencyDefect
    66	  apply avgOver_congr
    67	  intro x
    68	  let term : Alpha → Alpha → ℝ := fun a b =>
    69	    if a = b then 0 else
    70	      (inner ℂ psi ((EuclideanSpace.equiv iota ℂ).symm
    71	        (((A x a) * (B x b)).mulVec psi))).re
    72	  calc
    73	    _ = ∑ a : Beta, ∑ b : Beta, term (e a) (e b) := by
    74	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    75	      intro a _
    76	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    77	      intro b _
    78	      unfold term
    79	      by_cases hab : a = b
    80	      · subst b
    81	        simp
    82	      · have heab : e a ≠ e b := fun h => hab (e.injective h)

    85	        ∑ a : Beta, ∑ b : Alpha, term (e a) b := by
    86	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    87	      intro a _
    88	      exact Equiv.sum_comp e (fun b => term (e a) b)

    90	      Equiv.sum_comp e (fun a => ∑ b : Alpha, term a b)

    93	/-- Simultaneous bijective relabeling of uniform questions and outcomes leaves
    94	the consistency defect unchanged. -/
    95	theorem consistencyDefect_uniform_question_outcome_equiv
    96	    {X Y Alpha Beta iota : Type*}
    97	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Nonempty X]
    98	    [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y] [Nonempty Y]
    99	    [Fintype Alpha] [DecidableEq Alpha]
   100	    [Fintype Beta] [DecidableEq Beta]
   101	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   102	    (questionEquiv : X ≃ Y) (outcomeEquiv : Beta ≃ Alpha)
   103	    (A B : Y → Alpha → Op iota) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
   104	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
   105	        (fun x b => A (questionEquiv x) (outcomeEquiv b))
   106	        (fun x b => B (questionEquiv x) (outcomeEquiv b)) psi =
   107	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Y) A B psi := by
   108	  calc
   109	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
   110	        (fun x b => A (questionEquiv x) (outcomeEquiv b))
   111	        (fun x b => B (questionEquiv x) (outcomeEquiv b)) psi =
   112	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
   113	        (fun x a => A (questionEquiv x) a)
   114	        (fun x a => B (questionEquiv x) a) psi :=
   115	      consistencyDefect_outcome_equiv (uniformDistribution X)
   116	        outcomeEquiv _ _ psi

   118	      consistencyDefect_uniform_question_equiv questionEquiv A B psi

   125	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
   126	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]

   134	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   135	  intro a _
   136	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   137	  intro b _
   138	  by_cases hab : a = b
   139	  · simp [hab]
   140	  · simp only [hab, if_false]
   141	    rw [hA x a, hB x b]

     3	/-!
     4	# Matrix-valued measurements for the MIP*=RE project
     5	
     6	This file provides the matrix-valued measurement layer used by the LDT formalization.
     7	
     8	## Main definitions
     9	
    10	* `Submeasurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to at most the identity.
    11	* `Measurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to exactly the identity.
    12	* `Submeasurement.postprocess` — data-processed submeasurements via answer relabeling.
    13	* `Measurement.postprocess` — the paper's postprocessing proposition for complete POVMs.
    14	* `inconsistency` — the off-diagonal mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`.
    15	* `diagOverlap` — the diagonal mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`.
    16	
    17	## References
    18	
    19	This file builds the project's finite-dimensional measurement layer on top of
    20	the normalized-trace and positive-operator facts in `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix`
    21	for the quantum formalization in `references/ldt-paper/`.
    22	-/

    24	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder

    28	/-! ## Submeasurements and measurements -/
    29	
    30	/--
    31	A submeasurement on a finite answer type `α` is a family of PSD matrices
    32	`M : α → Op d` with `∑ a, M a ≤ 1`.
    33	-/
    34	structure Submeasurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
    35	  /-- The effect operators. -/
    36	  effect : α → Op d
    37	  /-- Each effect is positive semidefinite. -/
    38	  pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a
    39	  /-- The effects sum to at most the identity. -/
    40	  sum_le_one : ∑ a, effect a ≤ 1
    41	
    42	/--
    43	A measurement is a submeasurement whose effects sum exactly to the identity.
    44	-/
    45	structure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    46	    extends Submeasurement α d where
    47	  /-- The effects sum to the identity. -/
    48	  sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1
    49	
    50	/-! ## Totals and postprocessing -/
    51	
    52	namespace Submeasurement
    53	
    54	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    55	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    56	
    57	/-! ### Totals and postprocessing -/
    58	
    59	/-- The total operator `∑ a, M_a`. -/
    60	noncomputable def total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d :=
    61	  ∑ a, M.effect a
    62	
    63	/--
    64	Data processing: relabel the answer set by `f : α → β`, summing the effects over
    65	fibers.
    66	-/
    67	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    68	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d where
    69	  effect b := ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    70	  pos b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
    71	  sum_le_one := by
    72	    calc
    73	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    74	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
    75	      _ ≤ 1 := M.sum_le_one
    76	
    77	/-- Restatement of `sum_le_one` in terms of the named total operator. -/
    78	theorem total_le_one (M : Submeasurement α d) :
    79	    M.total ≤ 1 := by
    80	  simpa [total] using M.sum_le_one
    81	
    82	/-- Postprocessing preserves the sum of all effects. -/
    83	theorem postprocess_sum_eq [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    84	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    85	    ∑ a, M.effect a = ∑ b, (M.postprocess f).effect b :=
    86	  (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect).symm
    87	
    88	/-- Postprocessing preserves the named total operator. -/
    89	theorem postprocess_total [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    90	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    91	    (M.postprocess f).total = M.total := by
    92	  simpa [total] using (M.postprocess_sum_eq f).symm
    93	
    94	end Submeasurement

   101	/--
   102	Build a complete measurement from effects whose sum is exactly the identity.
   103	
   104	This constructor keeps the equality proof as the primary hypothesis and derives
   105	the inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper
   106	sites that are explicitly POVMs rather than relaxed sub-POVMs.
   107	-/
   108	def ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)
   109	    (sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1) : Measurement α d where
   110	  effect := effect
   111	  pos := pos
   112	  sum_le_one := le_of_eq sum_eq_one
   113	  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one
   114	
   115	/-- The named total of a complete measurement is the identity. -/
   116	theorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :
   117	    M.total = 1 :=
   118	  M.sum_eq_one
   119	
   120	/--
   121	Postprocess a complete measurement by relabeling outcomes.
   122	
   123	This formalizes `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex:169--180`: regrouping
   124	the effects along the fibers of `f` preserves the total operator, so a POVM
   125	remains a POVM after postprocessing.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   128	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) : Measurement β d where
   129	  toSubmeasurement := M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f
   130	  sum_eq_one := by
   131	    calc
   132	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
   133	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
   134	      _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one

   136	@[simp] theorem postprocess_effect [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   137	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
   138	    (M.postprocess f).effect b =
   139	      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a :=
   140	  rfl

   142	@[simp] theorem postprocess_to_submeasurement [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   143	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) :
   144	    (M.postprocess f).toSubmeasurement = M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f :=
   145	  rfl

   147	/-- A complete measurement is determined by its effects. -/
   148	theorem ext {M N : Measurement α d} (h : ∀ a, M.effect a = N.effect a) :
   149	    M = N := by
   150	  cases M with
   151	  | mk M hM =>
   152	      cases N with
   153	      | mk N hN =>
   154	          cases M with
   155	          | mk effectM posM leM =>
   156	              cases N with
   157	              | mk effectN posN leN =>
   158	                  simp only at h
   159	                  have heffect : effectM = effectN := funext h
   160	                  subst effectN
   161	                  rfl
   162	
   163	/-- Relabeling along `f` and then along `g` is relabeling along `g ∘ f`: the
   164	fiber of `g ∘ f` over `c` is the disjoint union of the fibers of `f` over the
   165	fiber of `g` over `c`, and regrouping a finite sum of effects along it does not
   166	change the sum. -/
   167	theorem postprocess_comp {γ : Type*} [Fintype γ]
   168	    [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
   169	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (g : β → γ) :
   170	    (M.postprocess f).postprocess g = M.postprocess (fun a => g (f a)) := by
   171	  classical
   172	  apply ext
   173	  intro c
   174	  calc
   175	    ((M.postprocess f).postprocess g).effect c =
   176	        ∑ b : β, if g b = c then
   177	          ∑ a : α, if f a = b then M.effect a else 0
   178	        else 0 := by
   179	          change (∑ b ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun b : β => g b = c),
   180	            ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a : α => f a = b), M.effect a) = _
   181	          rw [Finset.sum_filter]
   182	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   183	          intro b _
   184	          by_cases hgb : g b = c
   185	          · simp only [hgb, if_true]
   186	            rw [Finset.sum_filter]
   187	          · simp [hgb]
   188	    _ = ∑ b : β, ∑ a : α,
   189	        if g b = c ∧ f a = b then M.effect a else 0 := by
   190	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   191	          intro b _
   192	          by_cases hgc : g b = c <;> simp [hgc]
   193	    _ = ∑ a : α, ∑ b : β,
   194	        if g b = c ∧ f a = b then M.effect a else 0 := by
   195	          rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   196	    _ = ∑ a : α,
   197	        if g (f a) = c then M.effect a else 0 := by
   198	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   199	          intro a _
   200	          by_cases hgc : g (f a) = c
   201	          · rw [Finset.sum_eq_single (f a)]
   202	            · simp [hgc]
   203	            · intro b _ hba
   204	              by_cases hfa : f a = b
   205	              · exact (hba hfa.symm).elim
   206	              · simp [hfa]
   207	            · simp
   208	          · have hzero :
   209	                (∑ b : β,
   210	                  if g b = c ∧ f a = b then M.effect a else 0) = 0 := by
   211	              apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
   212	              intro b _
   213	              by_cases hfa : f a = b
   214	              · subst b
   215	                simp [hgc]
   216	              · simp [hfa]
   217	            simp [hgc, hzero]
   218	    _ = (M.postprocess (fun a => g (f a))).effect c := by
   219	          change _ = ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter
   220	            (fun a : α => g (f a) = c), M.effect a
   221	          rw [Finset.sum_filter]
   222

     2	\label{chap:qpbt-test}
     3	% Paper label sec:pauli-verifier kept for cross-reference fidelity; it resolves to this chapter.
     4	\label{sec:pauli-verifier}
     5	
     6	This chapter defines the two testing primitives underlying the question-reduction step: the \emph{classical low individual degree game}, in its simultaneous form, and the \emph{Pauli basis test}, a nonlocal game built from the classical game together with the Magic Square game. The chapter closes with the qubit form of the soundness statement (Corollary~\ref{cor:pauli-binary}) and the canonical parameter choice with its soundness bound (Definition~\ref{def:introparams}, Lemma~\ref{lem:delta-bound}).

    10	\section{The classical low individual degree game}
    11	% Paper labels sec:ld-verifier and sec:ld-game kept for cross-reference fidelity.
    12	\label{sec:ld-verifier}
    13	\label{sec:ld-game}
    14	
    15	The classical low individual degree game is a two-player game based on the low individual degree variant of the multilinearity test of Babai, Fortnow, and Lund. In the basic version, one player (the ``points player'') receives a uniformly random point $u \in \F_q^m$ and answers with a value $a \in \F_q$, while the other player (the ``lines player'') receives a random line through $u$ --- either axis-parallel or diagonal --- and answers with a univariate polynomial describing the restriction of a global function to that line. If the players share a polynomial $g\colon \F_q^m \to \F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$ and answer with $g(u)$ and with the restriction $g|_\ell$, they win with probability $1$; the soundness theorem below states that the converse approximately holds. In the simultaneous version, the players' answers are $k$-tuples, checked coordinatewise against a $k$-tuple of low individual degree polynomials.

    17	\begin{definition}[The classical low individual degree game: parameters and registers]\label{def:ld-game}

    25		% It is load-bearing: at d = 0 or k = 0 the prefactor a(dmk)^a of delta_ld in

    28		% hold trivially, is likewise outside the source's domain and is omitted.

We write $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{ld}}_{\mathsf{ldparams}}$ to emphasize the dependence on the parameter tuple. The type set of $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{ld}}$ is
    30		\[
    31			\mathcal T^{\mathrm{ld}} = \{\mathsf{Point}, \mathsf{ALine}, \mathsf{DLine}\}\;,
    32		\]
    33		and the distribution over type pairs $(t_{\mathrm A}, t_{\mathrm B})$ is uniform over $\mathcal T^{\mathrm{ld}} \times \mathcal T^{\mathrm{ld}}$. The ambient space is the direct sum $V = V_X \oplus V_I \oplus V_V$ of three register subspaces: the \emph{point register} $V_X \cong \F_q^m$, the \emph{coordinate register} $V_I \cong \F_q$, and the \emph{direction register} $V_V \cong \F_q^m$. Elements of $V$ are identified with triples $(u,s,v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q \times \F_q^m$.     36	\begin{definition}[Question distribution of the classical low individual degree game]\label{def:ld-question-distribution}
    37		\uses{def:ld-game, def:cl-func, def:cl-dist, lem:cl-concat, def:cl-canonical, def:line-representative}
    38		Let $\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$ be as in Definition~\ref{def:ld-game}. Define $L_{\mathsf{Point}}$ to be the $1$-level CL function on $V$ that projects onto $V_X$: for every $(u,s,v) \in V$,
    39		\begin{equation}
    40			\label{eq:cl-ptf}
    41			L_{\mathsf{Point}}(u,s,v) = (u,0,0)\;.
    42		\end{equation}
    43		For $s \in \F_q$, let $\chi(s)$ be the unique integer such that
    44		\begin{equation}
    45			\label{eq:chi-func}
    46			s = (\chi(s)-1)\,\frac{q}{m} + r
    47		\end{equation}
    48		for some $0 \le r < q/m$, where $s$ is interpreted as an integer in $\{0,1,\ldots,q-1\}$ under the identification of $\F_q$ with binary strings fixed in Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-algebra}.     49		\begin{equation}
    50			\label{eq:cl-alnf}
    51			L_{\mathsf{ALine}}(u,s,v) = \bigl(L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_{e_i}(u),\, s,\, 0\bigr)\quad\text{for all } (u,s,v) \in V\;,
    52		\end{equation}
    53		where $i = \chi(s)$ and $L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v$ denotes the canonical linear map with one-dimensional kernel spanned by $v$, used to compute canonical representatives of lines (Definition~\ref{def:line-representative}).     54		\begin{equation}
    55			\label{eq:cl-dlnf}
    56			L_{\mathsf{DLine}}(u,s,v) = \bigl(L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_{\pi_{i-1}(v)}(u),\, s,\, \pi_{i-1}(v)\bigr)\;,
    57		\end{equation}
    58		where $i = \chi(s)$ and $\pi_{i-1}$ zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of its input.     59	\section{Key theorem forms}
    60	
    61	Throughout, $q = 2^k$ with $k$ odd is an admissible field size, the tuple
    62	$(q,m,d)$ is admissible when moreover $d \ge 1$ and $m \mid q$, and
    63	$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ denotes the $m$-variate polynomial representatives
    64	over $\F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$.  The comparison involves four
    65	theorem forms.
    66	\begin{enumerate}
    67	  \item \textbf{Source theorem form} (the polynomial-pair measurement).  There
    68	  is a function $\delta_S(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$,
    69	  for universal constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$, such that for every
    70	  admissible $(q,m,d)$ and every projective strategy for the Pauli basis test
    71	  succeeding with probability at least $1-\eps$, there is a projective
    72	  measurement $\{\hat S_{g_X,g_Z}\}$ with outcomes pairs of polynomials in
    73	  $\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ whose evaluations are $\delta_S$-consistent, on
    74	  average over a uniform point $u \in \F_q^m$ and in both bases
    75	  $W \in \{X,Z\}$, with the corresponding points measurements
    76	  $\{\hat M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\}$ of the strategy, together with the
    77	  symmetric counterpart of this relation.

    79	  individual degree game with parameter tuple $(q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)$ is well

   108	\section{The source assertion and the obstruction}
   109	
   110	We examine the final step of the subsection ``Applying the classical
   111	low-degree test'' in the analysis of the Pauli basis test in the compression
   112	paper of Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright, and Yuen (MIP$^{*}$=RE,
   113	arXiv:2001.04383), whose quantum soundness component builds on the low
   114	individual degree test of \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}.%
   115	\footnote{Tracked in \localissue{0002}.  In the mirror of the source
   116	consulted here, the polynomial-pair lemma and its proof are at
   117	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
   118	lines~1267--1288; the sub-line lemma is at lines~1063--1116 and the combined
   119	line lemma at lines~1020--1034 of the same file.  The game parametrization
   120	with its divisibility, the index function, the soundness statement with its
   121	proof, and admissibility are at
   122	\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
   123	lines~33--35, 214--219, 413--458, and 958--961.}
   124	There, the combined point measurements
   125	$\{\hat Q^{x,z,\alpha,\beta}_c\}$ and combined line measurements
   126	$\{\hat Q^{\ell}_f\}$, indexed by points of $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and lines in
   127	$\F_q^{2m+2}$, are asserted to form a strategy for the classical low
   128	individual degree game with parameters
   129	\[
   130	  \mathsf{ldparams} = (q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)
   131	  \tag{\path{lem:qld-4-7}}
   132	\]
   133	of value $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$, and the quantum soundness theorem
   134	for that game is applied to produce the global polynomial-pair measurement.
   135	The two lemmas feeding this step are stated for the line-point distribution
   136	over $\F_q^{2m+2}$.
   137	
   138	The game, however, is parametrized by tuples $(q,m',d,k)$ with $q$ an
   139	admissible field size \emph{and $m'$ dividing $q$}.  The divisibility is not
   140	incidental: the question distribution is a conditionally linear distribution
   141	in which a uniform seed coordinate $s \in \F_q$, read as an integer in
   142	$\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$, determines the axis or diagonal index through the unique
   143	$\chi(s)$ with
   144	\[
   145	  s = (\chi(s)-1)\,\frac{q}{m'} + r, \qquad 0 \le r < \frac{q}{m'},
   146	  \tag{\path{eq:chi-func}}
   147	\]
   148	so that the $m'$ classes $\chi^{-1}(i)$ partition $\F_q$ into sets of equal
   149	size $q/m'$ and the index is uniform.  For $m' \nmid q$ neither the index
   150	function nor the line-point distribution built from it is defined.
   151	
   152	Admissibility of $(q,m,d)$ supplies only $m \mid q$.  Since an admissible $q$
   153	is a power of two, $m \mid q$ forces $m = 2^j$.  For $j \ge 1$ the integer
   154	$m+1 \ge 3$ is odd, so $2m+2 = 2(m+1)$ has an odd factor exceeding $1$ and
   155	divides no power of two; for $m = 1$ the condition $4 \mid q$ holds for every
   156	admissible $q$ except $q = 2$.  Thus the instantiation at dimension $2m+2$ is
   157	undefined for every admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$: for instance
   158	$(q,m,d) = (8,2,1)$ is admissible, while $6 \nmid 8$.  The source performs
   159	the instantiation without addressing the divisibility, so its proof route
   160	establishes the polynomial-pair lemma, and with it the soundness theorem for
   161	the Pauli basis test that rests on it, only for $m = 1$ and $q \ge 8$.

   163	\section{What the cited soundness theorem requires: the import obligations}
   164	\label{sec:import-obligations}
   165	
   166	The quantum soundness theorem for the classical game inherits the constraint
   167	$m' \mid q$ solely because it is stated for the game just described; its
   168	proof fixes an admissible $q$ with $m' \mid q$, asserts that the game with
   169	simultaneity parameter $1$ is \emph{identical} to the two-prover tensor-code
   170	test for the Reed--Solomon tensor code $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$ of the same
   171	authors' \emph{Quantum soundness of testing tensor codes} (arXiv:2111.08131)
   172	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}, and concludes by Theorem~4.7 there, instantiated with
   173	that theorem's auxiliary integer parameter --- denoted $k$ in that source,
   174	and written $K$ here to avoid clashing with the field exponent and the
   175	simultaneity parameter --- chosen as $(m')^3 d$.  Neither
   176	the asserted identity nor the instantiation is complete as stated, so the
   177	import carries two verification obligations, which this section details and
   178	which the blueprint's proof node for the soundness statement records as
   179	open.  Both obligations are independent of the divisibility question: they
   180	arise at every dimension, for the $\chi$-based game where it is defined and
   181	equally for the directly indexed variant proposed under the candidate
   182	repairs.
   183	
   184	\paragraph{The cited test.}
   185	In the two-prover tensor-code test (Figures~1 and~2 of
   186	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}; the two-prover strategy format and the goodness

  1989	\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for the compression of a correlated residue register]
  1990		\label{lem:direct-ld-residue-compression}
  1991		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldStrategyToDirect_pointPolynomial_compression}
  1992		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldStrategyToDirect_polynomialPoint_compression}
  1993		\leanok

  1996		compression identities between the classical low individual degree game
  1997		and its directly indexed presentation.
  1998	
  1999		Let $(\psi, A, B)$ be a strategy for the classical game with parameters
  2000		$(q,m,d,k)$, and extend it to the directly indexed game by adjoining to

  2004		register are perfectly correlated in the extended state. For a
  2005		polynomial-tuple POVM $G^{\mathrm B}$ on
  2006		$\hilb_{\mathrm B}\ot\C^{q/m}$, let $\bar G^{\mathrm B}$ be the

+  unfold stateQForm applyOperatorToState
+  change (inner ℂ (pureStateEuclideanVector ψ)

    41	  cases g with

    53	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    54	    PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d ≃
    55	      MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters := by
    56	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    57	  refine
    58	    { toFun := fun g =>
    59	        { poly := MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev g.1
    60	          lowIndividualDegree := directPolynomialRename_degreeOf_le D g.1
    61	            (degreeOf_le_of_mem_polyFunc g.2) }
    62	      invFun := fun g =>
    63	        ⟨MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev g.poly, ?_⟩
    64	      left_inv := ?_
    65	      right_inv := ?_ }
    66	  · rw [MvPolynomial.mem_restrictDegree]
    67	    intro s hs i
    68	    exact (MvPolynomial.degreeOf_le_iff.mp
    69	      (directPolynomialRename_degreeOf_le D g.poly g.lowIndividualDegree i)) s hs
    70	  · intro g

    72	    change MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev
    73	      (MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev g.1) = g.1
    74	    rw [MvPolynomial.rename_rename]
    75	    rw [show Fin.rev ∘ Fin.rev = id by funext i; simp]

    82	          rw [MvPolynomial.rename_rename]
    83	          rw [show Fin.rev ∘ Fin.rev = id by funext i; simp]
