    28	/-! ## Equality of the two consistency formulations -/
    29	
    30	-- The following identities identify pure-state expectation with the
    31	-- Euclidean quadratic form used in the consistency calculations below.  They
    32	-- send a pure state to its Euclidean coordinate vector and identify the
    33	-- quadratic form of that vector with evaluation in the associated density
    34	-- state; they are stated for an arbitrary finite index type in
    35	-- `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/DistanceTheorems/Support.lean`.
    36	export MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus (pureStateEuclideanVector
    37	  pureStateEuclideanVector_apply pureStateEuclideanVector_norm
    38	  pureState_stateQForm_eq_ev)
    39	
    40	/-- For complete projective families and a pure bipartite state, the LDT
    41	consistency relation is exactly the QPBT off-diagonal defect.  In
    42	particular, changing between the density and vector formulations incurs no
    43	loss in the error parameter. -/
    44	theorem consRel_iff_consistencyDefect
    45	    {Question Outcome iotaA iotaB : Type*}
    46	    [Fintype Question] [DecidableEq Question]
    47	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
    48	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
    49	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
    50	    [Nonempty (iotaA × iotaB)]
    51	    (psi : PureState (iotaA × iotaB))
    52	    (mu : Distribution Question) (hmu : mu.IsProbability)
    53	    (A : Question → ProjMeas Outcome iotaA)
    54	    (B : Question → ProjMeas Outcome iotaB) (delta : ℝ) :
    55	    ConsRel (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB)) mu
    56	        (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) delta ↔
    57	      consistencyDefect mu
    58	        (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
    59	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a))
    60	        (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) ≤ delta := by
    61	  let AM : Question → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement Outcome (iotaA × iotaB) :=
    62	    fun x => DistanceCalculus.leftPlacedMeasurement
    63	      (ldtMeasurementToMatrixMeasurement (A x).toMeasurement)
    64	  let BM : Question → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement Outcome (iotaA × iotaB) :=
    65	    fun x => DistanceCalculus.rightPlacedMeasurement
    66	      (ldtMeasurementToMatrixMeasurement (B x).toMeasurement)
    67	  have hAM (x : Question) (a : Outcome) :
    68	      (AM x).effect a = heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1 := rfl
    69	  have hBM (x : Question) (a : Outcome) :
    70	      (BM x).effect a = heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a) := rfl
    71	  have hdefect :
    72	      consistencyDefect mu
    73	          (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
    74	          (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a))
    75	          (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) =
    76	        bipartiteConsError (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB)) mu
    77	          (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) := by
    78	    calc
    79	      consistencyDefect mu
    80	          (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
    81	          (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a))
    82	          (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) =
    83	          1 - avgOver mu (fun x => ∑ a,
    84	            DistanceCalculus.stateQForm (pureStateEuclideanVector psi)
    85	              ((AM x).effect a * (BM x).effect a)) := by
    86	            simpa only [hAM, hBM] using
    87	              DistanceCalculus.consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_overlap
    88	                mu AM BM (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) hmu
    89	                  (pureStateEuclideanVector_norm psi)
    90	      _ = avgOver mu (fun x => 1 - ∑ a,
    91	            DistanceCalculus.stateQForm (pureStateEuclideanVector psi)
    92	              ((AM x).effect a * (BM x).effect a)) := by
    93	            rw [avgOver_sub, avgOver_const_of_isProbability mu hmu]
    94	      _ = bipartiteConsError (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB)) mu
    95	          (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) := by
    96	            unfold bipartiteConsError
    97	            apply avgOver_congr
    98	            intro x
    99	            rw [qBipartiteConsDefect_of_measurements
   100	              (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB))
   101	              (A x).toMeasurement (B x).toMeasurement]
   102	            rw [ev_one_of_isNormalized (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB))
   103	              psi.toQuantumState_isNormalized]
   104	            congr 1
   105	            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   106	            intro a _
   107	            rw [hAM, hBM]
   108	            rw [DistanceCalculus.placed_product_stateQForm_eq]
   109	            exact pureState_stateQForm_eq_ev psi
   110	              (opTensor ((A x).outcome a) ((B x).outcome a))
   111	  constructor
   112	  · intro h
   113	    rw [hdefect]
   114	    exact h.offDiagonalBound
   115	  · intro h
   116	    refine ⟨?_⟩
   117	    rw [← hdefect]
   118	    exact h

   239	/-! ## Correlated-ancilla compression -/
   240	
   241	/-!
   242	The diagonal-block conditional expectation preserves either mixed defect
   243	exactly because the point measurement on the opposite carrier is constant on
   244	the residue register.  It does not yield a global/global compression theorem:
   245	the lifted state pairs equal residues, whereas separately compressing both
   246	polynomial measurements produces an independent double average over residues.
   247	Neither quantity bounds the other in general.  This open obstruction is
   248	recorded in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
   249	-/
   250	
   251	/-- The normalized diagonal-block average of an operator on a carrier with a
   252	finite ancillary register.  This is the local conditional expectation used to
   253	discard one half of the correlated seed-residue ancilla. -/
   254	noncomputable def averageDiagonalBlock
   255	    {iota block : Type*} [Fintype iota] [Fintype block]
   256	    (A : Op (iota × block)) : Op iota := by
   257	  classical
   258	  exact (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   259	    ∑ r, A.submatrix (fun i => (i, r)) (fun i => (i, r))
   260	
   261	/-- Compress a POVM through the normalized diagonal-block average.  The
   262	nonemptiness assumption says precisely that the normalized finite average is
   263	defined over at least one ancillary basis element. -/
   264	noncomputable def correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement
   265	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
   266	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   267	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block] [Nonempty block]
   268	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha (iota × block)) :
   269	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota :=
   270	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
   271	    (fun a => averageDiagonalBlock (M.effect a))
   272	    (fun a => by
   273	      unfold averageDiagonalBlock
   274	      apply smul_nonneg
   275	      · positivity
   276	      · exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun r _ =>
   277	          Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr
   278	            ((Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp (M.pos a)).submatrix
   279	              (fun i => (i, r))))
   280	    (by
   281	      classical
   282	      ext i j
   283	      simp only [averageDiagonalBlock, Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.smul_apply,
   284	        Matrix.submatrix_apply]
   285	      calc
   286	        ∑ a, (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   287	              ∑ r, M.effect a (i, r) (j, r) =
   288	            (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   289	              ∑ a, ∑ r, M.effect a (i, r) (j, r) := by
   290	                rw [Finset.smul_sum]
   291	        _ = (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   292	              ∑ r, ∑ a, M.effect a (i, r) (j, r) := by
   293	                rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   294	        _ = (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   295	              ∑ r, (1 : Op (iota × block)) (i, r) (j, r) := by
   296	                congr 1
   297	                apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   298	                intro r _
   299	                simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using
   300	                  congrFun (congrFun M.sum_eq_one (i, r)) (j, r)
   301	        _ = (1 : Op iota) i j := by
   302	              simp [Matrix.one_apply, Fintype.card_ne_zero])
   303	
   304	@[simp] theorem correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement_effect
   305	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
   306	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   307	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block] [Nonempty block]
   308	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha (iota × block)) (a : alpha) :
   309	    (correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement M).effect a =
   310	      averageDiagonalBlock (M.effect a) :=
   311	  rfl
   312	
   313	private theorem averageDiagonalBlock_finset_sum
   314	    {alpha iota block : Type*} [Fintype iota] [Fintype block]
   315	    (s : Finset alpha) (A : alpha → Op (iota × block)) :
   316	    averageDiagonalBlock (∑ a ∈ s, A a) =
   317	      ∑ a ∈ s, averageDiagonalBlock (A a) := by
   318	  classical
   319	  ext i j
   320	  simp only [averageDiagonalBlock, Matrix.smul_apply, Matrix.sum_apply,
   321	    Matrix.submatrix_apply]
   322	  simp_rw [Finset.smul_sum]
   323	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   324	
   325	/-- Normalized diagonal-block compression commutes with deterministic outcome
   326	postprocessing. -/
   327	theorem correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement_postprocess
   328	    {alpha beta iota block : Type*}
   329	    [Fintype alpha] [DecidableEq alpha]
   330	    [Fintype beta] [DecidableEq beta]
   331	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   332	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block] [Nonempty block]
   333	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha (iota × block))
   334	    (f : alpha → beta) :
   335	    correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement (M.postprocess f) =
   336	      (correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement M).postprocess f := by
   337	  classical
   338	  apply MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ext
   339	  intro b
   340	  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect,
   341	    correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement_effect,
   342	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
   343	  exact averageDiagonalBlock_finset_sum
   344	    (Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b)) M.effect

   346	/-- Specialize ancillary compression to the nonempty residue fiber supplied by
   347	the divisibility data of `LdParams`. -/
   348	noncomputable def seedFiberCompressMeasurement
   349	    (L : LdParams) {alpha iota : Type*}
   350	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   351	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha
   352	      (iota × Fin (L.q / L.m))) :
   353	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota := by
   354	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   355	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   356	  exact correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement M
   357

   359	    (L : LdParams) {alpha iota : Type*}
   360	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   361	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha
   362	      (iota × Fin (L.q / L.m))) (a : alpha) :
   363	    (seedFiberCompressMeasurement L M).effect a =
   364	      averageDiagonalBlock (M.effect a) :=
   365	  rfl

   367	/-- Seed-fiber compression commutes with deterministic outcome
   368	postprocessing. -/
   369	theorem seedFiberCompressMeasurement_postprocess
   370	    (L : LdParams) {alpha beta iota : Type*}
   371	    [Fintype alpha] [DecidableEq alpha]
   372	    [Fintype beta] [DecidableEq beta]
   373	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   374	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha

   219	theorem directPolynomialPolynomial_consistencyDefect_eq
   220	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) :
   221	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   222	    ∀ (GA : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιA)
   223	      (GB : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιB),
   224	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
   225	          (fun _ g => heteroKron ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GA).effect g) 1)
   226	          (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GB).effect g))
   227	          S.ψ =

   229	          (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialLeftPlaced D GA g)
   230	          (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialRightPlaced D GB g) S.ψ := by
   231	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   232	  intro GA GB

   235	        (fun _ g => heteroKron ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GA).effect g) 1)
   236	        (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GB).effect g))

   257	/-- Convert the global/global conclusion of `LDT.Test.mainFormal` to the direct
   258	QPBT defect, with the identical numerical bound. -/
   259	theorem directPolynomialPolynomial_consistencyDefect_le
   260	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) :
   261	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   262	    ∀ (GA : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιA)
   263	      (GB : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιB)
   264	      (delta : ℝ),
   265	      ConsRel (strategyQuantumState S) (uniformDistribution Unit)
   266	          (constSubMeasFamily GA.toSubMeas)
   267	          (constSubMeasFamily GB.toSubMeas) delta →
   268	        consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
   269	          (fun _ g => heteroKron ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GA).effect g) 1)
   270	          (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 ((directPolynomialMeasurement D GB).effect g))
   271	          S.ψ ≤ delta := by
   272	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   273	  intro GA GB delta h
   274	  have hldt := strategyConsRel_consistencyDefect_le S
   275	    (uniformDistribution Unit) (uniformDistribution_isProbability Unit)
   276	    (fun _ => GA) (fun _ => GB) delta h
   277	  have heq := consistencyDefect_congr (uniformDistribution Unit)
   278	    (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialLeftPlaced D GA g)
   279	    (fun _ g => heteroKron (GA.outcome g) 1)
   280	    (fun _ g => ldtPolynomialRightPlaced D GB g)
   281	    (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 (GB.outcome g)) S.ψ
   282	    (by intro _ g; rfl) (by intro _ g; rfl)
   283	  rw [directPolynomialPolynomial_consistencyDefect_eq D S GA GB, heq]
   284	  exact hldt

   347	\begin{fact}
   348	\label{fact:add-a-proj2}
   349	Let $\mathcal{X},\mathcal{A}$ denote finite sets, and let $\mathcal{G}$ denote a set of functions $g: \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{A}$. Let $\{A^x_a \}$, $\{B^x_a\}$ be POVMs indexed by $\mathcal{X}$ and outcomes in $\mathcal{A}$. Let $\{ S_g^x \}_{x\in \mathcal{X}, g\in\mathcal{G}}$ denote a set of operators such that for all $x \in \mathcal{X}$, $\sum_g (S_g^x)^\dagger S_g^x \leq \Id$. 
   350	If $A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a$ on average over $x$, then $S_g^x A^x_{g(x)} \approx_\delta S_g^x B^x_{g(x)}$. 
   351	\end{fact}
   352	\begin{proof}
   353		We expand:
   354		\begin{align*}
   355			\E_x \sum_g \norm{ S^x_g (A^x_{g(x)} - B^x_{g(x)}) \ket{\psi}}^2 &= \E_x \sum_g \bra{\psi} (A^x_{g(x)} - B^x_{g(x)})^\dagger  (S_g^x)^\dagger S_g^x (A^x_{g(x)} - B^x_{g(x)}) \ket{\psi} \\
   356			&= \E_x \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^x_a - B^x_a)^\dagger  \Big(\sum_{g: g(x) = a} (S_g^x)^\dagger S_g^x \Big) (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi} \\
   357			&\leq \E_x \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^x_a - B^x_a)^\dagger (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi} \\
   358			&= \E_x \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi} }^2.
   359		\end{align*}
   360		The inequality follows from the fact that $\sum_{g: g(x) = a} (S_g^x)^\dagger S_g^x \leq \sum_g (S_g^x)^\dagger (S_g^x) \leq \Id$. The last line is at most $\delta$ by assumption, and we obtain the desired conclusion.
   361	\end{proof}

   364	\begin{lemma}
   365	\label{lem:cool-closeness-fact}
   366	Let $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{A}$ be finite sets and $\mu$ a distribution on $\mX$. Let $\{A^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be a projective measurement and let $\{B^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be a set of matrices. If $A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a$, then for all subsets $S \subseteq \mathcal{A}$, we have
   367	\[
   368		\sum_{a \in S} A^x_a \approx_\delta \sum_{a \in S} A^x_a \cdot B^x_a.
   369	\]
   370	\end{lemma}
   371	\begin{proof}
   372	We expand:
   373	\begin{align*}
   374		\E_x \norm{ \sum_{a \in S} \Big(A^x_a - A^x_a \cdot B^x_a\Big) \ket{\psi}}^2 &= \E_x \norm{ \sum_{a \in S} A^x_a \cdot \Big(A^x_a - B^x_a\Big) \ket{\psi}}^2 \\
   375		&= \E_x \sum_{a \in S} \bra{\psi} (A^x_a - B^x_a)^\dagger A^x_a (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi} \\
   376		&\leq \E_x \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a -  B^x_a) \ket{\psi}}^2\;,
   377	\end{align*}
   378	where all expectations are taken according to $\mu$. 
   379	In the second line we used the projectivity of $\{ A^x_a \}$, and in the third line we used that $A^x_a \leq \Id$.
   380	\end{proof}

   385	  If $A_a^x \approx_\delta B_a^x$ and $B_a^x \approx_\epsilon C_a^x$, then

+/-- A complete measurement is determined by its effects. -/
+theorem ext {M N : Measurement α d} (h : ∀ a, M.effect a = N.effect a) :
+    M = N := by
+  cases M with
+  | mk M hM =>
+      cases N with
+      | mk N hN =>
+          cases M with
+          | mk effectM posM leM =>
+              cases N with
+              | mk effectN posN leN =>
+                  simp only at h
+                  have heffect : effectM = effectN := funext h
+                  subst effectN
+                  rfl
+
+/-- Relabeling along `f` and then along `g` is relabeling along `g ∘ f`: the
+fiber of `g ∘ f` over `c` is the disjoint union of the fibers of `f` over the
+fiber of `g` over `c`, and regrouping a finite sum of effects along it does not
+change the sum. -/
+theorem postprocess_comp {γ : Type*} [Fintype γ]
+    [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
+    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (g : β → γ) :
+    (M.postprocess f).postprocess g = M.postprocess (fun a => g (f a)) := by
+  classical
+  apply ext
+  intro c
+  calc
+    ((M.postprocess f).postprocess g).effect c =
+        ∑ b : β, if g b = c then
+          ∑ a : α, if f a = b then M.effect a else 0
+        else 0 := by
+          change (∑ b ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun b : β => g b = c),
+            ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a : α => f a = b), M.effect a) = _
+          rw [Finset.sum_filter]
+          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+          intro b _
+          by_cases hgb : g b = c
+          · simp only [hgb, if_true]
+            rw [Finset.sum_filter]
+          · simp [hgb]
+    _ = ∑ b : β, ∑ a : α,
+        if g b = c ∧ f a = b then M.effect a else 0 := by
+          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+          intro b _
+          by_cases hgc : g b = c <;> simp [hgc]
+    _ = ∑ a : α, ∑ b : β,
+        if g b = c ∧ f a = b then M.effect a else 0 := by
+          rw [Finset.sum_comm]
+    _ = ∑ a : α,
+        if g (f a) = c then M.effect a else 0 := by
+          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+          intro a _
+          by_cases hgc : g (f a) = c
+          · rw [Finset.sum_eq_single (f a)]
+            · simp [hgc]
+            · intro b _ hba
+              by_cases hfa : f a = b
+              · exact (hba hfa.symm).elim
+              · simp [hfa]
+            · simp
+          · have hzero :
+                (∑ b : β,
+                  if g b = c ∧ f a = b then M.effect a else 0) = 0 := by
+              apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
+              intro b _
+              by_cases hfa : f a = b
+              · subst b
+                simp [hgc]
+              · simp [hfa]
+            simp [hgc, hzero]
+    _ = (M.postprocess (fun a => g (f a))).effect c := by
+          change _ = ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter
+            (fun a : α => g (f a) = c), M.effect a
+          rw [Finset.sum_filter]
+

 % Paper labels sec:ld-verifier and sec:ld-game kept for cross-reference fidelity.
 \label{sec:ld-verifier}
 \label{sec:ld-game}
 
 The classical low individual degree game is a two-player game based on the low individual degree variant of the multilinearity test of Babai, Fortnow, and Lund. In the basic version, one player (the ``points player'') receives a uniformly random point $u \in \F_q^m$ and answers with a value $a \in \F_q$, while the other player (the ``lines player'') receives a random line through $u$ --- either axis-parallel or diagonal --- and answers with a univariate polynomial describing the restriction of a global function to that line. If the players share a polynomial $g\colon \F_q^m \to \F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$ and answer with $g(u)$ and with the restriction $g|_\ell$, they win with probability $1$; the soundness theorem below states that the converse approximately holds. In the simultaneous version, the players' answers are $k$-tuples, checked coordinatewise against a $k$-tuple of low individual degree polynomials.

    28	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
    29	    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    30	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α ιA) :
    31	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α (ιA × ιB) :=
    32	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
    33	    (fun a => heteroKron (M.effect a) 1)
    34	    (fun a => MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg (M.pos a)
    35	      (Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg : 0 ≤ (1 : Op ιB)))

    37	      change ∑ a : α, leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB) (M.effect a) = 1

# Mathematical Language Guidelines

MIPStarRE Lean names and documentation should be written for readers comparing
the formalization with the paper and blueprint.

This is a project-local supplement to the Mathlib-derived documentation,
naming, and style guides in the lean-conventions skill's `MATHLIB_doc`,
`MATHLIB_naming`, and `MATHLIB_style` references.

## Scope

These guidelines apply to:

- public Lean declaration names and namespace names;
- module docstrings;
- declaration docstrings;
- documentation-visible section comments;
- explanatory comments that describe the mathematical role of a declaration.
- blueprint prose and formalization-support notes;
- issue titles and issue bodies;
- PR titles and PR descriptions.

## Source of Truth

Use terminology from the following sources, in this order:

1. `references/ldt-paper/`
2. `blueprint/src/chapter/`
3. established local conventions in nearby Lean files

When the paper has a term for the object, use that term. For Section 5, for
example, prefer orthogonalization lemma, truncation function, rounding to
projectors, rank reduction, and completing to measurement.

## Reference Notation And Terminology

The notation and terminology of the original reference are the default for
reader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean
docstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source
without first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.

When Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a
location which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the
first applicable location in the following order:

1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation
   differs from the paper;
2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a
   family of declarations in that file;
3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the
   blueprint;
4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a
   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.

The explanation should say:

- the notation or term used in the paper;
- the Lean object or name which represents it;
- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;
- the scope in which the replacement should be used.

A PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place
where future readers can learn it.

Formalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose
should name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,
rather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.

## Naming Norm

Names and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or
conclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was
assembled.

Avoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,
`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source
uses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes
such as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a
clearer phrase.

This is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.
Module names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,
blueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the
mathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line
number, or implementation history.

### Concrete examples

The table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the
codebase and on names seen during review.  Some entries are existing names;
others are proposed names for future refactors.  The "avoid" column lists
process-shaped names that encode the history of how the formalization was
assembled; the "prefer" column lists mathematical names that a reader of the
paper or blueprint would recognize.

| Avoid (process-shaped)                        | Prefer (mathematical)                     | Rationale                                              |
|:----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
| `Line130`                                     | `ProjectiveConsistency`                   | Paper Lemma 5.13, not "the line-130 identity"          |
| `Line169`                                     | `CompletionTransport`                     | Paper Lemma 5.16, step that transports completed data  |
| `Step6`                                       | `Orthonormalization`                      | Paper Section 5, the orthonormalization construction   |
| `FinalAssembly`                               | `DiagonalCompletion`                      | Paper Lemma 5.17, constructing a diagonal POVM         |
| `OneShotIneq`                                 | `SelfConsistencyDataProcessing` (or existing module `Preliminaries.SelfConsistency.DataProcessing`)           | Paper's data-processing inequality for self-consistency |
| `PipelineCheck`                               | `ErrorPropagationBound` (proposed)                   | The bound that propagates error through the test       |
| `QxpLayerWrapper`                             | `ProjectivePOVMCompletion` (proposed)                | The construction from round-projectors to POVMs        |
| `RawSpectralTruncation`                       | `SpectralTruncation`                      | The paper's spectral truncation, not an "unwrapped" version |
| `AddInUStep3To5`                              | `AddInUUpperExcessMass` (proposed)                  | Paper Addendum in §U, the upper excess-mass estimate   |
| `AddInUStep12`                                | `AddInUCommutationTail` (proposed)                   | Paper Addendum in §U, the commutation tail estimate    |

An avoided name is acceptable only when the cited paper itself uses that
phrase as the mathematical name (e.g., a lemma the paper calls "Step 2").
In that case the docstring should cite the paper's phrasing.

File-split PRs are a common place where this rule matters: new leaves should be
named by the mathematical boundary they isolate, and any public declarations
exposed by the split should be reviewed under the same standard.

### Shared helpers

When the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or
more chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single
shared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and
ensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all
call sites at once.  Issue [#1145] tracks this work across the repository.

Procedure:

1. **Confirm equivalence.**  Compare the statement of each copy.  If the
   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,
   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),
   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or
   explicit argument.
2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by
   both call sites.  Typical candidates:
   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/` for parameter-free operators and bounds,
   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Preliminaries/` for polynomial/field/character lemmas,
   - The highest chapter that is a common dependency of the two sites.
3. **Name mathematically.**  Give the shared helper a name that describes
   what it states, not which chapter it originally came from.
4. **Replace call sites.**  Delete the chapter-local copies and replace
   their uses with the shared helper.  A thin wrapper is allowed only when it
   preserves a paper-facing or blueprint-facing name that external readers
   need to search for; such wrappers should have a docstring or compatibility
   comment explaining why the alias exists.  Remove the wrapper once that
   paper-facing name is no longer needed for external reference.
5. **Document.**  Add a docstring to the shared helper citing the paper or
   blueprint location it supports.

### Legacy identifier treatment

If a docstring must mention a legacy Lean identifier, cite it in backticks and
describe the mathematical object in paper terminology. If an old public
identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR, record the required migration
in the issue, PR description, or an audit file under `audits/`.

Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
public name.  This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the
shared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or
blueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.

## Review Checklist

Reviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and
documentation prose.  Flag any item that fails.

- [ ] **Naming.**  Do public declaration names, namespace names, module names,
      theorem field names, and docstring prose describe a mathematical object,

/-! ## Equality of the two consistency formulations -/

-- The following identities identify pure-state expectation with the
-- Euclidean quadratic form used in the consistency calculations below.  They
-- send a pure state to its Euclidean coordinate vector and identify the
-- quadratic form of that vector with evaluation in the associated density
-- state; they are stated for an arbitrary finite index type in
-- `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/DistanceTheorems/Support.lean`.
export MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus (pureStateEuclideanVector
  pureStateEuclideanVector_apply pureStateEuclideanVector_norm
  pureState_stateQForm_eq_ev)

/-- For complete projective families and a pure bipartite state, the LDT
consistency relation is exactly the QPBT off-diagonal defect.  In
particular, changing between the density and vector formulations incurs no
loss in the error parameter. -/
theorem consRel_iff_consistencyDefect
    {Question Outcome iotaA iotaB : Type*}
    [Fintype Question] [DecidableEq Question]
    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
    [Nonempty (iotaA × iotaB)]
    (psi : PureState (iotaA × iotaB))
    (mu : Distribution Question) (hmu : mu.IsProbability)
    (A : Question → ProjMeas Outcome iotaA)
    (B : Question → ProjMeas Outcome iotaB) (delta : ℝ) :
    ConsRel (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB)) mu
        (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) delta ↔
      consistencyDefect mu
        (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a))
        (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) ≤ delta := by
  let AM : Question → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement Outcome (iotaA × iotaB) :=
    fun x => DistanceCalculus.leftPlacedMeasurement
      (ldtMeasurementToMatrixMeasurement (A x).toMeasurement)
  let BM : Question → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement Outcome (iotaA × iotaB) :=
    fun x => DistanceCalculus.rightPlacedMeasurement
      (ldtMeasurementToMatrixMeasurement (B x).toMeasurement)
  have hAM (x : Question) (a : Outcome) :
      (AM x).effect a = heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1 := rfl
  have hBM (x : Question) (a : Outcome) :
      (BM x).effect a = heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a) := rfl
  have hdefect :
      consistencyDefect mu
          (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
          (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a))
          (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) =
        bipartiteConsError (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB)) mu
          (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) := by
    calc
      consistencyDefect mu
          (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
          (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a))
          (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) =
          1 - avgOver mu (fun x => ∑ a,
            DistanceCalculus.stateQForm (pureStateEuclideanVector psi)
              ((AM x).effect a * (BM x).effect a)) := by
            simpa only [hAM, hBM] using
              DistanceCalculus.consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_overlap
                mu AM BM (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) hmu
                  (pureStateEuclideanVector_norm psi)
      _ = avgOver mu (fun x => 1 - ∑ a,
            DistanceCalculus.stateQForm (pureStateEuclideanVector psi)
              ((AM x).effect a * (BM x).effect a)) := by
            rw [avgOver_sub, avgOver_const_of_isProbability mu hmu]
      _ = bipartiteConsError (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB)) mu
          (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) := by
            unfold bipartiteConsError
            apply avgOver_congr
            intro x
            rw [qBipartiteConsDefect_of_measurements
              (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB))
              (A x).toMeasurement (B x).toMeasurement]
            rw [ev_one_of_isNormalized (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB))
              psi.toQuantumState_isNormalized]
            congr 1
            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
            intro a _
            rw [hAM, hBM]
            rw [DistanceCalculus.placed_product_stateQForm_eq]
            exact pureState_stateQForm_eq_ev psi
              (opTensor ((A x).outcome a) ((B x).outcome a))
  constructor
  · intro h
    rw [hdefect]
    exact h.offDiagonalBound
  · intro h
    refine ⟨?_⟩
    rw [← hdefect]
    exact h

/-! ## Direct-strategy state and point readout -/

private theorem quantumState_ext
    {iota : Type*} [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    {rho sigma : QuantumState iota} (h : rho.density = sigma.density) : rho = sigma := by
  cases rho with
  | mk rho hrho =>
      cases sigma with
      | mk sigma hsigma =>
          simp only at h
          subst sigma
          rfl

/-- The pure state carried by a game strategy, regarded as an LDT pure state. -/
noncomputable def gameStrategyPureState {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) :
    letI : Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
      (strategyQuantumState_isNormalized S).nonempty
    PureState (S.ιA × S.ιB) := by
  letI : Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
    (strategyQuantumState_isNormalized S).nonempty
  exact strategyPureState S

@[simp] theorem gameStrategyPureState_vector {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) :
    letI : Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
      (strategyQuantumState_isNormalized S).nonempty
    (gameStrategyPureState S).vector = S.ψ := by
  letI : Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
    (strategyQuantumState_isNormalized S).nonempty
  rfl

/-- The density state used by `directCoordinateProjStrat` is the density of
the strategy's displayed pure state. -/
theorem strategyQuantumState_eq_gameStrategyPureState
    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) :
    letI : Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
      (strategyQuantumState_isNormalized S).nonempty
    strategyQuantumState S =
      (gameStrategyPureState S : QuantumState (S.ιA × S.ιB)) := by
  letI : Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
    (strategyQuantumState_isNormalized S).nonempty
  apply quantumState_ext
  rfl

/-- The Euclidean vector of the strategy's pure-state presentation is the
original game vector. -/
@[simp] theorem gameStrategyPureState_euclideanVector
    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) :
    letI : Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
      (strategyQuantumState_isNormalized S).nonempty
    pureStateEuclideanVector (gameStrategyPureState S) = S.ψ := by
  letI : Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
    (strategyQuantumState_isNormalized S).nonempty
  apply (EuclideanSpace.equiv (S.ιA × S.ιB) ℂ).injective
  rfl

/-- An LDT consistency relation on the density state associated with a game
strategy gives the identical QPBT defect bound on the strategy vector. -/
theorem strategyConsRel_consistencyDefect_le
    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
    {Question Outcome : Type*}
    [Fintype Question] [DecidableEq Question]
    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
    (mu : Distribution Question) (hmu : mu.IsProbability)
    (A : Question → ProjMeas Outcome S.ιA)
    (B : Question → ProjMeas Outcome S.ιB) (delta : ℝ)
    (h : ConsRel (strategyQuantumState S) mu
      (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) delta) :
    consistencyDefect mu
      (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
      (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a)) S.ψ ≤ delta := by
  letI : Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
    (strategyQuantumState_isNormalized S).nonempty
  let pure : PureState (S.ιA × S.ιB) := strategyPureState S
  have hpure :
      ConsRel (pure : QuantumState (S.ιA × S.ιB)) mu
        (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) delta := by
    simpa [pure, strategyQuantumState] using h
  have hconverted := (consRel_iff_consistencyDefect pure mu hmu A B delta).mp hpure
  have hv : pureStateEuclideanVector pure = S.ψ := by
    exact gameStrategyPureState_euclideanVector S
  rw [hv] at hconverted
  exact hconverted

@[simp] theorem directPointQuestionOf_directPointEquiv
    (D : DirectLdParams) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
    directPointQuestionOf D (directPointEquiv D u) =
      directLdPointQuestionOf D u := by
  unfold directPointQuestionOf ldtPointToDirect
  rw [(directPointEquiv D).symm_apply_apply]

/-- LDT points associated with direct parameters have a canonical zero
witness. -/
instance directLdtPointNonempty (D : DirectLdParams) :
    Nonempty (Point D.toLDTParameters) :=
  ⟨fun _ => ⟨0, D.toLDTParameters.hq⟩⟩

/-- The LDT scalar readout is the direct coordinate readout followed by
the scalar coding equivalence. -/
@[simp] theorem directPointAnswerReadout_eq
    (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k) (answer : DirectLdAnswer D) :
    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    directPointAnswerReadout D r answer =
      directScalarEquiv D (directLdPointValuesOrZero D answer r) := by
  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
  cases answer <;> rfl

/-- At corresponding points and scalar outcomes, the LDT point effect is
the effect of the direct point measurement followed by coordinate projection. -/
theorem directCoordinatePointMeasurement_effect_transport
    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k)
    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (a : DirectScalarQ D) :
    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    (((directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementA
      (directPointEquiv D u)).outcome (directScalarEquiv D a)) =
      ((S.A (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
        (fun answer => directLdPointValuesOrZero D answer r)).effect a := by
  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
  classical
  simp only [directCoordinateProjStrat, directCoordinatePointMeasurement,
    directLdGame,
    ProjMeas.postprocess, SubMeas.postprocess_outcome,
    matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas_outcome,
    directPointQuestionOf_directPointEquiv,
    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
  congr 1
  ext answer
  rw [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_filter]
  simp only [Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
  simpa only [directPointAnswerReadout_eq] using
    (directScalarEquiv D).injective.eq_iff

/-- Bob's point effects satisfy the same direct-to-LDT readout identity. -/
theorem directCoordinatePointMeasurementB_effect_transport
    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k)
    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (a : DirectScalarQ D) :
    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    (((directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementB
      (directPointEquiv D u)).outcome (directScalarEquiv D a)) =
      ((S.B (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
        (fun answer => directLdPointValuesOrZero D answer r)).effect a := by
  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
  classical
  simp only [directCoordinateProjStrat, directCoordinatePointMeasurement,
    directLdGame,
    ProjMeas.postprocess, SubMeas.postprocess_outcome,
    matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas_outcome,
    directPointQuestionOf_directPointEquiv,
    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
  congr 1
  ext answer
  rw [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_filter]
  simp only [Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
  simpa only [directPointAnswerReadout_eq] using
    (directScalarEquiv D).injective.eq_iff

/-- Alice's direct point measurement followed by projection to coordinate
`r`. -/
noncomputable def directPointCoordinateMeasurementA
    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
    (r : Fin D.k) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectScalarQ D) S.ιA :=
  (S.A (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
    (fun answer => directLdPointValuesOrZero D answer r)

/-- Bob's direct point measurement followed by projection to coordinate
`r`. -/
noncomputable def directPointCoordinateMeasurementB
    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
    (r : Fin D.k) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectScalarQ D) S.ιB :=
  (S.B (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
    (fun answer => directLdPointValuesOrZero D answer r)

/-- Evaluate a transported LDT polynomial measurement at a direct point. -/
noncomputable def directPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement
    (D : DirectLdParams) :
    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    {iota : Type*} → [Fintype iota] → [DecidableEq iota] →
      ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) iota →
        (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) →
          MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectScalarQ D) iota := by
  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
  intro iota _ _ G u
  exact (directPolynomialMeasurement D G).postprocess
    (fun g => MvPolynomial.eval u g.1)

/-- Alice's LDT point family obtained from direct coordinate `r`. -/
noncomputable def ldtCoordinatePointMeasurementA
    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) :
    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    IdxProjMeas (Point D.toLDTParameters) (Fq D.toLDTParameters) S.ιA := by
  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
  exact (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementA

/-- Bob's LDT point family obtained from direct coordinate `r`. -/
noncomputable def ldtCoordinatePointMeasurementB
    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) :
    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    IdxProjMeas (Point D.toLDTParameters) (Fq D.toLDTParameters) S.ιB := by
  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
  exact (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementB

/-- The LDT projective evaluation family associated with a global
polynomial projective measurement. -/
noncomputable def ldtPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement
    (D : DirectLdParams) :
    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    {iota : Type*} → [Fintype iota] → [DecidableEq iota] →
      ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) iota →
        IdxProjMeas (Point D.toLDTParameters) (Fq D.toLDTParameters) iota := by
  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
  intro iota _ _ G u
  exact ProjMeas.postprocess G (fun g => g u)

/-- Left placement of Alice's LDT point family. -/
noncomputable def ldtPointAPlaced
    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) :
    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    Point D.toLDTParameters → Fq D.toLDTParameters → Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) := by
  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
  intro u a
  exact heteroKron ((ldtCoordinatePointMeasurementA D S hS r u).outcome a) 1

/-- Right placement of Bob's LDT point family. -/
noncomputable def ldtPointBPlaced
    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) :
    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    Point D.toLDTParameters → Fq D.toLDTParameters → Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) := by
  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
  intro u a
  exact heteroKron 1 ((ldtCoordinatePointMeasurementB D S hS r u).outcome a)

/-- Left placement of an LDT polynomial evaluation family. -/
noncomputable def ldtPolynomialEvaluationLeft
    (D : DirectLdParams) {iotaA iotaB : Type*}
    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB] :
    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) iotaA →
      Point D.toLDTParameters → Fq D.toLDTParameters → Op (iotaA × iotaB) := by
  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
  intro G u a
  exact heteroKron ((ldtPolynomialEvaluationMeasurement D G u).outcome a) 1

/-- Right placement of an LDT polynomial evaluation family. -/
noncomputable def ldtPolynomialEvaluationRight

65:structure PureState (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι] where
import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.ParametersBase
import MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix

/-!
# Quantum states and tensor placement for the low individual degree test

Core quantum-state definitions together with tensor-placement operators.
-/

open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.LDT

/-- A PSD density matrix indexed by `ι`.

There is intentionally no global `Inhabited` instance: the zero matrix is PSD but
not a physical state of unit trace, so an ambient default would silently
trivialize later statements. Use `IsNormalized` to additionally require
`τ(ρ) = 1`.

This remains the ambient state space for the current LDT development: strategy
packages in `LDT/Test/StrategyCore.lean`, the SWAP-symmetry API `PermInvState`,
and the expectation-value lemmas in `LDT/Basic/OperatorExpectations.lean` are all
stated for arbitrary density matrices, not only pure states. -/
structure QuantumState (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] where
  density : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι := 0
  density_psd : 0 ≤ density := by positivity

/-- Unit normalized trace for the concrete matrix carried by a state. -/
def QuantumState.IsNormalized {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (ψ : QuantumState ι) : Prop :=
  MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace ψ.density = 1

/-- A normalized state has a nonempty carrier: if the carrier were empty, the
trace would vanish and `normalizedTrace = 0 / 0 = 0`, contradicting `= 1`. -/
theorem QuantumState.IsNormalized.nonempty {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    {ψ : QuantumState ι} (hψ : ψ.IsNormalized) : Nonempty ι := by
  by_contra h
  rw [not_nonempty_iff] at h
  letI := h
  rw [QuantumState.IsNormalized] at hψ
  have hzero : MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace ψ.density = 0 := by
    simp [MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace]
  exact zero_ne_one (hzero.symm.trans hψ)

/-- The scaled rank-one density matrix attached to a state vector.

Because this development uses the normalized trace `τ(A) = tr(A) / dim`, the
quantum state represented by a unit vector `ψ` is `dim · |ψ⟩⟨ψ|` rather than the
raw projector `|ψ⟩⟨ψ|`. This scaling makes `τ(ρ) = 1` and keeps `ev` aligned
with the paper's bra-ket expectations. -/
noncomputable def pureDensity {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (ψ : ι → ℂ) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι :=
  (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) • Matrix.vecMulVec ψ (star ψ)

/-- Swap the two tensor coordinates of a bipartite state vector. -/
def swapVector {ι : Type*} (ψ : ι × ι → ℂ) : ι × ι → ℂ :=
  fun ij => ψ (ij.2, ij.1)

/-- A pure-state witness as a unit vector in the ambient finite Hilbert space.

The associated density matrix is `pureDensity ψ.vector = dim · |ψ⟩⟨ψ|`, so that
coercing to `QuantumState` preserves the paper's scalar `⟨ψ|X|ψ⟩` formulas
despite our use of the normalized trace. -/
structure PureState (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι] where
  vector : ι → ℂ
  unit : star vector ⬝ᵥ vector = 1

namespace PureState

/-- The coordinate-basis vector has unit self-dot product. -/
private theorem basis_unit {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (i : ι) :
    star (fun j => if j = i then (1 : ℂ) else 0) ⬝ᵥ
        (fun j => if j = i then (1 : ℂ) else 0) = 1 := by
  rw [dotProduct]
  simp

/-- The coordinate-basis pure state at a distinguished basis vector. -/
noncomputable def basis {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (i : ι) : PureState ι where
  vector := fun j => if j = i then 1 else 0
  unit := basis_unit i

/-- The density matrix represented by a pure-state witness. -/
noncomputable def density {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (ψ : PureState ι) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι :=
  pureDensity ψ.vector

theorem density_psd {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (ψ : PureState ι) :
    0 ≤ ψ.density := by
  refine Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr ?_
  exact (Matrix.posSemidef_vecMulVec_self_star ψ.vector).smul
    (by positivity : 0 ≤ (Fintype.card ι : ℂ))

noncomputable def toQuantumState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (ψ : PureState ι) : QuantumState ι where
  density := ψ.density
  density_psd := ψ.density_psd

noncomputable instance {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι] :
    Coe (PureState ι) (QuantumState ι) where
  coe := toQuantumState

@[simp] theorem coe_density {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (ψ : PureState ι) :
    (ψ : QuantumState ι).density = ψ.density := rfl

theorem normalizedTrace_density {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (ψ : PureState ι) :
    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace ψ.density = 1 := by
  have hcard : (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Fintype.card_ne_zero
  unfold density pureDensity MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace
  rw [Matrix.trace_smul, Matrix.trace_vecMulVec, dotProduct_comm, ψ.unit]
  change ((Fintype.card ι : ℂ) * 1) / (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) = 1
  rw [mul_one, div_self hcard]

theorem toQuantumState_isNormalized {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (ψ : PureState ι) :
    (ψ : QuantumState ι).IsNormalized := by
  simpa [QuantumState.IsNormalized] using ψ.normalizedTrace_density

theorem normalizedTrace_density_mul {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (ψ : PureState ι) (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace ((ψ : QuantumState ι).density * X) =
      star ψ.vector ⬝ᵥ (X *ᵥ ψ.vector) := by
  have hcard : (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Fintype.card_ne_zero
  calc
    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace ((ψ : QuantumState ι).density * X)

    25	/-- `\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}` from the paper's definition of low-individual-degree

    27	noncomputable abbrev polyFunc (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] (d : ℕ) :
    28	    Submodule K (MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) :=
    29	  MvPolynomial.restrictDegree (Fin m) K d

    31	/-- If `p ∈ polyFunc m K d`, then `p.degreeOf i ≤ d` for every variable `i`. -/
    32	theorem degreeOf_le_of_mem_polyFunc {m d : ℕ} {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K]
    33	    {p : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K} (hp : p ∈ polyFunc m K d) (i : Fin m) :
    34	    p.degreeOf i ≤ d :=
    35	  MvPolynomial.degreeOf_le_iff.mpr fun s hs =>
    36	    (MvPolynomial.mem_restrictDegree (σ := Fin m) (R := K) p d).mp hp s hs i

    44	  intro p hp
    45	  rw [MvPolynomial.mem_restrictDegree] at hp ⊢
    46	  intro s hs i
    47	  exact (hp s hs i).trans (Nat.le_succ d)

    49	/-- The uniform agreement probability of two polynomials on `K^m`, written as a
    50	finite cardinality ratio over `K^m`. -/
    51	noncomputable def polynomialAgreementProbability (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] [Fintype K]
    52	    [DecidableEq K] (g h : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : ℚ≥0 :=
    53	  #{x ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m → K)) |
    54	      MvPolynomial.eval x g = MvPolynomial.eval x h} /
    55	    (Fintype.card K ^ m : ℚ≥0)

    59	theorem totalDegree_le_mul_of_degreeOf_le {m d : ℕ} {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K]

    61	    p.totalDegree ≤ m * d := by
    62	  rw [MvPolynomial.totalDegree]
    63	  refine Finset.sup_le ?_
    64	  intro s hs
    65	  calc
    66	    s.sum (fun _ e => e) = ∑ i : Fin m, s i := by

    68	      intro i

    70	    _ ≤ ∑ _i : Fin m, d := by

% The two lemmas below are not statements of the source; they record which
% consequences of Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness} are available for the directly
% indexed presentation of the classical game discussed in the preceding remark.
\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for the consistency conclusions in directly indexed coordinates]
	\label{lem:direct-ld-consistency-coordinates}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.directPointPolynomial_consistencyDefect_le}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.directPolynomialPoint_consistencyDefect_le}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.directPolynomialPolynomial_consistencyDefect_le}
	\leanok
	\uses{def:consistency, def:ld-game, lem:ld-soundness}
	This is not a named statement of \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. It records the
	form in which the approximate-agreement conclusions of
	Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness} are available for the directly indexed
	presentation of the classical low individual degree game, in which the
	sampled coordinate is carried by the question itself rather than by a
	residue class of $\F_q$; that presentation, and the divisibility
	obstruction motivating it, are the subject of
	Remark~\ref{rem:qld-4-7-divisibility}.

	Let $\delta \ge 0$, let $(\psi, A, B)$ be a projective strategy for the
	directly indexed game, and let $G^{\mathrm A}$ and $G^{\mathrm B}$ be
	measurements on $\hilb_{\mathrm A}$ and $\hilb_{\mathrm B}$ whose
	outcomes are single polynomials of individual degree at most $d$ in $m$
	variables. Fix one coordinate $r \in \{1, \dots, k\}$ of the answer
	tuple and write $A^{\mathsf{Point},\,u,\,r}$ and
	$B^{\mathsf{Point},\,u,\,r}$ for the point measurements of the two
	players read out at that coordinate. Then:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item if, over a uniformly random point $u \in \F_q^m$,
		      $A^{\mathsf{Point},\,u,\,r} \ot I_{\mathrm B}$ and
		      $I_{\mathrm A} \ot G^{\mathrm B}_{[g(u) = a]}$ satisfy the
		      relation $\simeq_{\delta}$ of
		      Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness} on the density operator of
		      $\psi$, then the off-diagonal defect of
		      Definition~\ref{def:consistency} of that same pair, written
		      in the directly indexed question and answer types and
		      evaluated on the vector $\psi$, is at most $\delta$;
		\item the same statement with the two players exchanged, for
		      $G^{\mathrm A}_{[g(u) = a]} \ot I_{\mathrm B}$ and
		      $I_{\mathrm A} \ot B^{\mathsf{Point},\,u,\,r}$;
		\item if $G^{\mathrm A} \ot I_{\mathrm B}$ and
		      $I_{\mathrm A} \ot G^{\mathrm B}$ satisfy that relation,
		      taken over the one-element question set, then the
		      off-diagonal defect of the corresponding pair in the
		      directly indexed answer type is at most $\delta$.
	\end{enumerate}
	The first two statements fix the coordinate $r$ and assume the relation
	only for that coordinate, and all three take single polynomials rather
	than tuples as the outcomes of $G^{\mathrm A}$ and $G^{\mathrm B}$.
	None of them constructs the joint measurement of a whole $k$-tuple of
	polynomials asserted by Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness}; that
	construction is not established here.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for the compression of a correlated residue register]
	\label{lem:direct-ld-residue-compression}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldStrategyToDirect_pointPolynomial_compression}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldStrategyToDirect_polynomialPoint_compression}
	\leanok
	\uses{def:consistency, def:ld-game, def:ld-question-distribution}
	This is not a named statement of \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. It records the
	two compression identities that are available between the classical low
	individual degree game and its directly indexed presentation, and the
	one that is not.

	Let $(\psi, A, B)$ be a strategy for the classical game with parameters
	$(q,m,d,k)$, and extend it to the directly indexed game by adjoining to
	each player a register of dimension $q/m$, the common size of the
	classes of the index function $\chi$ of
	Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution}; the two copies of that
	register are perfectly correlated in the extended state. For a
	measurement $G$ on the extended carrier
	$\hilb \ot \C^{q/m}$ whose outcomes are $k$-tuples of polynomials,
	write $\bar G$ for its compression: the normalized average of its
	diagonal blocks over the residue register. Then, over a uniformly
	random point $u \in \F_q^m$, the off-diagonal defect of
	Definition~\ref{def:consistency} between the point measurement of the
	first player and the evaluation of $G$ at $u$, taken on the extended
	strategy, equals the off-diagonal defect between the point measurement
	of the first player and the evaluation of $\bar G$ at $u$, taken on
	$(\psi, A, B)$; and symmetrically with the two players exchanged.

	No such identity is recorded when both measurements are polynomial
	measurements on the extended carrier. The extended state pairs equal
	residues, whereas compressing the two measurements separately averages
	independently over two residues, and neither quantity bounds the other
	in general; this open point is analyzed in
	\cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{remark}[Constant regimes in the quotation of the classical soundness
	theorem]
	\label{rem:qld-4-7-constants}
	Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness} states its error function with universal
	constants $a \ge 1$ and $0 < b \le 1$, while the source proof of
	Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7} in \cite{Ji2020MIPStar} quotes it, and the
	statement of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7} is phrased, with $a > 1$ and
	$0 < b < 1$. The discrepancy is harmless: enlarging $a$ and shrinking
	$b$ only weakens a bound of this form, so any admissible pair for
	Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness} yields an admissible pair for
	Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}. The closing computation of the source proof
	also mixes the terms $d/q$ and $md/q$ in the bound for $\delta_S$; the

   177	theorem strategyConsRel_consistencyDefect_le
   178	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   179	    {Question Outcome : Type*}
   180	    [Fintype Question] [DecidableEq Question]
   181	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
   182	    (mu : Distribution Question) (hmu : mu.IsProbability)
   183	    (A : Question → ProjMeas Outcome S.ιA)
   184	    (B : Question → ProjMeas Outcome S.ιB) (delta : ℝ)
   185	    (h : ConsRel (strategyQuantumState S) mu
   186	      (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) delta) :
   187	    consistencyDefect mu
   188	      (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
   189	      (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a)) S.ψ ≤ delta := by
   190	  letI : Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
   191	    (strategyQuantumState_isNormalized S).nonempty
   192	  let pure : PureState (S.ιA × S.ιB) := strategyPureState S
   193	  have hpure :
   194	      ConsRel (pure : QuantumState (S.ιA × S.ιB)) mu
   195	        (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) delta := by
   196	    simpa [pure, strategyQuantumState] using h
   197	  have hconverted := (consRel_iff_consistencyDefect pure mu hmu A B delta).mp hpure
   198	  have hv : pureStateEuclideanVector pure = S.ψ := by
   199	    exact gameStrategyPureState_euclideanVector S
   200	  rw [hv] at hconverted
   201	  exact hconverted

     4	# Low-degree consistency transport
     5	
     6	This module identifies the low individual degree polynomial outcomes with the
     7	bounded polynomial representatives used by the directly indexed QPBT game.  It
     8	also transports complete measurements and their evaluation postprocessings
     9	without changing either coordinate order or consistency error.
    10

    14	- `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:180-202`
    15	- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`
    16	-/

    30	private theorem directPolynomialRename_degreeOf_le
    31	    (D : DirectLdParams) (p : MvPolynomial (Fin D.m) (DirectScalarQ D))
    32	    (hp : ∀ i, MvPolynomial.degreeOf i p ≤ D.d) (i : Fin D.m) :
    33	    MvPolynomial.degreeOf i (MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev p) ≤ D.d := by
    34	  rw [← Fin.rev_rev i,
    35	    MvPolynomial.degreeOf_rename_of_injective Fin.rev_injective]
    36	  exact hp (Fin.rev i)

    38	private theorem ldtPolynomial_ext
    39	    {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    40	    {g h : MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial params} (hpoly : g.poly = h.poly) : g = h := by
    41	  cases g with
    42	  | mk gp hg =>
    43	      cases h with
    44	      | mk hp hh =>
    45	          simp only at hpoly
    46	          subst hp
    47	          rfl

    49	/-- Bounded QPBT polynomial representatives are equivalent to LDT
    50	polynomial outcomes.  The variable renaming is the same coordinate reversal
    51	as `directPointEquiv`, so evaluation retains the direct coordinate order. -/
    52	noncomputable def directPolyEquivPolynomial (D : DirectLdParams) :
    53	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    54	    PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d ≃
    55	      MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters := by
    56	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    57	  refine
    58	    { toFun := fun g =>
    59	        { poly := MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev g.1
    60	          lowIndividualDegree := directPolynomialRename_degreeOf_le D g.1
    61	            (degreeOf_le_of_mem_polyFunc g.2) }
    62	      invFun := fun g =>
    63	        ⟨MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev g.poly, ?_⟩
    64	      left_inv := ?_
    65	      right_inv := ?_ }
    66	  · rw [MvPolynomial.mem_restrictDegree]
    67	    intro s hs i
    68	    exact (MvPolynomial.degreeOf_le_iff.mp
    69	      (directPolynomialRename_degreeOf_le D g.poly g.lowIndividualDegree i)) s hs
    70	  · intro g
    71	    apply Subtype.ext
    72	    change MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev
    73	      (MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev g.1) = g.1
    74	    rw [MvPolynomial.rename_rename]
    75	    rw [show Fin.rev ∘ Fin.rev = id by funext i; simp]
    76	    exact MvPolynomial.rename_id_apply g.1
    77	  · intro g
    78	    cases g with
    79	    | mk p hp =>
    80	        have hpoly : MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev
    81	            (MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev p) = p := by
    82	          rw [MvPolynomial.rename_rename]
    83	          rw [show Fin.rev ∘ Fin.rev = id by funext i; simp]
    84	          exact MvPolynomial.rename_id_apply p
    85	        apply ldtPolynomial_ext
    86	        exact hpoly

    88	@[simp] theorem directPolyEquivPolynomial_poly
    89	    (D : DirectLdParams) (g : PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d) :
    90	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    91	    (directPolyEquivPolynomial D g).poly = MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev g.1 := by
    92	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    93	  rfl

    95	/-- The polynomial equivalence commutes with evaluation after the direct point
    96	and scalar codings. -/
    97	@[simp] theorem directPolyEquivPolynomial_apply
    98	    (D : DirectLdParams) (g : PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d)
    99	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
   100	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   101	    directPolyEquivPolynomial D g (directPointEquiv D u) =
   102	      directScalarEquiv D (MvPolynomial.eval u g.1) := by
   103	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   104	  unfold MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial.toFun evalPolynomialModel
   105	  rw [directPolyEquivPolynomial_poly]
   106	  unfold decodePoint
   107	  rw [MvPolynomial.eval_rename]
   108	  congr 1
   109	  apply congrArg (fun v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D =>
   110	    MvPolynomial.eval v g.1)
   111	  funext i
   112	  simp only [Function.comp_apply, directPointEquiv_apply, Fin.rev_rev]
   113	  change (directScalarEquiv D).symm (directScalarEquiv D (u i)) = u i
   114	  exact (directScalarEquiv D).symm_apply_apply (u i)

   122	    (M : MIPStarRE.LDT.Measurement alpha iota) :
   123	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota :=

   125	    rw [M.sum_eq_total, M.total_eq_one])

   136	    (D : DirectLdParams) :
   137	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel

   140	        PolyMeas D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d iota := by

   214	            (directScalarEquiv D a) := by

   239	/-! ## Correlated-ancilla compression -/
   240	
   241	/-!
   242	The diagonal-block conditional expectation preserves either mixed defect
   243	exactly because the point measurement on the opposite carrier is constant on
   244	the residue register.  It does not yield a global/global compression theorem:
   245	the lifted state pairs equal residues, whereas separately compressing both
   246	polynomial measurements produces an independent double average over residues.
   247	Neither quantity bounds the other in general.  This open obstruction is
   248	recorded in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
   249	-/
   250	
   251	/-- The normalized diagonal-block average of an operator on a carrier with a
   252	finite ancillary register.  This is the local conditional expectation used to
   253	discard one half of the correlated seed-residue ancilla. -/
   254	noncomputable def averageDiagonalBlock
   255	    {iota block : Type*} [Fintype iota] [Fintype block]
   256	    (A : Op (iota × block)) : Op iota := by
   257	  classical
   258	  exact (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   259	    ∑ r, A.submatrix (fun i => (i, r)) (fun i => (i, r))
   260	
   261	/-- Compress a POVM through the normalized diagonal-block average.  The
   262	nonemptiness assumption says precisely that the normalized finite average is
   263	defined over at least one ancillary basis element. -/
   264	noncomputable def correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement
   265	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
   266	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   267	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block] [Nonempty block]
   268	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha (iota × block)) :
   269	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota :=
   270	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
   271	    (fun a => averageDiagonalBlock (M.effect a))
   272	    (fun a => by
   273	      unfold averageDiagonalBlock
   274	      apply smul_nonneg
   275	      · positivity
   276	      · exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun r _ =>
   277	          Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr
   278	            ((Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp (M.pos a)).submatrix
   279	              (fun i => (i, r))))
   280	    (by
   281	      classical
   282	      ext i j
   283	      simp only [averageDiagonalBlock, Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.smul_apply,
   284	        Matrix.submatrix_apply]
   285	      calc
   286	        ∑ a, (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   287	              ∑ r, M.effect a (i, r) (j, r) =
   288	            (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   289	              ∑ a, ∑ r, M.effect a (i, r) (j, r) := by
   290	                rw [Finset.smul_sum]
   291	        _ = (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   292	              ∑ r, ∑ a, M.effect a (i, r) (j, r) := by
   293	                rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   294	        _ = (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   295	              ∑ r, (1 : Op (iota × block)) (i, r) (j, r) := by
   296	                congr 1
   297	                apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   298	                intro r _
   299	                simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using
   300	                  congrFun (congrFun M.sum_eq_one (i, r)) (j, r)
   301	        _ = (1 : Op iota) i j := by
   302	              simp [Matrix.one_apply, Fintype.card_ne_zero])
   303	
   304	@[simp] theorem correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement_effect
   305	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
   306	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   307	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block] [Nonempty block]
   308	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha (iota × block)) (a : alpha) :
   309	    (correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement M).effect a =
   310	      averageDiagonalBlock (M.effect a) :=
   311	  rfl

   313	private theorem averageDiagonalBlock_finset_sum
   314	    {alpha iota block : Type*} [Fintype iota] [Fintype block]
   315	    (s : Finset alpha) (A : alpha → Op (iota × block)) :
   316	    averageDiagonalBlock (∑ a ∈ s, A a) =
   317	      ∑ a ∈ s, averageDiagonalBlock (A a) := by
   318	  classical
   319	  ext i j
   320	  simp only [averageDiagonalBlock, Matrix.smul_apply, Matrix.sum_apply,
   321	    Matrix.submatrix_apply]
   322	  simp_rw [Finset.smul_sum]
   323	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   324	
   325	/-- Normalized diagonal-block compression commutes with deterministic outcome
   326	postprocessing. -/
   327	theorem correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement_postprocess
   328	    {alpha beta iota block : Type*}
   329	    [Fintype alpha] [DecidableEq alpha]
   330	    [Fintype beta] [DecidableEq beta]
   331	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   332	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block] [Nonempty block]
   333	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha (iota × block))
   334	    (f : alpha → beta) :
   335	    correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement (M.postprocess f) =
   336	      (correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement M).postprocess f := by
   337	  classical
   338	  apply MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ext
   339	  intro b
   340	  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect,
   341	    correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement_effect,
   342	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
   343	  exact averageDiagonalBlock_finset_sum
   344	    (Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b)) M.effect
   345	
   346	/-- Specialize ancillary compression to the nonempty residue fiber supplied by
   347	the divisibility data of `LdParams`. -/
   348	noncomputable def seedFiberCompressMeasurement
   349	    (L : LdParams) {alpha iota : Type*}
   350	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   351	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha
   352	      (iota × Fin (L.q / L.m))) :
   353	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota := by
   354	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   355	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   356	  exact correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement M

   358	@[simp] theorem seedFiberCompressMeasurement_effect
   359	    (L : LdParams) {alpha iota : Type*}
   360	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   361	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha
   362	      (iota × Fin (L.q / L.m))) (a : alpha) :
   363	    (seedFiberCompressMeasurement L M).effect a =
   364	      averageDiagonalBlock (M.effect a) :=
   365	  rfl
   366	
   367	/-- Seed-fiber compression commutes with deterministic outcome
   368	postprocessing. -/
   369	theorem seedFiberCompressMeasurement_postprocess
   370	    (L : LdParams) {alpha beta iota : Type*}
   371	    [Fintype alpha] [DecidableEq alpha]
   372	    [Fintype beta] [DecidableEq beta]
   373	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   374	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha
   375	      (iota × Fin (L.q / L.m))) (f : alpha → beta) :
   376	    seedFiberCompressMeasurement L (M.postprocess f) =
   377	      (seedFiberCompressMeasurement L M).postprocess f := by
   378	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   379	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   380	  exact correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement_postprocess M f

   382	/-- Compress a direct polynomial-tuple POVM from the correlated seed-residue
   383	carrier to the corresponding seed-indexed polynomial POVM. -/
   384	noncomputable def seedFiberCompressPolyMeasTuple
   385	    (L : LdParams) {iota : Type*} [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   386	    (G : DirectPolyMeasTuple L.toDirectLdParams
   387	      (iota × Fin (L.q / L.m))) : PolyMeasTuple L iota := by
   388	  exact seedFiberCompressMeasurement L G
   389	
   390	@[simp] theorem seedFiberCompressPolyMeasTuple_effect
   391	    (L : LdParams) {iota : Type*} [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   392	    (G : DirectPolyMeasTuple L.toDirectLdParams
   393	      (iota × Fin (L.q / L.m))) (g : PolyTuple L) :
   394	    (seedFiberCompressPolyMeasTuple L G).effect g =
   395	      averageDiagonalBlock (G.effect g) :=
   396	  rfl
   397	
   398	/-- Polynomial evaluation commutes exactly with compression of the correlated
   399	seed-residue carrier. -/
   400	theorem seedFiberCompressPolyMeasTuple_evaluation
   401	    (L : LdParams) {iota : Type*} [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   402	    (G : DirectPolyMeasTuple L.toDirectLdParams
   403	      (iota × Fin (L.q / L.m))) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) :
   404	    (seedFiberCompressPolyMeasTuple L G).postprocess (evalPolyTupleAt u) =
   405	      seedFiberCompressMeasurement L
   406	        (G.postprocess (evalDirectPolyTupleAt u)) := by
   407	  exact (seedFiberCompressMeasurement_postprocess L G
   408	    (evalDirectPolyTupleAt u)).symm
   409	
   410	/-- Block-diagonal assembly commutes with deterministic outcome
   411	postprocessing. -/
   412	theorem blockDiagonalMeasurement_postprocess
   413	    {alpha beta iota block : Type*}
   414	    [Fintype alpha] [DecidableEq alpha]
   415	    [Fintype beta] [DecidableEq beta]
   416	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   417	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block]
   418	    (M : block → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
   419	    (f : alpha → beta) :
   420	    (blockDiagonalMeasurement M).postprocess f =
   421	      blockDiagonalMeasurement (fun r => (M r).postprocess f) := by
   422	  classical
   423	  apply MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ext
   424	  intro b
   425	  ext ⟨i, r⟩ ⟨j, s⟩
   426	  simp only [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect,
   427	    blockDiagonalMeasurement_effect, Matrix.sum_apply,
   428	    Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply]
   429	  by_cases hrs : r = s
   430	  · subst s
   431	    simp only [if_pos]
   432	  · simp [hrs]

   434	private theorem matrixMeasurementTransport_eq_postprocess
   435	    {alpha beta iota : Type*}
   436	    [Fintype alpha] [DecidableEq alpha]
   437	    [Fintype beta] [DecidableEq beta]
   438	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   439	    (e : alpha ≃ beta) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota) :
   440	    matrixMeasurementTransport e M = M.postprocess e := by
   441	  classical
   442	  apply MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ext
   443	  intro b
   444	  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
   445	  rw [Finset.sum_eq_single (e.symm b)]
   446	  · simp
   447	  · intro a haMem ha
   448	    have hea : e a = b := (Finset.mem_filter.mp haMem).2
   449	    exact (ha (e.injective (hea.trans (e.apply_symm_apply b).symm))).elim
   450	  · simp

   452	/-- Relabeling along an outcome equivalence commutes with subsequent
   453	postprocessing. -/
   454	theorem matrixMeasurementTransport_postprocess
   455	    {alpha beta gamma iota : Type*}
   456	    [Fintype alpha] [DecidableEq alpha]
   457	    [Fintype beta] [DecidableEq beta]
   458	    [Fintype gamma] [DecidableEq gamma]
   459	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   460	    (e : alpha ≃ beta) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
   461	    (f : beta → gamma) :
   462	    (matrixMeasurementTransport e M).postprocess f =
   463	      M.postprocess (fun a => f (e a)) := by
   464	  rw [matrixMeasurementTransport_eq_postprocess,

   101	private theorem correlatedState_compress_left
   102	    {iotaA iotaB block : Type*}
   103	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   104	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   105	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block] [Nonempty block]
   106	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB))
   107	    (phi : EuclideanSpace ℂ ((iotaA × block) × (iotaB × block)))
   108	    (hphi : ∀ i j r s, phi ((i, r), (j, s)) =
   109	      if r = s then
   110	        psi (i, j) * (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card block : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹
   111	      else 0)
   112	    (A : Op (iotaA × block)) (B : Op iotaB) :
   113	    DistanceCalculus.stateQForm phi
   114	        (heteroKron A (Matrix.blockDiagonal fun _ => B)) =
   115	      DistanceCalculus.stateQForm psi
   116	        (heteroKron (averageDiagonalBlock A) B) := by
   117	  classical
   118	  unfold DistanceCalculus.stateQForm
   119	  apply congrArg Complex.re
   120	  unfold applyOperatorToState heteroKron Matrix.kronecker averageDiagonalBlock
   121	  simp_rw [EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct]
   122	  simp only [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_apply, dotProduct,
   123	    Matrix.mulVec]
   124	  simp_rw [← Finset.univ_product_univ, Finset.sum_product]
   125	  suffices h :
   126	      (∑ i : iotaA, ∑ r : block, ∑ j : iotaB,
   127	        ∑ i' : iotaA, ∑ j' : iotaB,
   128	          (starRingEnd ℂ)
   129	              (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card block : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
   130	            (starRingEnd ℂ) (psi (i, j)) *
   131	              (B j j' * (A (i, r) (i', r) *
   132	                ((Real.sqrt (Fintype.card block : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
   133	                  psi (i', j'))))) =
   134	        ∑ i : iotaA, ∑ j : iotaB, ∑ i' : iotaA,
   135	          ∑ j' : iotaB, ∑ r : block,
   136	            (starRingEnd ℂ) (psi (i, j)) *
   137	              (psi (i', j') * (B j j' *
   138	                ((Fintype.card block : ℂ)⁻¹ * A (i, r) (i', r)))) by

   169	      if r = s then

   180	  unfold applyOperatorToState heteroKron Matrix.kronecker averageDiagonalBlock

+        (fun x b => A (questionEquiv x) (outcomeEquiv b))
+        (fun x b => B (questionEquiv x) (outcomeEquiv b)) psi =
+      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Y) A B psi := by
+  calc
+    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
+        (fun x b => A (questionEquiv x) (outcomeEquiv b))
+        (fun x b => B (questionEquiv x) (outcomeEquiv b)) psi =
+      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
+        (fun x a => A (questionEquiv x) a)
+        (fun x a => B (questionEquiv x) a) psi :=
+      consistencyDefect_outcome_equiv (uniformDistribution X)
+        outcomeEquiv _ _ psi
+    _ = consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Y) A B psi :=
+      consistencyDefect_uniform_question_equiv questionEquiv A B psi
+
+/-- Pointwise equality of both operator families gives equality of their
+consistency defects. -/
+theorem consistencyDefect_congr
+    {X Outcome iota : Type*}
+    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X]
+    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
+    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
+    (mu : Distribution X) (A A' B B' : X → Outcome → Op iota)
+    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota)
+    (hA : ∀ x a, A x a = A' x a) (hB : ∀ x a, B x a = B' x a) :
+    consistencyDefect mu A B psi = consistencyDefect mu A' B' psi := by
+  unfold consistencyDefect
+  apply avgOver_congr
+  intro x
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro a _
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro b _
+  by_cases hab : a = b
+  · simp [hab]
+  · simp only [hab, if_false]
+    rw [hA x a, hB x b]
